title: [Bug] OpenAI top_logprobs: entries silently collapse when top-k candidates decode to identical text (dict keyed by decoded string)
body:
### Checklist
- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution (#30188 / PR #30187 fix streaming misalignment and mixed-batch crashes; they do not touch this path).
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version (reproduced on v0.5.15.post1; the code is unchanged on current `main` @ 15d73f1e038e).
- [x] This report includes environment information and a minimal reproducible demo.

### Describe the bug

`to_openai_style_logprobs` stores each position's top-k candidates as a dict keyed by the **decoded token text**:

```python
# python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/openai/utils.py (append_top_logprobs)
ret_logprobs.top_logprobs.append(
    {token[2]: token[0] for token in tokens}
)
```

When two distinct token ids in the top-k decode to the same string — routine with byte-fallback tokenizers, where several byte-fragment tokens all decode to U+FFFD `�` — the dict comprehension silently merges them. Two effects follow directly from the text-keyed dict collapse:

1. **Fewer entries than requested**: `top_logprobs=5` can return 4 or fewer entries for affected positions.
2. **Wrong logprob survives**: the comprehension keeps the *last* duplicate, so the surviving entry can carry a lower-ranked candidate's logprob instead of the higher-ranked one.

A related representation issue (adjacent, not caused by the collapse itself): the OpenAI layer reconstructs `bytes` by re-encoding the decoded text (`top_token.encode("utf-8")` in `serving_chat._process_logprobs_tokens`), so the original token bytes are unavailable for byte-fallback tokens — they surface as the UTF-8 of U+FFFD (`[239,191,189]`) even when no collision occurs.

### Minimal reproduction (CPU-only, no model)

```python
from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.utils import to_openai_style_logprobs

out = to_openai_style_logprobs(
    output_token_logprobs=[(-0.1, 1, "A")],
    output_top_logprobs=[[(-0.1, 1, "A"), (-0.5, 77, "�"), (-2.5, 88, "�")]],
)
print(len(out.top_logprobs[0]))       # 2 — expected 3
print(out.top_logprobs[0]["�"])      # -2.5 — the higher-ranked candidate was -0.5
```

### End-to-end observation

`/v1/chat/completions` with `logprobs=true, top_logprobs=5` against DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8 (TP4, 4×H200, both with and without EAGLE speculative decoding) returns positions whose `top_logprobs` length < 5; affected positions show `�`-decoded candidates.

### Suggested fix direction

Minimal correctness fix: preserve all candidates without keying solely by decoded text, while maintaining their order and token identity. A complete OpenAI-compatible fix may also require carrying original token bytes through the internal logprob representation rather than reconstructing them from decoded text. Happy to submit a focused PR for the minimal fix with a CPU regression test (the snippet above) if that direction sounds right.

### Environment
- SGLang v0.5.15.post1 (official `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.15.post1` image); code path unchanged on current `main` (`15d73f1e038e`)
- 4×NVIDIA H200, CUDA 13.0 container stack
- Reproduction of the root cause itself is CPU-only

title: [Bug] update_weights_from_disk crashes for FusedMoE DeepseekV3.2 with 'narrow exceeds dim_size' (initial load OK)
body:
## Summary

After a successful initial `Engine.__init__` load of a DeepseekV32 model on NPU, the **second** load of the same checkpoint via `update_weights_from_disk` crashes the scheduler subprocess with:

```
RuntimeError: start (0) + length (4096) exceeds dimension size (1408).
```

The error path is in `srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py:482` `_load_w13`, called for the `mlp.experts.N.gate_proj.weight` tensors. First-pass load works because it takes a different code path; the second-pass reload hits a `narrow(0, intermediate_size_per_partition * 2)` against the on-disk tensor whose first dim is `intermediate_size_per_partition`.

This blocks RL post-training flows that use `/update_weights_from_disk` to push trained actor weights back to the rollout engine each step (e.g. miles, the framework this was found in).

## Reproduction

Image: `lmsysorg/sglang:main-cann8.5.0-a3` (sglang `0.5.12.post2.dev434+gb13d3d18c`, sgl-kernel-npu `2026.5.1`, transformers `5.8.1`).

Random-init 1-layer DeepseekV32 HF checkpoint built with:

```
hidden_size=4096
num_attention_heads=64
num_hidden_layers=1
first_k_dense_replace=0    # MoE on layer 0
n_routed_experts=4
n_shared_experts=1
moe_intermediate_size=1408
num_experts_per_tok=2
q_lora_rank=1024
kv_lora_rank=512
qk_nope_head_dim=64
qk_rope_head_dim=64
v_head_dim=512
index_topk=8
```

Safetensors saved with `mlp.experts.{0..3}.{gate_proj,up_proj,down_proj}.weight` separate (not pre-fused as `gate_up_proj`).

Driver:

```python
import sglang as sgl
llm = sgl.Engine(
    model_path="/path/to/fab_ckpt",
    dtype="bfloat16", device="npu",
    mem_fraction_static=0.10, tp_size=1, disable_cuda_graph=True,
    enable_return_routed_experts=True,
)
# Initial load: succeeds
llm.generate(["Hi"], sampling_params={"temperature":0.0,"max_new_tokens":4})

# Trigger: reload same ckpt
llm.update_weights_from_disk(model_path="/path/to/fab_ckpt")  # CRASH
```

Full traceback in the scheduler subprocess:

```
File ".../sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 1638, in process_input_requests
    output = self._request_dispatcher(recv_req)
File ".../sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/weight_updater.py", line 62, in update_weights_from_disk
    success, message = self.tp_worker.update_weights_from_disk(recv_req)
File ".../sglang/srt/managers/tp_worker.py", line 97, in update_weights_from_disk
    success, message = self.model_runner.update_weights_from_disk(recv_req)
File ".../sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py", line 1634, in update_weights_from_disk
    self.model = model_load_weights(self.model, iter)
File ".../sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py", line 1616, in model_load_weights
    loader.load_weights_and_postprocess(model, iter, target_device)
File ".../sglang/srt/model_loader/loader.py", line 735, in load_weights_and_postprocess
    model.load_weights(weights)
File ".../sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py", line 2645, in load_weights
    self.do_load_weights(weights, is_nextn)
File ".../sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/deepseek_weight_loader.py", line 373, in do_load_weights
    future.result()
File ".../sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py", line 662, in weight_loader
    self._weight_loader_physical(...)
File ".../sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py", line 692, in _weight_loader_physical
    self._weight_loader_impl(...)
File ".../sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py", line 950, in _weight_loader_impl
    self._load_model_weight_or_group_weight_scale(...)
File ".../sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py", line 398, in _load_model_weight_or_group_weight_scale
    self._load_w13(...)
File ".../sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py", line 482, in _load_w13
    loaded_weight = loaded_weight.narrow(0, ?, ?)
RuntimeError: start (0) + length (4096) exceeds dimension size (1408).
```

After the crash the scheduler dies (SIGQUIT), so even with try/except around the user-facing call, the engine is gone.

## What I think is happening

In `fused_moe_triton/layer.py:_load_w13`, the reload path computes the source slice with the expectation that the on-disk weight is pre-fused (gate+up packed along dim 0 = `2 * intermediate_size`). When the on-disk weight is separate (`gate_proj.weight` shape `[intermediate_size, hidden_size]`), the narrow tries to read `2 * intermediate_size_per_partition` from a tensor whose dim 0 is `intermediate_size`, hence `length (4096) > dim_size (1408)` -- here `4096 = 2 * 2048` (sglang's internal `intermediate_size_per_partition` likely rounded up or counted both halves) and `1408 = moe_intermediate_size`.

In the initial `Engine.__init__` load, `stacked_params_mapping` in `deepseek_common/deepseek_weight_loader.py` (lines 122-125):
```
("gate_up_proj", "gate_proj", 0),
("gate_up_proj", "up_proj", 1),
```
correctly handles separate names, so the first load works. The reload path doesn't appear to honor the same mapping.

## Workarounds

- Pre-fuse `gate_proj` + `up_proj` into a single `gate_up_proj` tensor of shape `[2 * intermediate_size, hidden_size]` when saving the HF checkpoint, then `update_weights_from_disk` succeeds (cumbersome for downstream trainers).
- Use `update_weights_from_tensor` (in-memory) instead, which bypasses the on-disk reload path. (Requires Engine to be co-located with the trainer process or HCCL group setup.)
- Avoid MoE in the layer that gets reloaded.

## Related

- #22784 (gpt-oss-120b EP=8 crashes with tensor size mismatch in weight_loader_fused) -- similar shape-mismatch family but with EP setup as trigger, not specific to reload.
- #20516 (KTransformers-MoE narrow regressions).

## Environment

- platform: Ascend A3 (910C / dav-c220), CANN 8.5.0
- image: `lmsysorg/sglang:main-cann8.5.0-a3` (built 2026-05-25)
- sglang: `0.5.12.post2.dev434+gb13d3d18c`
- sgl-kernel-npu: `2026.5.1`
- torch: `2.8.0+cpu`, torch_npu: `2.8.0.post2`
- transformers: `5.8.1`
- attention_backend: `ascend`
- tp_size=1, ep_size=1

## Question for maintainers

Is the reload path in `_load_w13` expected to honor `stacked_params_mapping` like the initial load? If yes this looks like a regression; if no, what's the recommended on-disk format for reloading FusedMoE checkpoints (pre-fused `gate_up_proj` or something else)? Happy to test a patch.

title: Fully migrate IPC to msgpack: eliminate remaining PickleWrapper workarounds and flip default
body:
## Context

PR #28688 converted IPC dataclasses to `msgspec.Struct` and added opt-in msgpack transport (`SGLANG_USE_PICKLE_IPC=0`). However, several fields still use `PickleWrapper` as a fallback, and pickle remains the default. This issue tracks the remaining work to make the IPC path fully msgpack-native.

---

### Task 1 — [P0] Make `mm_inputs` fully msgpack-compatible

The `mm_inputs` field on both [`TokenizedGenerateReqInput`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/267d165ad0/python/sglang/srt/managers/io_struct.py#L775) and [`TokenizedEmbeddingReqInput`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/267d165ad0/python/sglang/srt/managers/io_struct.py#L1124) is typed as `Optional[PickleWrapper]` and carries a pickled [`MultimodalProcessorOutput`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/267d165ad0/python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py#L381).

**Why this is hard:** `MultimodalProcessorOutput` contains a list of [`MultimodalDataItem`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/267d165ad0/python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py#L244), which can hold:
- `torch.Tensor` / `np.ndarray` features (handled by existing `enc_hook`/`dec_hook`)
- [`CudaIpcTensorTransportProxy`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/267d165ad0/python/sglang/srt/utils/cuda_ipc_transport_utils.py#L286) — an opaque CUDA IPC handle wrapper with internal state dicts, pool handles, etc.
- `model_specific_data: dict[str, Any]` — a catch-all dict that different model processors populate with arbitrary tensors/values

**Work needed:**
1. Convert `MultimodalDataItem` and `MultimodalProcessorOutput` from `@dataclass` to `msgspec.Struct`.
2. Tighten `model_specific_data` — either enumerate known keys or add a `Dict[str, Union[torch.Tensor, ...]]` annotation.
3. Change the field type from `Optional[PickleWrapper]` to its real type and remove the corresponding lines in `wrap_pickle_fields()`/`unwrap_pickle_fields()` on [`TokenizedGenerateReqInput`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/267d165ad0/python/sglang/srt/managers/io_struct.py#L861-L869) and [`TokenizedEmbeddingReqInput`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/267d165ad0/python/sglang/srt/managers/io_struct.py#L1148-L1154).

---

### Task 2 — [P0] Make `time_stats` fully msgpack-compatible

The `time_stats` field appears on:
- [`TokenizedGenerateReqInput`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/267d165ad0/python/sglang/srt/managers/io_struct.py#L859) — carries `APIServerReqTimeStats` or `DPControllerReqTimeStats`
- [`TokenizedEmbeddingReqInput`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/267d165ad0/python/sglang/srt/managers/io_struct.py#L1146) — same
- [`BatchTokenIDOutput`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/267d165ad0/python/sglang/srt/managers/io_struct.py#L1251), [`BatchStrOutput`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/267d165ad0/python/sglang/srt/managers/io_struct.py#L1326), [`BatchEmbeddingOutput`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/267d165ad0/python/sglang/srt/managers/io_struct.py#L1360) — carry `List[SchedulerReqTimeStats]`

**Why this is hard:** The time stats classes ([`ReqTimeStatsBase`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/267d165ad0/python/sglang/srt/observability/req_time_stats.py#L224)) are `@dataclass` hierarchies that hold:
- [`TraceReqContext`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/267d165ad0/python/sglang/srt/observability/req_time_stats.py#L229) / `TraceNullContext` — OpenTelemetry tracing contexts with custom `__getstate__`/`__setstate__`
- [`SchedulerMetricsCollector`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/267d165ad0/python/sglang/srt/observability/req_time_stats.py#L226-L228) / `TokenizerMetricsCollector` — Prometheus metric objects (not serializable; excluded via `__getstate__`)
- [`DisaggregationMode`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/267d165ad0/python/sglang/srt/observability/req_time_stats.py#L232) enum
- Cross-process time calibration logic in `__getstate__`/`__setstate__`

**Work needed:**
1. Convert `ReqTimeStatsBase`, `APIServerReqTimeStats`, `DPControllerReqTimeStats`, `SchedulerReqTimeStats` from `@dataclass` to `msgspec.Struct`.
2. Update all `time_stats` fields from `Optional[PickleWrapper]` to their real types.

---

### Task 3 — [P1] Flip `SGLANG_USE_PICKLE_IPC` default to `False`

[`SGLANG_USE_PICKLE_IPC`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/267d165ad0/python/sglang/srt/environ.py#L245) is currently `EnvBool(True)`. Once Tasks 1 and 2 are done, flip to `False` and fix any CI failures that surface. This can be done incrementally — run CI with `SGLANG_USE_PICKLE_IPC=0` to find breakages before flipping the default.

---

### Task 4 — [P2] Eliminate opaque type annotations in `_REQ_TYPES_WITH_OPAQUE_FIELDS`

 [13 struct types](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/267d165ad0/python/sglang/srt/managers/io_struct.py#L2131-L2145) still use `Dict[str, Any]` / `List[Any]` fields, which forces them through whole-struct pickle wrapping in the msgpack path. For each type, tighten the field annotations to precise msgspec-compatible types so they can be removed from the registry.

---

### Task 5 — [P2] Make `customized_info` fully msgpack-compatible

The [`customized_info`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/267d165ad0/python/sglang/srt/managers/io_struct.py#L1243) field on `BatchTokenIDOutput` and [`BatchStrOutput`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/267d165ad0/python/sglang/srt/managers/io_struct.py#L1318) is typed as `Optional[PickleWrapper]` and carries arbitrary per-request metadata. Needs a concrete type annotation and msgpack serialization path.

---

### Task 6 — [P2] Make `mm_data_mooncake` fully msgpack-compatible

The [`mm_data_mooncake`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/267d165ad0/python/sglang/srt/managers/io_struct.py#L848) field on `TokenizedGenerateReqInput` is typed as `Optional[PickleWrapper]` and carries a pickled `Optional[List[{"url": MultimodalDataInputItem, "modality": Modality}]]` from `MMReceiverBase._extract_url_data`. Needs a concrete struct/type and msgpack serialization path.

---

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Task 1: `mm_inputs` uses real types, no `PickleWrapper`
- [ ] Task 2: All `time_stats` fields use real types, no `PickleWrapper`
- [ ] Task 3: `SGLANG_USE_PICKLE_IPC` defaults to `False`, CI green
- [ ] Task 4: `_REQ_TYPES_WITH_OPAQUE_FIELDS` is empty
- [ ] Task 5: `customized_info` uses real types, no `PickleWrapper`
- [ ] Task 6: `mm_data_mooncake` uses real types, no `PickleWrapper`

title: [Refactor] Confusing name: `global_num_tokens` collapses to `[local_num_tokens]` in pure DP+EP layout
body:
### Summary

The field `global_num_tokens` (and its variants `global_num_tokens_cpu` / `global_num_tokens_gpu` on `ForwardBatch`, plus the accessor `get_dp_global_num_tokens()`) has a misleading name: despite the `global_` prefix, in the pure DP + EP layout it does **not** hold a cross-rank list — it collapses to a length-1 list `[local_num_tokens]` holding only the current rank's count.

This is a documentation/naming issue only. Not requesting an immediate fix, just tracking it.

### Where the overloading happens

`python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler_components/dp_attn.py` (`_update_gather_batch`):

```python
if not require_mlp_tp_gather:
    batch.global_num_tokens = [mlp_sync_info.num_tokens]          # length 1: only THIS rank's count
else:
    batch.global_num_tokens = mlp_sync_info.global_num_tokens     # full length-dp_size gathered list
```

So the field's length and meaning are context-dependent:
- `require_mlp_tp_gather=True`  → full length-`dp_size` gathered list (the DP MLP-gather buffer packs every rank's tokens).
- `require_mlp_tp_gather=False` → `[local_num_tokens]` (length 1), because there is no shared buffer — each rank is standalone (attention DP + dense TP=1 + EP all-to-all).

Its true role (see `python/sglang/srt/model_executor/forward_batch_info.py` `prepare_mlp_sync_batch`, where `buffer_len` / per-rank slice are derived from it) is a **DP MLP-gather buffer layout descriptor**, not a global token census.

### Why it's confusing

- The name promises "across all ranks," but the value can be the *local* count — the opposite.
- Consumers must guard with `len(dp_global) > 1` to detect whether the gathered list is actually available. For example the FlashInfer A2A dispatcher (`python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/flashinfer.py`) does exactly this in its `runtime_max_tokens_per_rank` Case 1. This subtlety was a real trap while debugging #30242.
- Note `MLPSyncBatchInfo.global_num_tokens` (in `dp_attn.py`) is **accurately** named — it is always the true gathered list. Only the `ScheduleBatch` / `ForwardBatch` copies are overloaded.

### Suggested actions (pick one; no rush)

1. **Minimum:** add a precise comment at the field definitions (`schedule_batch.py`, `forward_batch_info.py`) and at the collapse site in `_update_gather_batch`, stating that `len` may be 1 (`[local]`), and that consumers must not assume `len == dp_size`.
2. **Better (invasive):** rename to something that reflects "MLP-gather buffer layout," e.g. `mlp_gather_num_tokens` / `mlp_sync_num_tokens`, and update all call sites including `get_dp_global_num_tokens()`. This touches the scheduler, forward batch, both cuda-graph runners, dp_attention, and spec decoding, so it should be a deliberate standalone change.

### Context

Surfaced while analyzing #30242 (FlashInfer A2A dispatcher `runtime_max_tokens_per_rank` selection). The `len(dp_global) > 1` guard is only correct because of this collapse behavior, which is not documented anywhere.

title: [Bug] MiniMax-M3: `thinking: {"type":"disabled"}` is silently ignored, model keeps reasoning
body:
## Checklist
- [x] Searched existing issues
- [x] Reproduced on latest main

## Describe the bug

MiniMax-M3 exposes reasoning control through the official OpenAI-compatible request field
`thinking: {"type": "disabled" | "adaptive"}` (documented in the MiniMax platform API docs, the
HuggingFace model card, and used by MiniMax's own `MiniMax-Provider-Verifier`).

When this field is sent to SGLang, it is **silently dropped**: the request returns `200 OK`, but the
model still produces reasoning (`reasoning_content` is non-empty). So `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}`
has no effect — thinking is never actually disabled.

This makes MiniMax's official verifier test `TestThinking::test_04_01_thinking_disabled` fail against
SGLang.

## Reproduction

Launch:

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --reasoning-parser auto \
  --tool-call-parser auto \
  --tp-size 4 \
  --port 8043
```

### A) Official API field — DOES NOT WORK (bug)

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8043/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello"}],
  "max_tokens": 128,
  "thinking": {"type": "disabled"}
}' | python3 -c 'import sys,json;m=json.load(sys.stdin)["choices"][0]["message"];print("reasoning_content:",repr(m.get("reasoning_content"))[:160])'
```

Actual: `reasoning_content: 'The user is asking me to say hello...'`  ← still thinking ❌

### B) reasoning_effort:"none" (SGLang native "reasoning off") — ALSO DOES NOT WORK

Same request but with `"reasoning_effort": "none"` instead of `thinking` → still returns
`reasoning_content` ❌

### C) chat_template_kwargs.thinking_mode=disabled — WORKS

```bash
curl -s http://localhost:8043/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3",
  "messages": [{"role,
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say hello"}],
  "max_tokens": 128,
  "chat_template_kwargs": {"thinking_mode": "disabled"}
}' | python3 -c 'import sys,json;m=json.load(sys.stdin)["choices"][0]["message"];print("reasoning_content:",repr(m.get("reasoning_content")))'
```

Actual: `reasoning_content: None` ← thinking disabled ✅

So the model and the M3 chat template are correct; only the serving-layer field mapping is missing.


## Expected behavior

Sending the official `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}`  should disable reasoning for MiniMax-M3


## Environment

- SGLang version: `0.5.15.post1.dev20260722+gb13abfdedf` (also present on current main)
- Model: `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3`

title: [RFC][Feature] Topology-transparent multi-NIC HTTP ingress with a single logical scheduling queue
body:
## Checklist

- [x] This is a feature request rather than a general question.
- [x] This issue is written in English.

## Motivation

### Summary

This RFC proposes topology-transparent multi-NIC HTTP ingress for the SGLang
router/server:

> Requests arriving through multiple host-facing NICs should converge into one
> logical scheduling queue, without changing the OpenAI-compatible API or
> application request path.

This is useful on inference nodes equipped with multiple front-side
NICs/DPUs/ENIs. A single ingress NIC can become a bandwidth or packets-per-second
bottleneck even when the Prefill/Decode and KV-transfer data planes have spare
capacity on other NICs.

### What Linux already provides

With one wildcard listener (`0.0.0.0:PORT` or `[::]:PORT`), Linux already
accepts connections addressed to any matching local interface into the same
listen socket and accept queue. Therefore, the baseline multi-NIC fan-in path
does **not** require per-NIC listeners or changes to SGLang's request API.

There are two important qualifications:

1. The accept queue is ordered by TCP handshake completion, not by client send
   time or SYN arrival time. This RFC does not promise a strict total order
   across NICs.
2. `SO_REUSEPORT` or multiple server workers create multiple kernel accept
   queues. If those modes are used for higher PPS, SGLang still needs one
   logical fan-in point before request scheduling to preserve global admission,
   priority, and fairness semantics.

### Current gap

Today this behavior is implicit. Operators lack:

- an explicit and tested multi-homed ingress contract;
- startup diagnostics confirming which addresses/interfaces can reach the
  listener;
- per-ingress-interface observability for connection rate, request rate,
  errors, and queueing;
- a benchmark that compares 1/2/4 ingress NICs and detects whether traffic
  actually spreads across them;
- a supported scale-up path when one accept queue or one HTTP worker becomes
  the bottleneck;
- a documented guarantee that optional multi-listener ingress converges before
  SGLang's scheduling/admission policy.

### Proposed design

#### Phase 0: Define and validate the zero-change baseline

- Document wildcard binding as the default multi-NIC ingress mode.
- At startup, report the bound address family, port, and whether the listener is
  wildcard-bound.
- Warn when configuration unintentionally binds to one specific host address.
- Add an integration test using two local destination addresses to verify that
  both paths reach the same SGLang endpoint and scheduler.

No request schema, OpenAI-compatible API, or model-worker change is required.

#### Phase 1: Add ingress observability

Expose optional, low-overhead metrics such as:

- accepted connections and HTTP requests by local destination
  address/interface;
- accept/HTTP queue depth or queueing delay where available;
- connection errors and resets by ingress path;
- aggregate versus per-path throughput and PPS.

Interface attribution may use the accepted socket's local address plus a cached
address-to-interface mapping. It should not add per-request routing decisions to
the model-serving hot path. If reliable attribution is unavailable on a
platform, metrics should fall back to local-address or aggregate labels instead
of guessing.

Suggested metric labels must remain bounded; raw client addresses must never be
used as labels.

#### Phase 2: Optional multi-listener fan-in for PPS scaling

If profiling shows that one accept queue/HTTP worker is the bottleneck, add an
opt-in ingress mode:

```text
NIC/IP A ─ listener/worker A ─┐
NIC/IP B ─ listener/worker B ─┼─> bounded MPSC fan-in ─> one logical
NIC/IP C ─ listener/worker C ─┘                         admission/scheduling queue
```

Possible implementations include `SO_REUSEPORT` workers or explicitly bound
per-address listeners. The implementation choice should be hidden behind the
router/server boundary.

Required semantics:

- existing endpoints and request schemas remain unchanged;
- all ingress paths share the same admission, priority, deadline, and fairness
  policy;
- bounded backpressure prevents one NIC from exhausting global queue capacity;
- no strict ordering is promised across independent TCP connections;
- failure or removal of one ingress NIC does not stop healthy listeners;
- the default remains the current single wildcard listener unless benchmarks
  justify enabling another mode.

### Alternatives considered

- **Linux bonding/LACP:** useful when available, but often unavailable for cloud
  ENIs, SR-IOV VFs, or independently managed DPUs. It also hides per-path
  observability.
- **External L4/L7 load balancer:** valid for cluster-level routing, but it does
  not remove the need to validate and observe multiple local ingress paths.
- **One SGLang instance per NIC:** duplicates serving state and fragments
  admission/scheduling queues, which is the opposite of the desired contract.
- **DPDK/XDP in the first version:** significantly increases operational
  complexity. The kernel wildcard-listener baseline should be measured first.

### Non-goals

- Configuring cloud ENIs, IP addresses, routes, bonding, or DPU firmware.
- Reordering packets or connections across NICs.
- Changing Mooncake/TENT KV-transfer path selection.
- Claiming bandwidth scaling when upstream routing still sends traffic to only
  one destination IP.

### Validation plan

On a node with 1/2/4 routable host-facing NICs:

1. Send independent HTTP workloads to each NIC's local IP and the same SGLang
   port.
2. Verify that all requests reach the same logical scheduler and preserve
   existing API behavior.
3. Measure aggregate requests/s, goodput, p50/p95/p99 latency, CPU utilization,
   accept/queue delay, drops, and fairness per ingress path.
4. Compare:
   - specific-address bind;
   - one wildcard listener;
   - optional `SO_REUSEPORT`/multi-listener fan-in.
5. Disable one ingress path during load and verify bounded impact on the others.

### Open questions

1. Should the first contribution be documentation + diagnostics + benchmark
   only, with multi-listener fan-in gated on evidence?
2. Is the SGLang Router the preferred single logical queue, or should the HTTP
   server expose a generic fan-in abstraction reusable without the router?
3. Which existing queue-delay/admission metrics should be reused to avoid a
   second ingress-only metric model?

## Related resources

- Linux `ip(7)`: binding to `INADDR_ANY` accepts traffic addressed to any local
  interface.
- Linux `socket(7)`: `SO_REUSEPORT` permits multiple sockets bound to the same
  address and port and distributes incoming connections.
- SGLang HTTP server entry point:
  `python/sglang/srt/entrypoints/http_server.py`.
- Related but separate work: #28631 proposes propagating request priority into
  the KV-transfer layer. This RFC concerns HTTP ingress before that scheduling
  and transfer path.

title: [RFC] Refactor weight loading code
body:
# Weight Loader RFC

Claude assisted, I took a pass, and most of the suggestions seem reaonsable.

This RFC describes a proposal for interfaces and abstractions for the model weight loading layer.

Today, we have 165 model files in `python/sglang/srt/models/`, each carrying its own ~50–150 line `load_weights`. The largest (`deepseek_v2.py`) is 2.4k lines. And `sglang/python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/deepseek_weight_loader.py` is over 700 lines long. 

Every time someone wants to fix a behavior here, they end up touching one model and missing the rest, since the same control flow is copy-pasted across the whole directory. For examples, the following PRs are for simply adding remapping per model for NVFP4 models:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/18224
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/18189

But the same happens for supporting PP, etc. 

(There are more, but I cannot find them right now..)

## Motivation

The per-model `load_weights` functions repeat the same boilerplate over and over. Some quick numbers from grep today:

- 116 / 165 model files declare their own `stacked_params_mapping` (almost always the same `qkv_proj` / `gate_up_proj` tuples).
- 83 / 165 files repeat the `rotary_emb.inv_freq` / `cos_cached` / `sin_cached` skip block verbatim.
- 27 / 165 files repeat the `maybe_remap_kv_scale_name(...)` block.
- 28 / 165 files repeat the `tie_word_embeddings` + `lm_head.weight` skip.
- 352 call sites to `is_pp_missing_parameter` / `start_layer` / `end_layer` guards, all sprinkled inside the per-model loops.

So fixes to FP8 kv-scale remapping, fused module support, or PP edge cases tend to land in one or two files and quietly miss the rest. The `DeepseekV2WeightLoaderMixin` extraction is evidence that we already feel this pain — but the pattern stops at one model family.

The control flow inside each `load_weights` is fundamentally the same procedural sweep:

```text
for name, weight in weights:
    skip rotary buffers;
    skip out-of-range PP layers;
    remap kv-scale names;
    skip lm_head if tied;
    walk stacked_params_mapping → maybe load + break;
    walk expert_params_mapping → maybe load + break;
    fall-through default_weight_loader.
```

This isn't really domain logic, it's plumbing — and it would be much nicer to have it living in one place.

For reference, vLLM solved a very similar problem with `AutoWeightsLoader` (`vllm/model_executor/models/utils.py:117`). Their `llama.py:load_weights` is 5 lines. Ours is 74 lines doing essentially the same thing.

## Proposal

### Abstraction

Three pieces, each non-intrusive:

1. **Walker** (`AutoWeightsLoader`). Given a root `nn.Module` and an iterable of `(name, tensor)`, it walks the module tree. For each child it finds, if that child has its own `load_weights`, defer to it; otherwise recurse; at the leaf, look up `param.weight_loader` (already the convention used by sglang's linear / fused MoE layers) and call it. This is where rotary skip, PP skip, kv-scale remap, tie-word-embeddings skip, and "not found" diagnostics all live exactly once.

2. **Name remapper** (`WeightsMapper`). A small declarative dataclass: `{regex|substr|prefix|suffix → new_name | None}`. Replaces the dozens of `name = name.replace("foo", "bar")` lines, plus the "set name to None to drop it" idiom. Composable via `|` so quant remaps and model remaps stack cleanly.

3. **Quirks registry**, parallel to the `OverrideRegistry` in the server-args proposal. Per-architecture hooks for things like DeepSeek's `fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa` (currently injected into `packed_modules_mapping` inside `__init__`) or w4afp8's expert-input-scale mapping. Today these are `if quant_config.get_name() == "w4afp8": ...` branches inside the loader; they should be registered, not branched, in the model loading code.

### Interface

After the walker is in place, a typical model's `load_weights` would look like:

```python
class LlamaForCausalLM(nn.Module):
    def load_weights(self, weights):
        loader = AutoWeightsLoader(
            self,
            skip_prefixes=["lm_head."] if self.config.tie_word_embeddings else None,
        )
        return loader.load_weights(weights)
```

That covers the 80% case. Models with real special cases override at the *module* level instead of the top-level model:

```python
class DeepseekV2MoE(nn.Module):
    def load_weights(self, weights):
        # MoE-specific expert sharding — only this submodule, not the whole model
        ...
```

The walker sees `DeepseekV2MoE.load_weights` exists and defers to it; the rest of the model still rides the auto path. This is where most of the win comes from: today, one quirk in one submodule forces you to write the entire top-level loader by hand.

```python
@WeightQuirkRegistry.register(["DeepseekV3ForCausalLM"])
def deepseek_quirks(model, mapper: WeightsMapper) -> WeightsMapper:
    if model.fuse_qkv_a_proj:
        mapper |= WeightsMapper(orig_to_new_substr={
            "q_a_proj": "fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa",
            "kv_a_proj_with_mqa": "fused_qkv_a_proj_with_mqa",
        })
    return mapper
```

Subsystem interface: nothing else in the codebase needs to know the walker exists. `model_loader/loader.py` keeps calling `model.load_weights(...)` exactly as today, and the change is local to `srt/models/*`.

## Breaking Changes

Since this is not exactly **public** API, we can maybe keep on making further changes for readability/usability/ease of maintenance. It will only affect those with out of tree models (requires them changing the mdoel code).

- Delete `stacked_params_mapping` and `packed_modules_mapping` from every model class. They move to the layer that owns the fusion. Out-of-tree models that copy-pasted these will need to drop them.
- Standardize the `load_weights` return type to `set[str]` (loaded param names). Today some return `None`, some return nothing. This unblocks "expected but missing" diagnostics in the walker.
- Delete `do_load_weights` / `DeepseekV2WeightLoaderMixin` — the walker subsumes it. Submodule-level `load_weights` overrides replace it cleanly.
- Delete `get_module_name_from_weight_name`, `get_num_params`, `get_weights_by_name` from individual model classes (used mostly by tests and weight-update RPC). These are mechanical and belong on the walker / a single helper, not duplicated per model.
- Drop the per-loop `is_pp_missing_parameter` / `start_layer` / `end_layer` checks. Make `PPMissingLayer` short-circuit traversal in the walker so model code never has to think about PP boundaries again. (~352 call sites go away.)
- Lift the `ThreadPoolExecutor` + `should_async_load` path out of the DeepSeek mixin and make it the default in the walker, so every model gets it for free. Behavior change: load order becomes non-deterministic, but `weight_loader` callers should already not depend on order.
- Standardize on `Iterable[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]` (drop the legacy `Tuple` typing, drop the variant signatures like `is_nextn=False` kwarg — the NextN distinction can be handled by a quirk that swaps in a different mapper).
- `bitsandbytes_stacked_params_mapping` becomes the same registry mechanism, not a separate per-model attribute.

These are aggressive but each one removes a category of duplication, not just lines.

## Open questions

1. Migration order. first, do the easy and less used models, we can do Deepseek files at the very end.

title: [Bug] FP8 KV-cache decode slowdown: unfused K/V quantization + per-layer Q conversion overhead
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug


## 1. Problem

When enabling `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` on Hopper (H200, SM90) with the fa3 backend, **decoding slows down** compared to BF16 KV-cache, especially on small batches and short contexts. The slowdown is caused by **runtime overhead** that is absent on the BF16 path and that is **not eliminated by a static FP8 checkpoint**.

The root cause is architectural: sglang performs FP8 KV-cache quantization as a series of **separate Python-level tensor operations** (multiple kernel launches per layer per step), whereas the BF16 path is a single optimized `store_cache` call. On memory-bound decode with small batches, this overhead outweighs the 2× reduction in KV read traffic.

### Symptom

| Scenario | BF16 KV | FP8 KV (fa3) |
|----------|---------|---------------|
| Small batch (1-8), short context | baseline | **10-30% slower** |
| Small batch, long context (32K+) | baseline | possibly faster |
| Large batch (128+) | baseline | slightly faster |

---

## 2. Bottlenecks & comparison with vLLM

### 2.1. Bottleneck 1: Unfused K/V quantization on cache write

In [`set_kv_buffer`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/bc82b064004f2e17f09db52afeed52cdf53a87be/python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/memory_pool.py#L1784), quantizing K/V to FP8 is **3-4 separate operations**:

```python
# memory_pool.py:1784-1790 — 4 separate kernel launches per layer per step
if cache_k.dtype != self.dtype:
    if k_scale is not None:
        cache_k.div_(k_scale)      # launch 1: in-place divide K
    if v_scale is not None:
        cache_v.div_(v_scale)      # launch 2: in-place divide V
    cache_k = cache_k.to(self.dtype)  # launch 3: cast K → FP8
    cache_v = cache_v.to(self.dtype)  # launch 4: cast V → FP8
```

This is followed by a separate `store_cache` call to write into the paged cache. On the BF16 path, only `store_cache` runs (single optimized kernel).

**vLLM solution:** vLLM fuses quantization **into the cache-write kernel** itself. In [`reshape_and_cache_kernel_flash`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/26ff616bbf43c5c5ecb847589705cebdbff46706/vllm/v1/attention/ops/triton_reshape_and_cache_flash.py#L109), the division by scale and the implicit FP8 cast happen inside the same triton kernel that stores to the paged cache:

```python
# vLLM: 1 kernel launch — load → divide → implicit cast → store
if FP8_KV_CACHE:
    key_tile = key_load if key_load.dtype.is_fp8() else key_load / tl.load(k_scale)
else:
    key_tile = key_load
# ...
tl.store(key_cache_ptr + tgt_idx_k, key_tile, mask=...)  # implicit cast to FP8
```

### 2.2. Bottleneck 2: Per-layer Q→FP8 conversion in fa3 backend

In `forward_decode`, Q is converted to FP8 **on every layer, every step**:

```python
# flashattention_backend.py:1608-1615 — 3 conversions per layer per step
if self.kv_cache_dtype_str != "auto" and layer.head_dim <= 256:
    if layer.k_scale is not None:
        descale_shape = (forward_batch.batch_size, layer.tp_k_head_num)
        k_descale = layer.k_scale.expand(descale_shape)
        v_descale = layer.v_scale.expand(descale_shape)
    q = q.to(self.kv_cache_dtype)              # conversion 1: Q → FP8
    q_rope = q_rope.to(self.kv_cache_dtype)    # conversion 2: q_rope → FP8
    k_rope = k_rope.to(self.kv_cache_dtype)    # conversion 3: k_rope → FP8
```

For a model with ~64 layers, this is **64+ × 3 = ~192 `.to()` launches** per forward pass. Each `.to()` has ~2-5μs launch overhead → **~400-1000μs of pure launch overhead** per decode step, comparable to the entire attention computation on small batches.

**vLLM solution:** vLLM quantizes Q **centrally in the Attention layer** (once), not in each backend. In `Attention.forward`, a single `query_quant` call handles it, and crucially it **fuses with preceding ops via `torch.compile`**:

```python
# vLLM attention.py:511-521 — single quantization, fused via torch.compile
if self.query_quant is not None:
    # quantizing with a simple torch operation enables
    # torch.compile to fuse this into previous ops
    # which reduces overheads during decoding.
    if self.impl.supports_quant_query_input:
        query, _ = self.query_quant(query, self._q_scale)
```

### 2.3. Bottleneck 3: fa3 FP8 decode kernel less optimized than BF16

FA3 split-KV decode with FP8 Q × FP8 KV is a less-tuned path than the primary BF16 path. The `num_splits=0` auto-heuristic `flashattention_backend.py:345` adds a combine-stage overhead.

**vLLM flashinfer on SM90:** completely avoids Q quantization on decode via `resolve_query_dtype` — uses **BF16 Q × FP8 KV** (descale on read), which is both faster and more accurate (single quantization error on KV only).

### 2.4. Tabular comparison: sglang vs vLLM

| Operation | sglang (fa3) | vLLM (flash_attn) | vLLM (flashinfer SM90) |
|-----------|-------------|-------------------|------------------------|
| **Q → FP8 conversion** | ❌ `q.to()` per layer (192+ launches) | ⚠️ `query_quant` once, **fused via torch.compile** | ✅ None (BF16 Q) |
| **q_rope → FP8** | ❌ per layer | ✅ None (handled in kernel) | ✅ None |
| **k_rope → FP8** | ❌ per layer | ✅ None (handled in kernel) | ✅ None |
| **K ÷ scale** | ❌ separate `div_` launch | ✅ **fused in write kernel** | ✅ **fused in write kernel** |
| **V ÷ scale** | ❌ separate `div_` launch | ✅ **fused in write kernel** | ✅ **fused in write kernel** |
| **K → FP8 cast** | ❌ separate `.to()` launch | ✅ implicit cast in `tl.store` | ✅ implicit cast in kernel |
| **V → FP8 cast** | ❌ separate `.to()` launch | ✅ implicit cast in `tl.store` | ✅ implicit cast in kernel |
| **Paged cache write** | separate `store_cache` | **same kernel as quant** | **same kernel as quant** |
| **Kernel launches for K/V write** | **~5** | **1** | **1** |
| **Attention compute** | FP8 Q × FP8 KV | FP8 Q × FP8 KV (descale params) | **BF16 Q × FP8 KV** (descale on read) |
| **Accuracy** | ❌ double quant error (Q+KV) | ❌ double quant error | ✅ single quant error (KV only) |

---

## 3. Proposed changes

### 3.1. Fuse K/V quantization into the cache-write kernel (high impact)

**Goal:** eliminate the 4 separate `div_` + `.to()` launches in `set_kv_buffer`.

**Approach:** extend the existing `store_cache` JIT kernel (or add a triton variant) to accept `k_scale`/`v_scale` and the target dtype, performing the division + cast **inside** the write kernel — exactly as vLLM does in `reshape_and_cache_kernel_flash` .

```python
# Proposed: single fused kernel call instead of div_ + to() + store_cache
store_cache_fp8(
    k, v,
    self.k_buffer[layer_id],
    self.v_buffer[layer_id],
    loc,
    k_scale=k_scale,   # passed into kernel, division fused
    v_scale=v_scale,
    out_dtype=self.dtype,  # FP8 — implicit cast on store
)
```

**Expected benefit:** reduces ~5 kernel launches to 1 per layer per step. On a 64-layer model, this removes ~256 launches per decode step.

**Affected files:**
- `memory_pool.py` — `set_kv_buffer`, `set_kv_buffer_prefix_valid` (line 1877), and the SWA variant (line 2234)
- `sglang/jit.kernel/kvcache` — extend `store_cache` or add `store_cache_fp8`

### 3.2. Centralize Q quantization and enable torch.compile fusion (high impact)

**Goal:** eliminate per-layer `q.to(FP8)` / `q_rope.to(FP8)` / `k_rope.to(FP8)` in `forward_decode` and `forward_extend` in flashattention_backend.py.

**Approach:** move Q quantization out of the backend into the RadixAttention layer (as vLLM does in `Attention.forward` - model_executor/layers/attention/attention.py:511, so it happens **once** and can be **fused with preceding ops** (RoPE, QKV projection) via torch.compile:

```python
# Proposed: in RadixAttention.forward, before calling backend
if self.kv_cache_dtype_str != "auto" and self.supports_quant_query_input:
    # single quantization, fusable with prior ops via torch.compile
    q, _ = scaled_fp8_quant(q, self.q_scale)
    # q_rope / k_rope handled inside the attention kernel, not here
```

Then the fa3 backend receives already-quantized Q and does **no** `.to()` calls.

**Expected benefit:** removes ~192 `.to()` launches per decode step on a 64-layer model; enables compiler fusion.

**Affected files:**
- `flashattention_backend.py` — remove `q.to()` / `q_rope.to()` / `k_rope.to()` from `forward_decode` and `forward_extend`
- RadixAttention layer — add centralized `query_quant`

---

## Summary

The FP8 KV-cache decode slowdown in sglang is caused by **unfused runtime quantization** — separate `div_` + `.to()` launches for K/V and per-layer `q.to(FP8)` conversions. vLLM avoids most of this overhead by (1) fusing K/V quantization into the cache-write kernel and (2) centralizing Q quantization in the Attention layer where it fuses with preceding ops via torch.compile. On SM90, vLLM's flashinfer further avoids Q quantization entirely on decode (BF16 Q × FP8 KV).

The proposed changes would bring sglang's FP8 KV-cache path closer to vLLM's efficiency, with the fused write kernel (3.1) and centralized Q quantization (3.2) providing the largest gains.

title: [Bug] --preferred-sampling-params is inert on /v1/chat/completions (re-report of #21816; the five get_param keys are affected too)
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

`--preferred-sampling-params` has no effect on `/v1/chat/completions`. Every key is
overridden, including the five that #21816 believed were working.

This re-reports **#21816**, which was closed by the stale bot on 2026-06-01 rather than by a
fix — both PRs that addressed it (#21821, #21997) were closed unmerged. Confirming it is live
in **v0.5.19**, and correcting one detail of the original report that matters for the fix.

**Mechanism.** `tokenizer_manager.py` merges preferred params *under* the request:

```python
sampling_kwargs = {**self.preferred_sampling_params, **obj.sampling_params}
```

and `ChatCompletionRequest.to_sampling_params()` resolves **every** sampler key eagerly through
`get_param()` — user value → `model_generation_config` → `_DEFAULT_SAMPLING_PARAMS` — so
`obj.sampling_params` is always fully populated and always wins. The merged dict is
byte-identical to the unmerged one.

**The correction to #21816.** That issue says only a handful of keys are affected and that
`temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k`, `min_p`, `repetition_penalty` "worked correctly because they
used the `get_param()` helper with proper `None` fallback." They do not. `get_param()` falls
back to the *generation config* and then to the *OpenAI default* — never to
`preferred_sampling_params` — so it always yields a concrete value that wins the merge. With
an empty generation config, `top_k` resolves to **`-1`**, silently disabling top-k sampling
rather than merely using a different value.

### Reproduction

No GPU or weights needed — it is entirely in the request-to-params path:

```python
from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.protocol import ChatCompletionRequest

pref = {"temperature": 0.7, "top_p": 0.80, "top_k": 20,
        "min_p": 0.0, "presence_penalty": 1.5, "repetition_penalty": 1.0}

r  = ChatCompletionRequest(model="m", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}])
sp = r.to_sampling_params(stop=[], model_generation_config={})   # client sends no sampler fields
print({**pref, **sp})        # <- the tokenizer_manager merge
```

```
                     preferred   effective
temperature          0.7         1.0     LOST
top_p                0.8         1.0     LOST
top_k                20          -1      LOST   <- top-k silently disabled
min_p                0.0         0.0     (coincides)
presence_penalty     1.5         0.0     LOST
repetition_penalty   1.0         1.0     (coincides)
```

Same result with a populated generation config — the values simply become the generation
config's instead of the flag's.

### Why this bites in practice

Qwen3.8 publishes **two** sampler rows on its model card — a thinking row and an instruct row
that differs in `temperature`, `top_p` and `presence_penalty`. The checkpoint's
`generation_config.json` carries the thinking row, so `--sampling-defaults model` serves that
one correctly. There is no way to serve the **other** row server-side: `--preferred-sampling-params`
is the flag for it and is inert, and `presence_penalty` is additionally outside the
`get_default_sampling_params()` allowlist. Operators running the documented non-thinking mode
get thinking-row sampling unless every client is modified to send the row itself.

### A fix already exists in this file

`ResponsesRequest.to_sampling_params()` (`protocol.py`) does the right thing and says so:

```python
# Omit None entries so they fall through to ``--preferred-sampling-params``
# rather than overriding it with a literal default.
```

The chat path needs the same treatment: emit only keys the user actually set (`model_fields_set`
distinguishes them), or exclude them from the merge. That is essentially what #21997 implemented
before it went stale.

Happy to open a PR narrowly scoped to the chat path if that shape is wanted.

### Environment

`lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.19`, stock, no patches. Reproduces in the image with no model loaded.

Found while building SGLang serving configs for Qwen3.8-27B in
https://github.com/noonghunna/club-3090 (issue is in SGLang, not in that repo).

title: [Bug] Illegal memory access in the Triton fused-MoE kernel when `flashinfer_megamoe` is combined with EAGLE speculative decoding (GLM-5.2-NVFP4, sm_107)
body:
## Summary

On a `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` (GLM-5.2-NVFP4, MLA + DSA) deployment, enabling
`--moe-a2a-backend flashinfer_megamoe --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_megamoe`
**together with** EAGLE speculative decoding reliably produces

```
RuntimeError: Triton Error [CUDA]: an illegal memory access was encountered
```

Either feature alone works. With `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, the fault is attributed
to **sglang's own Triton fused-MoE kernel on the unquantized (draft-model) MoE
path** — not to any FlashInfer MegaMOE kernel:

```
srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py       forward_impl -> run_moe_core
srt/layers/quantization/unquant.py:1008        apply
srt/layers/quantization/unquant.py:1110        forward_cuda
srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton.py:129        run
srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/triton_utils/fused_moe.py:620   _fused_moe_kernel_sequence
kernels/ops/moe/fused_moe_triton_kernels.py:1004          invoke_fused_moe_kernel
triton/runtime/jit.py -> <illegal memory access>
```

So this looks less like a MegaMOE kernel defect and more like a state/config
conflict between the two MoE backends coexisting in one server: the main model
runs MegaMOE while the EAGLE draft model runs the unquantized Triton fused-MoE
runner, and the draft path faults.

Note `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` is not in `validate_flashinfer_megamoe_model`'s
`validated_architectures`; we added it locally in order to evaluate MegaMOE (see
Reproduction). If the omission is deliberate, this report can be read as evidence
supporting it — but the fault location suggests the problem is not
architecture-specific.

## Ask

- Is `flashinfer_megamoe` expected to coexist with speculative decoding, given
  that the draft model dispatches through a different MoE runner?
- If the two are not meant to coexist, would a startup-time rejection be
  preferable to the current failure mode?
- We can re-run under `compute-sanitizer` and attach the kernel-level trace if
  that would help — please let us know the preferred invocation.

### Reproduction

Single node, 4 GPUs, stock container, no patches other than the allowlist line.

**Step 1 — allow the architecture.** `validate_flashinfer_megamoe_model` rejects
`GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` before the server starts, so it must be added first. This
is the only source change:

```diff
  # python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/moe_hook.py, validate_flashinfer_megamoe_model
   validated_architectures = (
       ...
       "Glm4MoeForCausalLM",
+      "GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM",
       "NemotronHForCausalLM",
       ...
   )
```

**Step 2 — launch with MegaMOE *and* EAGLE.**

```bash
export SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MEGAMOE_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=16384   # = chunked-prefill-size / dp_size
export CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1                                # for synchronous attribution

python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /path/to/GLM-5.2-NVFP4 --trust-remote-code \
  --quantization modelopt_fp4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --data-parallel-size 4 --expert-parallel-size 4 \
  --enable-dp-attention --enable-dp-lm-head \
  --chunked-prefill-size 65536 --max-running-requests 32 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --context-length 131072 \
  --disable-radix-cache --disable-cuda-graph --watchdog-timeout 1800 \
  --moe-a2a-backend flashinfer_megamoe --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_megamoe \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-steps 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 2
```

The server dies during startup/warmup, before serving any request. No load is
needed to trigger it.

**Step 3 — remove one of the two features and it runs.** Dropping
`--speculative-algorithm EAGLE ...` (keeping MegaMOE) serves requests normally,
including under sustained load — we verified 16 concurrent requests of ~67k
prompt tokens each, with prefill batches reaching the full 16,384 tokens/rank.

## Observed matrix

| MegaMOE | EAGLE/MTP | Result |
|---|---|---|
| on | off | works — full load, coherent output |
| **on** | **on** | **illegal memory access** in `invoke_fused_moe_kernel` |
| off | on | works (see caveat below) |

Reproduced with `--speculative-num-steps 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 2` and
with `3 / 4`; the outcome and the faulting frame are the same in both. Two
independent `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` runs attribute the fault to
`fused_moe.py:620` and `fused_moe.py:826` respectively — both inside
`_fused_moe_kernel_sequence` → `invoke_fused_moe_kernel`.

We also tried isolating the draft path with
`--speculative-moe-runner-backend deep_gemm` (and additionally
`--speculative-moe-a2a-backend deepep`). That removes the illegal-memory-access
signature but the server still fails, with `tvm.error.InternalError` from
deep_gemm and `CUDA error 719 (CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED)` respectively. Given
that 719 is a typical downstream symptom of a prior asynchronous memory fault, we
do not read these as a fix.

### Caveat on the third row

The "MegaMOE off, EAGLE on" cell is **not** from this single-node harness. In our
minimal setup that configuration never finished initializing — it reaches
`fired up and ready to roll!` and then stalls inside
`_draft_extend_for_prefill (eagle_worker_v2.py:1085)` until the watchdog fires.
Seven attempts, all infrastructure-bound (cold JIT compilation is very slow here;
we lack a warm `SGLANG_DG_CACHE`). We are not reporting that stall as a bug — it
may well be specific to our environment.

That row instead comes from our production deployment: a 6-node disaggregated
prefill/decode setup running the same model with EAGLE enabled and MegaMOE off,
which completes 3,600-second benchmark runs with no errors, repeatedly. So the
two arms of the comparison come from different scales, which we note for honesty.

### Environment

```
Python: 3.12.3 (main, Aug 31 2026, 10:18:26) [GCC 13.3.0]
CUDA available: True
GPU 0,1,2,3: NVIDIA Graphics Device
GPU 0,1,2,3 Compute Capability: 10.7
CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda
NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 13.4, V13.4.46
CUDA Driver Version: 620.43
PyTorch: 2.15.0.dev20260818+cu134
sglang: 0.0.0.dev1+g0abb251a2.d20260921
sglang-kernel: 0.4.7
flashinfer_python: 0.6.18
flashinfer_cubin: 0.6.18
flashinfer_jit_cache: 0.6.18+cu134
triton: 3.8.0+gitdf3f91dd
transformers: 5.12.1
torchao: Module Not Found
numpy: 2.3.5
aiohttp: 3.14.3
fastapi: 0.141.1
huggingface_hub: 1.32.0
interegular: 0.3.3
modelscope: 1.40.1
orjson: 3.12.0
outlines: 0.1.11
packaging: 26.3
psutil: 7.2.2
pydantic: 2.13.5
python-multipart: 0.0.32
pyzmq: 27.2.0
```

title: [Feature][DSv4.1] Tracking: every backend's two-level candidate indexer behind CandidateIndexer
body:
## Context

DeepSeek-V4.1's low-ratio index layers select attention positions in two levels: the candidate source (layer 20) keeps the best `candidate_topk_blocks = 2048` blocks of 8 compressed positions per query row, the consumers (24 / 28 / 32 / 36) run their top-512 among those blocks. PR [#40352](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40352) put the prefill side of that behind one interface, `CandidateIndexer` (`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsv4/candidate_indexer.py`):

```python
class CandidateIndexer(ABC):
    def publish_prefill(self, inputs: PrefillIndexerInputs, out_positions) -> CandidateMetadata
    def select_prefill(self, published, inputs, out_positions) -> None
    def prefill_tail(self, published, tail_lens) -> CandidateMetadata
```

with two implementations, and the decode side already had one:

| implementation | file | prefill | decode / verify |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DeepGemmCandidateIndexer` (SM100) | `dsv4/candidate_indexer_deep_gemm.py` | block table from the source's dense tiles (`amax8_varlen`, ragged top-k, `sort_candidate_blocks`, DeepGEMM schedule); consumers score only their blocks with `fp8_fp4_paged_sparse_mqa_logits` + `topk_transform_bf16_small` | `publish_decode` / `select_decode`, same kernels over the paged index-K pool |
| `DenseCandidateIndexer` | `dsv4/dense_prefill_indexer.py` | #40217's `dense_prefill_topk`: block ids per request (`PrefillCandidateBlocks`), consumers rebuild a mask per 2 GiB tile and run the plain top-k | — |

`make_candidate_indexer` returns the DeepGEMM indexer on SM100 (with the dense one for prefill under context parallelism) and `None` on everything else. The backend's dense prefill path (`_low_ratio_index_topk_dense`) only calls the three methods; on 4x B200 at 262K context that took the four consumer layers from 41 ms to 2.6 ms each and TTFT from 6.7 s to 5.3 s.

Everything else still scores the whole context and selects through masks inline in `deepseek_v4_backend.py`, or has no DSv4.1 low-ratio path at all. This issue lists what is left, per backend and mode, with the code that has to move.

## Where the candidate indexer runs today

| platform / mode | entry point | how candidates are handled | cost per index layer |
|---|---|---|---|
| SM100 CUDA (and `DeepseekV4TrtllmAttnBackend`, which inherits it), decode + target-verify | `_low_ratio_index_topk_decode` -> `DeepGemmCandidateIndexer.publish_decode` / `select_decode` | block table + DeepGEMM sparse logits; graph variants `candidate_all` / `candidate_c2_all` / `candidate_unfiltered` / `candidate_filtered` (`graph_variants.py`, `decode_cuda_graph_runner.py`) | consumers score 2048 x 8 positions |
| SM100 CUDA, extend (dense fp4 path) | `_low_ratio_index_topk_dense` -> `CandidateIndexer` | block table, consumers sparse | source 43.5 ms, consumer 2.6 ms at 16K rows x 262K |
| SM100 CUDA, extend under CP (`_forward_low_ratio_sources_cp`) | same, but `make_candidate_indexer` hands the DeepGEMM indexer a `DenseCandidateIndexer` for prefill | dense tiles + masks | consumer 41 ms |
| SM100 CUDA, extend inside the prefill CUDA graph | `_low_ratio_index_topk_prefill_graph` | none needed: asserts `width <= candidate_topk_blocks * candidate_block_size`, so every block is a candidate and the plain top-k is the whole selection | — |
| SM90 CUDA, decode + verify | `_low_ratio_index_topk_sm90_decode` | **inline**: Triton `fp4_index_logits_decode` scores all `[B, L]` positions per index layer; the source builds `CandidateMasks(mask=[B, L] bool)` with `select_candidate_blocks`; consumers `masked_fill` + `torch.topk` + `mask_topk_scores` | full context per consumer |
| SM90 CUDA, extend (and SM100 with `SGLANG_DSV41_TORCH_PREFILL_INDEXER=1`) | `_low_ratio_index_topk_torch` | **inline**: per request, per row chunk, bf16 einsum over dequantized K (`get_low_ratio_index_k_dequant`); source publishes `CandidateMasks(request_masks=[[rows_b, lc_b] bool])`, consumers mask + `torch.topk`; the tail cut goes through `_publish_prefill_masks` / `cut_request_masks` | full context per consumer, plus the masks |
| ROCm (`DeepseekV4HipRadixBackend`, selected for `dsv4` on HIP in `attention_registry.py`) | — | no ratio-1/2 (`low_ratio`) path at all: the backend carries the V4 C4 indexer only (`C4IndexerBackendMixin`); its metadata only knows compress ratios 0 / 4 / 128 | DSv4.1 not served |
| NPU (`DeepseekV4AscendAttnBackend`) | — | no DSv4.1 low-ratio path | DSv4.1 not served |

`make_candidate_indexer` and the graph variants are gated on `device_sm >= 100` / `not is_hip()`, so on every non-SM100 target the protocol is simply absent.

## Work items

### 1. Hopper decode / verify behind the protocol, consumers scoring candidates only

`_low_ratio_index_topk_sm90_decode` (backend ~L3475) is the only decode path outside `CandidateIndexer`. Today each consumer layer scores `[bs, L]` for the whole context and masks 15 of every 16 columns away, and the graph variants of `graph_variants.py` are not built for it.

- Add `publish_decode` / `select_decode` to the `CandidateIndexer` ABC (they exist on `DeepGemmCandidateIndexer` only) and move the SM90 code into an implementation, so the backend's decode dispatch is `self.candidate_indexer.publish_decode(...)` / `select_decode(...)` on every platform.
- Consumer scoring: there is no DeepGEMM paged sparse kernel below SM100. Options: extend `fp4_index_logits_decode` (Triton, `kernels/ops/attention/dsv4/fp4_indexer.py`) with a block-id input so it reads only the 2048 blocks per row (`slots[b, blocks[b, i // 8] * 8 + i % 8]`), or reuse the gathering Triton scorer of #40268 (`candidate_fp4_mqa_logits`, contiguous K) once it takes per-row block ids for a batch.
- Decode graph variants for SM90 once the selection has a fixed shape.

### 2. Torch prefill path behind the protocol

`_low_ratio_index_topk_torch` (backend ~L3555) is Hopper's prefill indexer and the SM100 test oracle. Its publish / consume is interleaved with the per-request row-chunk loop, so it does not fit `publish_prefill` / `select_prefill` as written.

- Restructure into a `TorchCandidateIndexer` (or fold into `DenseCandidateIndexer` with a torch scorer) that publishes `PrefillCandidateBlocks` per request and consumes them by gathering the kept blocks' dequantized K rows (`index_select` over `[2048 * 8]` rows per query row is the natural sparse path for torch) instead of scoring `[rows, lc]` and masking.
- Then `_publish_prefill_masks` / `cut_request_masks` / `CandidateMasks.request_masks` go away, and `enter_late_layer_tail` is the same on every platform.
- Keep the oracle property: the kernel tests (`test_dsv41_prefill_sparse_indexer.py`) compare implementations pairwise, so the torch one should stay the reference the others are checked against.

### 3. DeepGEMM sparse prefill under context parallelism

`make_candidate_indexer` gives the DeepGEMM indexer a `DenseCandidateIndexer` for prefill when `attn_cp_size > 1`, because a CP rank's local rows are interleaved across the prompt and `core.page_table[:num_tokens]` is not their page table. The consumers then pay the dense pass again (41 ms per layer at 262K).

- Build the per-row index page table from `req_to_token` (the way `slot_chunks` in `_low_ratio_index_topk_dense` already derives the slots: `req_to_token[req, j * ratio] // ratio`) so `PrefillIndexerInputs.kv_page_table` is CP-agnostic, then drop `prefill_dense`.
- Needs a CP run to validate; nothing in CI exercises DSv4.1 prefill CP with candidates today.

### 4. ROCm and the other backends

`DeepseekV4HipRadixBackend` (what `attention_registry.py` picks for `dsv4` on HIP) has no ratio-1/2 compressor / indexer path, so DSv4.1 does not run there yet; the Ascend backend has none either. When those land, the candidate indexer should be implemented against the protocol from the start rather than inline: `fp8_fp4_mqa_logits` / the paged sparse kernel are CUDA-only (`_has_dense_fp4_indexer` checks `torch.version.cuda`), so the ROCm implementation would be aiter or Triton (the scorer of item 1 is the natural shared piece).

### 5. SM100 follow-ups inside the DeepGEMM implementation

Not backend coverage, but the remaining cost on the covered path:

- `get_paged_sparse_mqa_logits_metadata` is one 14 ms launch per chunk at 16384 rows (about 290 MB of schedule); all rows of a chunk share one page-table row, so a cheaper schedule for many rows of one request is the next win on the source side.
- The source's own top-512 and the block keys read every score tile twice (`TODO(dark)` in `candidate_indexer_deep_gemm.py`: one kernel for both).
- Verify rows: `publish_decode` pairs rows by `request_ids`; the prefill table uses the same path, but DSpark target-verify with candidates only has the `candidate_filtered` variant.

## Contract for a new implementation

- Prefill: `publish_prefill(inputs, out_positions)` writes the source layer's own top-k (flattened-K columns, `-1` padded, unordered) into `out_positions` and returns the published metadata; `select_prefill(published, inputs, out_positions)` writes a consumer's top-k in the same layout; `prefill_tail(published, tail_lens)` returns the metadata restricted to the last `tail_lens[b]` rows of each request. `PrefillIndexerInputs` carries the fp4 query, head weights, `compress_lens`, `request_starts`, rows and lengths per request, the flattened index K, the index-K pool view and the KV page table; `dense_prefill_indexer.score_tiles(inputs)` yields the dense scores tile by tile under #40217's budget for implementations that need them.
- Decode: `publish_decode(inputs, page_indices, raw_indices)` / `select_decode(published, inputs, page_indices, raw_indices)` over `IndexerInputs` (to be added to the ABC with item 1).
- Equivalence: the published blocks must equal `select_candidate_blocks` on the `-inf`-masked scores block for block; a consumer's selection must agree with `DenseCandidateIndexer.select_prefill` on the same inputs except at rounding-boundary ties (`test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_dsv41_prefill_sparse_indexer.py` is parametrizable over implementations); `test_dsv4_nonpaged_indexer.py::TestCandidateIndexerGating` pins what `make_candidate_indexer` returns per platform.

### Related resources

_No response_

title: [Bug][Diffusion] Warmup request finalization reloads offloaded components and triggers OOM on Wan2.2 A14B
body:
## Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest release.
- [x] Environment information and a minimal reproduction are included below.
- [x] This is a bug report rather than a general question.
- [x] This report is written in English.

## Describe the bug

With component offload enabled for the DiT, text encoder, and VAE, Wan2.2-T2V-A14B fails during **synthetic server warmup request finalization** on a single NVIDIA L20.

The first OOM is in `ComponentOffloadStrategy.finish_request()` → `prepare_for_use()` → `module.to(device)`. Model loading and the warmup pipeline body have already completed. The server then retries smaller synthetic warmups, which also fail after the first failed reload leaves almost no free device memory.

On the same L20 checkout and with the same component-residency configuration, adding `--warmup-mode off` allows model loading and server startup to complete without OOM. No generation request was run in that control, so this comparison isolates the startup failure to the server-warmup path but does not establish that a full generation fits. We would like to keep warmup enabled while retaining the memory savings of component offload.

### Expected behavior

Warmup finalization should respect the available device-memory budget when restoring preferred components. A warmup request that reaches finalization under sequential component offload should not require a larger simultaneous weight footprint just to finish. If optional preloading cannot fit, the components should remain offloaded and be loaded when needed.

### Actual behavior and logs

The first automatic warmup candidate uses 832 × 480 and 17 frames. The first failure occurs in its finalization path:

```text
pipeline_executor.py, in _component_residency_request
    self.finish_component_residency_request()
pipeline_executor.py, in finish_component_residency_request
    self.component_residency_manager.finish_request()
component_manager.py, in finish_request
    strategy.finish_request(module, use, self.state, preferred=preferred)
component_residency_strategies.py, in finish_request
    self.prepare_for_use(module, use, state)
component_residency_strategies.py, in prepare_for_use
    _module_to_local_device(module, dtype=use.target_dtype)
component_residency_strategies.py, in _module_to_local_device
    module.to(device, non_blocking=True)

torch.OutOfMemoryError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 50.00 MiB.
GPU 0 has a total capacity of 44.39 GiB of which 6.06 MiB is free.
42.55 GiB is allocated by PyTorch, and 545.07 MiB is reserved by PyTorch but unallocated.

Synthetic server warmup failed; continuing startup
```

The first L20 warmup request reaches request finalization before failing. The server retries with fewer frames, but the failed `module.to()` has no rollback. Later retries therefore fail in text-encoder execution and then enter the same failing `finish_request()` path again. These are subsequent failures; the stack above identifies the initial warmup OOM.

The loaded component sizes reported in the same run are 21.16 GB for the text encoder, 26.62 GB for each transformer, and 0.47 GB for the VAE. Reloading preferred components at request end creates a simultaneous weight footprint that does not fit the L20's 44.39 GiB allocator-reported capacity, even though sequential component offload is configured.

### Investigation

The component-offload strategy reloads a component during `finish_request()` when both `preferred` and `state.batch_is_warmup` are true. The manager processes request-end components in a single loop, so this can interleave loading preferred components with releasing other components. There is also a separate `keep_ready_after_warmup` path.

Our hypothesis is that request-end preloading creates a larger simultaneous weight footprint than the sequential offload execution requires. We have not yet captured a per-component device-residency snapshot at the allocation failure, so the exact overlapping components remain to be confirmed.

Setting both DiT `preferred_ready_after_request` declarations to `False` did not eliminate the failure. This does not disable every request-end preference: text encoding has its own preference, and the manager has a fallback when there are no explicitly preferred uses.

On September 21, 2026, source inspection of upstream `main` still showed the warmup/preferred reload branch and the single-pass request-end loop:

- [Component offload strategies](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/memory_managers/component_residency_strategies.py)
- [Component residency manager](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/managers/memory_managers/component_manager.py)

The CUDA failure is reproduced on the latest release, v0.5.20 (`94602c9c2b7cbdb8efd5c52802dac6a1c180089e`).

Could request-end preloading be made memory-aware, with an option to leave component-offloaded modules on the CPU after warmup? Releasing unneeded components before any optional preload would address ordering, but the total preferred set would also need to fit the budget. Cleanup after a failed preload should leave the pipeline usable.

Related work found during our search: #37918 and #36703 concern residency planning, but we have not verified that either resolves this case. #34772 concerns CPU-offload decisions being lost during component loading, which appears to be a different failure stage.

## Reproduction

Run on a single NVIDIA L20:

```bash
sglang serve \
  --model-path /path/to/Wan2.2-T2V-A14B-Diffusers \
  --component-residency \
    dit=component-offload \
    text_encoder=component-offload \
    vae=component-offload
```

Model: `Wan-AI/Wan2.2-T2V-A14B-Diffusers`. In this command, `sglang serve` selects `warmup_mode=server`; FSDP and torch compilation are disabled.

1. Start the server and observe the synthetic warmup failure above. No external generation request is needed to trigger this first OOM.
2. As a comparison, restart with `--warmup-mode off` and otherwise identical settings. The model and worker initialize successfully and the server reaches `Application startup complete` without OOM. No generation request was submitted in this control run.

## Environment

The reproduction uses one NVIDIA L20. The failing process reports 44.39 GiB total device capacity.

```text

git describe: v0.5.20

CUDA Driver Version: 580.95.05

sglang-kernel: 0.4.7
```
