title: [RFC] Align KV cache events with vLLM's schema so shared consumers have a standard format
body:
### Checklist

- [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

# Motivation

## Summary

#37482 switched KV cache events to tagged msgpack maps, the same encoding vLLM moved to in vllm-project/vllm#42892. The fields both engines have use the same names. A consumer however can't treat events from both engines in a standard fashion because of the following:

1. Replay responses are missing the topic frame vLLM added in vllm-project/vllm#45177.
2. There's no `lora_name` in SGLang events. vLLM always sends it and its msgspec types reject events without it.
3. The salt is in a `cache_salt` field in SGLang. vLLM puts it in `extra_keys` on block 0 which is where a consumer like llm-d looks for it.
4. Event hashes leave out `extra_key` in SGLang, so LoRA and base model blocks with the same tokens share a hash.

This RFC proposes fixing those four in SGLang's native format in three phases to align with vLLM for standardization. It doesn't propose a vLLM hash mode or a format flag. Consumers like llm-d don't need vLLM's hash recipe and the in-repo router depends on SGLang's.

## Background

### What already matches

| Area | SGLang and vLLM |
|---|---|
| Event encoding | Tagged maps, class name under `type`, `None` optionals omitted |
| Batch | Positional `[ts, events, dp_rank]` |
| Live frames | `(topic, seq, payload)` |
| `BlockStored` fields | `block_hashes`, `parent_block_hash`, `token_ids`, `block_size`, `lora_id`, `medium`, `session_id` |
| `BlockRemoved`, `AllBlocksCleared` | Same, apart from vLLM's optional `group_idx` |

### Consumers checked

| Consumer | How it reads SGLang events |
|---|---|
| llm-d `engineType: sglang` | Positional arrays only. It can't read anything since #37482. That's llm-d's to fix |
| llm-d `engineType: vllm` | Reads SGLang's maps today. Derives its own block keys from `token_ids`, `lora_name` and `extra_keys` and uses engine hashes only as opaque keys |
| `experimental/sgl-router` | Decodes SGLang maps and ignores unknown keys. Recomputes SGLang's hash recipe on the request side (`kv_events/hash.rs`). Decodes hashes as `i64`. Maps `medium` strings to tiers |
| sgl-router replay client (#32729, open) | Parses today's two frame replay reply |
| vLLM's msgspec types | Fail on SGLang events (see below) |

Dynamo wasn't checked.

## Gaps

### 1. Replay replies have no topic frame

| | Replayed batch | End marker |
|---|---|---|
| vLLM | `(client_id, b"", topic, seq, payload)` | `(client_id, b"", b"", END_SEQ, b"")` |
| SGLang (`kv_events.py:541,546`) | `(client_id, b"", seq, payload)` | `(client_id, b"", END_SEQ, b"")` |

llm-d's replay client requires three frames after the delimiter (`parseEventFrame` in `pkg/kvevents/zmq_subscriber.go`). From reading that code: with `replaySocketPort` set for an SGLang pool, every replay
is rejected as malformed and the pod's index entries are cleared. Live batches that arrive before a successful replay are dropped and the retry 30 seconds later fails the same way, so the pod never gets indexed.

### 2. No `lora_name`

vLLM declares `lora_id`, `medium` and `lora_name` without defaults, so all three are always on the wire. Decoding a SGLang batch with vLLM's struct definitions (copied from `vllm/distributed/kv_events.py` at `de24e51908`) fails:

```
msgspec.ValidationError: Object missing required field `lora_name` - at `$[1][0]`
```

The reverse direction works. llm-d also uses `lora_name` as the model name when it derives keys, so SGLang LoRA blocks are indexed as base model blocks.

### 3. The salt isn't in `extra_keys`

vLLM sends one `extra_keys` entry per block: LoRA name, multimodal identifiers, then `cache_salt` only on the block starting at token 0. llm-d reads the salt only from there. Its precise prefix cache README says salted SGLang requests "are precise-cache misses until SGLang emits `extra_keys`". Unsalted requests can also score hits against salted only copies. SGLang still isolates the cache, so this costs routing quality, not safety.

A side note that corrects the earlier #27682 discussion: vLLM's hashes are salt namespaced too because the salt in block 0's extra keys is part of the hash. Neither engine has `BlockRemoved` ambiguity across salts.

### 4. Event hashes leave out `extra_key`

`compute_node_event_hash_values` (`mem_cache/utils.py:178`) seeds the chain with the salt only. `Req` folds the LoRA uuid into `extra_key` (`schedule_batch.py:1096-1099`). So from reading the code, a LoRA block and a base model block with the same tokens emit the same hash and a `BlockRemoved` for one looks like a removal of both. Storage hashes already include the namespace (`storage_namespace_seed`, `utils.py:125`). vLLM includes the LoRA name in its block hash.

## Proposal

### Phase 1: additive fields, no consumer breaks

**1a. `lora_name`, with `medium` required.** Use vLLM's field order:

```python
class BlockStored(KVCacheEvent):
    block_hashes: list[int]
    parent_block_hash: Optional[int]
    token_ids: list[int]
    block_size: int
    lora_id: Optional[int]
    medium: Optional[str]
    lora_name: Optional[str]
    extra_keys: Optional[list[Optional[tuple]]] = None
    cache_salt: Optional[str] = None
    session_id: Optional[str] = None


class BlockRemoved(KVCacheEvent):
    block_hashes: list[int]
    medium: Optional[str]
```

msgspec needs `medium` to lose its default so that `lora_name` is always sent. Every constructor already passes `medium`. `lora_name` stays `null` until phase 3. `lora_id` stays `null` because vLLM's is a deprecated int and SGLang's is a uuid string.

**1b. `extra_keys` with the salt.** When a node's parent is the root (its first page starts at token 0) and `cache_salt` is set, send `extra_keys=[(salt,), None, ...]` lined up with `block_hashes`. `KVCacheEventRecorder.enqueue` merges parent linked stores and would extend `extra_keys` the same way. The Rust tree core's tagged tuple (`rust_tree_core/adapter.py:85`) needs the field too. Keep `cache_salt`. It's documented and vLLM decoders ignore it.

Effect: vLLM typed decoders read SGLang and llm-d routes salted SGLang traffic correctly. sgl-router ignores both keys.

### Phase 2: replay topic frame

Send `self._topic_bytes` before the sequence number in replay replies and `b""` before `END_SEQ`. That's the vLLM layout.

Replay clients should accept both layouts: two frames after the delimiter is `[seq, payload]`, three is
`[topic, seq, payload]`. Then a new router works with old and new workers. Neither in-repo client has shipped: #32729 is open and #39610's example is open. So they can take the dual parse before this lands and only external clients written against the two frame layout would break.

### Phase 3: LoRA name and namespaced event hashes

These two go together. Adding `lora_name` without the hash change would give llm-d two keys for one engine hash.

**3a.** Carry the adapter name to the tree node, either as a `RadixKey` field or through a lookup in the scheduler's LoRA manager. Fill `lora_name`. With LoRA, put the name first in each `extra_keys` entry, as vLLM does.

**3b.** When `extra_key` is set, seed event hashes with the full namespace, the same way storage hashes do. Keep the current `sglang-cache-salt-v1` seed when only a salt is set, so salted hashes don't change. Mirror it in the Rust tree core.

**sgl-router cost:** its request side hash has no namespace. Today LoRA requests match base model blocks which can't be reused anyway. After 3b they match nothing until the router hashes with the namespace. That's a follow-up in `kv_events/hash.rs`.

### Not proposed

- **Renaming `CPU_PINNED` to `CPU`.** llm-d weights unknown tier names like GPU, so `cpu_pinned` scores 1.0 instead of 0.8. But sgl-router drops stores whose `medium` it doesn't know (`Tiers::for_store`, `kv_events/tree.rs`), so a  rename would turn off host-tier routing on older routers. llm-d users can set `kvCacheBackendConfigs: [{name: cpu_pinned, weight: 0.8}]` instead. See open question 1.
- **Unsigned hashes.** vLLM sends unsigned 64-bit and SGLang sends signed. llm-d accepts both (llm-d-router#2601 widens that). sgl-router decodes `i64`, so flipping would break it.
- **A vLLM hash recipe or `--kv-events-format vllm`.** llm-d doesn't recompute engine hashes and sgl-router depends on SGLang's recipe. Two formats would be a second thing to test with no consumer asking for it.
- **`group_idx` / `kv_cache_spec_kind`.** llm-d indexes events without `group_idx` as-is. Sending `group_idx` without a kind would make llm-d skip every store.

## Compatibility

| Change | vLLM-typed decoders | llm-d `vllm` adapter | sgl-router (main) | sgl-router replay (#32729) | #39610 docs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1a `lora_name`, required `medium` | Fixed | No change until phase 3 | Ignored | n/a | Add field |
| 1b `extra_keys` salt | Reads it | Salted routing fixed | Ignored | n/a | Add field |
| 2 Replay topic frame | n/a | Replay works | n/a | Needs dual parse | Update example |
| 3a `lora_name` filled | Reads it | LoRA indexed under adapter name | Ignored | n/a | Update |
| 3b Namespaced hashes | n/a | `BlockRemoved` unambiguous | LoRA misses until router follow-up | n/a | Note |

## Out of scope

- **Multimodal.** SGLang replaces image tokens with hash derived pad values, so `token_ids` differ from vLLM's placeholders. `extra_keys` can't fix that.
- **EAGLE bigram `token_ids`.** Tracked separately.
- **Pages smaller than llm-d's block size** (llm-d-router#2235).
- **A removal reason on `BlockRemoved`** (#39604). It's additive but it would be worth proposing to vLLM too so the schemas don't drift again.

## Open questions

1. **Tier names.** Keep `CPU_PINNED` and document the llm-d weight? Or have sgl-router accept `CPU` first and switch the engine a release later?
2. **LoRA name source.** A `RadixKey` field which also needs the Rust core or a scheduler side lookup?
3. **LoRA in `extra_keys`.** llm-d's `ParseRawExtraKeys` reads bare strings as multimodal hashes which looks like it would fold a vLLM `lora_name` into keys the request side never adds. That isn't verified. Should SGLang match vLLM anyway or wait until llm-d settles it?
4. **Snapshots.** Should snapshot payloads from #33394 / #34407 use the same event schema?

title: [Bug] GLM-5.3-Flash vision silently broken on main: pinned transformers==5.12.1 lacks glm5_next, AutoProcessor degrades to TokenizersBackend
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution. (Related: #19048, #36507, #37320 — none cover this exact failure.)
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version (`0.0.0.dev1+gc9a8fba99`, nightly image `20260916`).
- [x] Environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are included below.

### Describe the bug

Serving `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` from a recent `main` build starts successfully and `/model_info` reports `"has_image_understanding": true`, but **every image is silently reduced to exactly 3 tokens** (`<|begin_of_image|>` + 1×`<|image|>` + `<|end_of_image|>`), regardless of resolution or content. The `<|image|>` placeholder is never expanded into visual tokens and no `pixel_values` / `image_grid_thw` are produced, so the model answers from hallucination (e.g., describing a "person wearing a bright yellow jacket" when shown a solid red image). Text-only serving is unaffected. Reproduces via both `/v1/chat/completions` and the native `/generate`.

**Root cause (verified in-container):** the deployment pins `transformers==5.12.1` (per `python/pyproject.toml`), and the transformers **v5.12.1 release does not contain the `glm5_next` module** — it currently only exists on transformers `main`. On 5.12.1, `AutoProcessor.from_pretrained("zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash", trust_remote_code=True)` **silently returns a `TokenizersBackend`** (a bare tokenizer) instead of raising. SGLang then starts with a tokenizer as the multimodal processor: image *loading* still runs (a corrupt base64 payload correctly returns HTTP 400), but nothing expands placeholders or encodes pixels.

This presumably affects everyone deploying GLM-5.3-Flash from main-derived builds right now. The day-0 `lmsysorg/sglang:glm-5.3-flash` image was built from the #36507 branch with a transformers main snapshot, which is why vision works there.

### Reproduction

Launch (H200 TP8/EP8; shown with secrets redacted):

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --trust-remote-code \
  --tp-size 8 --ep-size 8 \
  --reasoning-parser glm45 --tool-call-parser glm47 \
  --dsa-prefill-backend tilelang --dsa-decode-backend tilelang \
  --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 5 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6
```

1. **Server-level probe** — `POST /v1/chat/completions` with a `data:image/png;base64,...` image and `temperature: 0`:

   | Request | Expected | Actual |
   |---|---|---|
   | text only (`"Hi"`) | — | `prompt_tokens=13` |
   | + one 256×256 image | ~100+ more tokens | `prompt_tokens=16` (**+3 per image**) |
   | + three 256×256 images | — | `prompt_tokens=22` |

   Answers are hallucinated: solid-red → "Yellow", white square on black → "Triangle", and two *different* images (RGB vs RGBA) yield byte-identical responses.

2. **Framework-level root-cause check** (inside the server container):

   ```python
   import transformers  # 5.12.1
   from transformers import AutoProcessor
   from PIL import Image
   p = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained("zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash", trust_remote_code=True)
   print(type(p).__name__)                    # TokenizersBackend  <- silent degradation
   out = p(images=[Image.new("RGB", (256, 256))], text="hi", return_tensors="pt")
   print(sorted(out.keys()))                  # ['attention_mask', 'input_ids']  (no pixel_values / image_grid_thw)
   ```

3. **Verified workaround**: install a transformers main snapshot (we used `5.18.0.dev0 @ 22e88feb58affcdd70514db734409c0af8cfa3ed`):

   ```dockerfile
   FROM lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260916-c9a8fba9
   RUN /opt/sglang/bin/pip install --no-cache-dir \
       "transformers @ https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/archive/22e88feb58affcdd70514db734409c0af8cfa3ed.tar.gz"
   ```

   With it, `AutoProcessor` resolves to `Glm5NextProcessor`, a 256×256 image expands to **100 tokens** (grid `1×20×20`, with `pixel_values` / `image_grid_thw` / `mm_token_type_ids`), and the same probes answer correctly: solid-red → "Red", white square → "Square", RGBA red → "Salmon" (alpha composited correctly — thanks for #37320).

   Caveat we hit: transformers `main` currently requires `tokenizers>=0.23.1` while SGLang pins `tokenizers==0.22.2`; we overrode the pin locally and re-validated this workload end-to-end (tokenizer round-trip, chat template, glm45/glm47 parsers, EAGLE speculative serving), but mention it in case the pin is load-bearing elsewhere.

### Suggestions

None of these are blockers for us anymore, but they would save the next deployer a confusing afternoon:

1. Bump the `transformers` pin once a release includes `glm5_next`, or document the required snapshot for GLM-5.3-Flash serving.
2. **Fail loudly (or at least warn) at startup when a multimodal architecture resolves its processor to a bare `PreTrainedTokenizerBase`** — silent degradation turns a packaging/dependency gap into wrong answers at runtime.
3. Optionally, a tiny multimodal smoke test for GLM-5.3-Flash that asserts per-image token expansion (`prompt_tokens` grows by the grid size, not by 3).

Happy to validate any fix on our H200 setup, and thank you for the GLM-5.3-Flash support work in #36507 and the follow-ups — everything else in this build (DSA tilelang paths, deep_gemm KPool fusion, MTP, the glm45/glm47 parsers) has been solid.

### Environment

Output of `python3 -m sglang.check_env` run inside the **unmodified** nightly image (the buggy environment; H200, GPU 1 shown):

```
Python: 3.12.3
CUDA available: True
GPU 0: NVIDIA H200 (Compute Capability 9.0)
CUDA: 13.0 / Driver 565.57.01
PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130
sglang: 0.0.0.dev1+gc9a8fba99
sgl-kernel: 0.4.7
flashinfer_python: 0.6.18
triton: 3.7.1
transformers: 5.12.1          <-- root cause
tokenizers: 0.22.2 (pinned)
Image: lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260916-c9a8fba9
Deployment: docker compose, 8x H200, TP8/EP8, unified serving
```

title: [Roadmap] Unified Hybrid Radix Cache Refactor
body:
Blog: https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2026-08-11-unified-radix-cache/

## Motivation
The current radix cache implementations (RadixCache, MambaRadixCache, SWARadixCache, etc.) share a large amount of logic but are maintained as separate, diverged copies. This leads to code duplication, inconsistent behavior, and high maintenance burden when extending cache functionality to new model types (e.g., hybrid linear models, sliding window attention models).

The goal of this refactor is to unify the hybrid radix cache hierarchy around a common base interface, making it easier to:
- Add new cache variants without duplicating logic
- Ensure consistency across all cache implementations
- Enable future extensions (e.g., HiCache, PD disaggregation, new model architectures)

title: [Bug] Kimi-K3 EP32: severe repetition and accuracy regression with MegaMoE, not observed with DeepEP
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

We observe severe reasoning degeneration when serving Kimi-K3 with MegaMoE on GB300. Switching the Decode backend to DeepEP resolves this behavior in our tests.

Requests initially produce coherent reasoning, then may enter prolonged repetition (hmm, or other words), generate tens of thousands of tokens, and fail to complete the task. This also occurs with approximately 34K input tokens, well below the context limit.

**Observed results**


Decode configuration | DeepSWE score
-- | --
TP8 baseline | 68.14% (77/113)
EP32 + DeepEP | ~65.5%
EP32 + MegaMoE, latest run | 42.48% (48/113)

In the latest MegaMoE run, 57/113 tasks contained long mechanical repetition, versus 0/113 in the TP8 baseline using the same detection rule. All 37 responses exceeding 50K output tokens contained repetitive loops. Some affected tasks eventually passed, so successful completion alone does not indicate normal generation.

### Reproduction

Request settings: temperature=1.0, top_p=0.95, thinking_effort=max.

DeepSWE benchmark case: ofetch-per-origin-circuit-breake__qTK9hR7

Expected: Coherent reasoning and normal task completion, as observed with DeepEP.

Actual: MegaMoE produces excessive reasoning and repetitive loops. We have not identified the underlying cause.

### Environment

**Environment**

- Hardware: NVIDIA GB300, ARM64, CUDA 13.0
- Model: Kimi-K3
- SGLang: internal v0.5.19-based build; also observed with an earlier v0.5.18-based build
- FlashInfer: 0.6.18
- sgl-deep-gemm: 0.1.7, with [DeepGEMM #389](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/pull/389) and [#441](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/pull/441) backported
- PD disaggregation using Mooncake
- Prefill: TP8, trtllm_mla
- Decode: 32 GPUs, EP32, Attention TP4 × DP8, CUDA Graph enabled

Relevant Decode arguments:

```
--disaggregation-mode decode \
--tp-size 32 \
--ep-size 32 \
--dp-size 8 \
--enable-dp-attention \
--enable-dp-lm-head \
--moe-a2a-backend megamoe \
--attention-backend cutedsl_mla \
--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
--mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 \
--disable-radix-cache \
--cuda-graph-backend-decode full \
--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 128 \
--reasoning-parser kimi_k3 \
--tool-call-parser kimi_k3
```

The problem persists with SGLANG_DEEPGEMM_PDL=0. It has also been observed with trtllm_mla and with Triton KDA.

title: [Bug] All schedulers hang in cuModuleLoadData on first EAGLE verify (DSA attention, PD-disagg decode), watchdog timeout
body:
# Issue Body

## Checklist

* [x] I have searched related issues but cannot find the same problem.

* [x] The bug appears on a recent main/nightly build.

## Description

Running a PD-disaggregated **decode** instance with DSA attention + EAGLE speculative decoding (Spec V2), the server starts up normally (weight loading, CUDA graph capture and warmup all complete), but it **hangs forever on the first real decode request**. After `watchdog_timeout=300s` the watchdog fires, dumps py-spy stacks, but does not recover. The process stays hung indefinitely (only `/metrics` keeps responding).

All 8 scheduler processes (DP0~~7 / TP0~~7 / EP0~7) are blocked at the **exact same stack**, inside the CUDA driver's `cuModuleLoadData` while Triton lazily loads the freshly JIT-compiled binary of the `fused_dsa_target_verify_metadata` kernel:

```
Thread (active): "MainThread"
    cuModuleLoadData (libcuda.so.590.48.01)
    loadBinary (cuda_utils.cpython-312-x86_64-linux-gnu.so)
    _init_handles (triton/compiler/compiler.py:466)
    launch_metadata (triton/compiler/compiler.py:482)
    run (triton/runtime/jit.py:743)
    fused_dsa_target_verify_metadata (sglang/kernels/ops/attention/dsa_metadata.py:407)
    _apply_cuda_graph_metadata (dsa_backend.py:1604)
    init_forward_metadata_out_graph (dsa_backend.py:845)
    load_batch (runner/decode_cuda_graph_runner.py:1189)
    eagle_prepare_for_verify (eagle_utils.py:571)
    run_eagle_verify (eagle_worker_common.py:495)
    verify (eagle_worker_v2.py:1464)
    forward_batch_generation (eagle_worker_v2.py:1160)
    run_batch (scheduler.py:3452)
    event_loop_overlap_disagg_decode (decode.py:2273)
```

Note that the stack is already inside `loadBinary`, i.e. the Triton compile itself finished — the hang happens while the driver loads the cubin.

## Observations

1. **Timeline**: server ready at T0 (Application startup complete, CUDA graphs captured). The first decode request arrives via PD transfer (~4 input tokens, `max_new_tokens=8`). All ranks enter the first EAGLE verify and never return. Watchdog fires exactly `watchdog_timeout=300s` later.
2. `fused_dsa_target_verify_metadata` is invoked through `init_forward_metadata_out_graph`, i.e. it runs **outside** the captured CUDA graph. Therefore it is not compiled during CUDA graph capture and is lazily JIT-loaded on the first real request.
3. All 8 ranks hit this lazy load **simultaneously** (DP attention: only DP1 has a real batch, other ranks run with empty batches but still participate in the forward), and all of them deadlock inside `cuModuleLoadData`.
4. No NCCL errors, no OOM, no Python exception anywhere in the log.

## Questions / Hypotheses

* Should this out-of-graph DSA metadata kernel be warmed up at startup (like the other kernels touched during CUDA graph capture) so the first request doesn't trigger a concurrent 8-rank lazy load?

* Or is this a known CUDA driver deadlock on sm\_103 + driver 590.48.01 when multiple contexts concurrently load a newly JIT-compiled module?

## Environment

* GPU: 8x NVIDIA B300 (sm\_103, 148 SMs), single node per instance

* Driver: 590.48.01

* Python 3.12.3, NCCL 2.28.9, FlashInfer 0.6.15.post1

* sglang: **internal fork** of a recent main (feat-mooncache branch, with DSA / mooncache / Spec V2 support; GLM-5.2 release notes era)

* Triton / torch version: (fill in if needed)

## Reproduction

1P1D mooncake PD setup: prefill instance on machine A (TP8, DSA context parallel), decode instance on machine B (the one that hangs), sglang router in `--pd-disaggregation` mode.

Key environment variables (decode side):

```bash
export SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2=1          # note: this build logs it as removed/always-on
export SGLANG_MOONCAKE_CUSTOM_MEM_POOL=True
export SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2=1
export SGLANG_LOG_GC=1
export SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_QUEUE_SIZE=8
export SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_THREAD_POOL_SIZE=16
export NCCL_IB_HCA=mlx5_0,mlx5_5,mlx5_8,mlx5_9,mlx5_10,mlx5_11,mlx5_14,mlx5_15
export NCCL_LAUNCH_ORDER_IMPLICIT=1
export SGLANG_ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM=1
```

Launch command (decode side, D0):

```bash
numactl --cpunodebind=0,1,2,3 --membind=0,1,2,3 \
    env CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 \
        MOONCAKE_DEVICE=mlx5_0,mlx5_5,mlx5_8,mlx5_9,mlx5_10,mlx5_11,mlx5_14,mlx5_15 \
        SGLANG_ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM=1 \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path /modules/GLM-5.2-FP8 \
    --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30001 \
    --log-level debug \
    --disaggregation-mode decode \
    --disaggregation-transfer-backend mooncake \
    --disaggregation-bootstrap-port 50030 \
    --disaggregation-ib-device mlx5_0,mlx5_5,mlx5_8,mlx5_9,mlx5_10,mlx5_11,mlx5_14,mlx5_15 \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --dist-init-addr 127.0.0.1:5501 \
    --nnodes 1 \
    --tp-size 8 --dp-size 8 --ep-size 8 \
    --enable-dp-attention --enable-dp-lm-head \
    --moe-dense-tp-size 1 \
```

title: [Bug] DSV v4.1 Flash 2x4 H200 TP8/EP8 + DSPARK causes startup deadlock after DSpark draft weight load on dev-cu13-dsv41 and latest dev-cu13 image
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

Serving `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` with `--speculative-algorithm DSPARK` on **2 nodes × 4 H200 (TP8 + EP8, LeaderWorkerSet, one 4-GPU pod per node over RoCE)** deterministically deadlocks during startup, right after the DSpark draft weights finish loading. Three consecutive attempts across two different images all hang at the same point with the same split stack; removing the DSPARK flags (identical everything else) starts cleanly in ~10 minutes.

**The split we capture on every occurrence (py-spy dump, all 8 scheduler processes):**

Node 0 schedulers (leader, TP0-3) — parked after `Load weight end ... type=DeepseekV4ForCausalLMDSpark`:

```
monitored_barrier (torch/distributed/distributed_c10d.py:5435)
dist_barrier_after_load (model_runner_components/load_model_utils.py:380)   # also seen :344 on dev-cu13
load_model (model_runner.py:1307)
initialize (model_runner.py:653)
```

Node 1 schedulers (worker, TP4-7) — parked earlier, inside the KV-pool memory probe:

```
all_reduce (torch/distributed/distributed_c10d.py:3252)
wrapper (torch/distributed/c10d_logger.py:83)
get_available_gpu_memory (utils/common.py:550)
_profile_available_bytes (kv_cache_configurator.py:2214)
```

The worker-side ranks have posted the memory-probe all-reduce and wait for the leader-side ranks, while the leader-side ranks wait at a different synchronization point (post-load barrier). The two node halves sit at mismatched collective sites permanently — GPU utilization 0%, GPU memory and logs frozen from that point on. No watchdog fires (the stall happens before the scheduler loop starts).

This looks like the same unsynchronized-decision family as #39886 (DSpark CUDA-graph memory check not synchronized across ranks → ranks disagree on collective participation) and the runtime variant in #33289 (multi-node TP + DSpark → per-rank divergence → unmatched collectives). Our case adds a multi-node TP8/EP8 startup reproduction with full per-node py-spy stacks.

**Reproduction rate:** 3/3 with DSPARK on 2 nodes (2× `dev-cu13`, 1× `dev-cu13-dsv41`); 0 failures without DSPARK — the identical non-DSPARK cell starts cleanly in ~10 min and served a full benchmark suite.

### Reproduction


### Reproduction

Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`

```bash

  --model-path /.cache/deepseek-v41-flash \

  --chunked-prefill-size 16384 \

  --ep-size 8 \
  --attention-backend dsv4 \
  --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64 \
  --max-prefill-tokens 32768 \
  --enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay \
  --reasoning-parser auto --tool-call-parser auto \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \
  --speculative-dspark-block-size 5
```

(`--node-rank 1` + same `--dist-init-addr` on the second node)

**Failure timeline:**

| Attempt | Image | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13` (digest `sha256:0e1b14e302619…`, built 2026-09-22, commit `582389ce`) | Hangs; last log `Load weight end … DeepseekV4ForCausalLMDSpark`; stacks above; pod restart reproduces it |
| 2 | `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.20-cu130` | Not applicable — V4.1-Flash not supported in the release yet (`unrecognized arguments: --enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay`) |
| 3 | `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-cu13-dsv41` (build commit `da64c5cbb8cf6bfd39be19da43573fdfd484c43a`, action run 34631178591) | Same hang, same split stacks |

**Control:** same image + same flags **without** `--speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-dspark-block-size 5` starts cleanly (health 200, ~10 min).

title: [Bug] `qwen3_coder` non-streaming parser drops visible text after a valid tool call
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

## Description

The `qwen3_coder` parser returns different visible content for the same complete model output depending on whether the request is streamed.

Input model output:

```text
before<tool_call><function=get_weather><parameter=city>Paris</parameter></function></tool_call>after
```

Non-streaming returns `content="before"`. Character-by-character streaming returns `content="beforeafter"`. Both paths parse the same valid `get_weather` tool call.

### Reproduction

## Reproduction

Tested with SGLang 0.5.20 using [repro_qwen3_coder.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32513779/repro_qwen3_coder.py):

```bash
python repro.py
```

The script exits with status 1 when the bug is reproduced. See `repro.log` for the captured output.

## Expected behavior

Streaming and non-streaming parsing of the same complete output should preserve the same visible content and tool call. Here, both should return `content="beforeafter"`.

## Root cause

In `sglang/srt/function_call/qwen3_coder_detector.py`, `Qwen3CoderDetector.detect_and_parse()` builds `normal_text` only from `text[:start_idx]`. It parses the tool-call block but never appends text after the closing `</tool_call>`. The streaming state machine continues after the closing marker and emits that tail normally.

title: [Bug] Disconnected streaming client leaves a zombie request that decodes to max_tokens and floods "state was deleted in TokenizerManager" (regression from #34160 revert)
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

> Submitted by GLM-5.3

When a streaming client disconnects mid-generation, the scheduler-side request
is never aborted and keeps decoding until `max_tokens`. Every output batch for
that request logs:

```
Received output for rid='...' but the state was deleted in TokenizerManager.
```

at a high rate (observed ~15 lines/s per request, sustained for the entire
remaining generation — in production two zombie requests burned GPU for 15+
minutes and occupied both `--max-running-requests` slots, blocking all new
requests from being scheduled).

Root cause (verified on current `main`):

1. `TokenizerManager.generate_request` has an `except BaseException` cleanup
   that calls `_discard_pending_req_states(obj)`. It was added for failures
   *before* the request reaches the scheduler (e.g. input-length validation),
   but a client disconnect raises `asyncio.CancelledError` — also a
   `BaseException` — so the state of a request that **is running on the
   scheduler** gets popped immediately at disconnect time.

2. The delayed safety net then doesn't fire: `create_abort_task` (attached to
   the `StreamingResponse` as a background task, runs ~2s after teardown)
   calls `abort_request(rid)`, which early-returns on
   `tokenizer_worker_num == 1 and rid not in self.rid_to_state`. The
   `AbortReq` is never dispatched, so the scheduler never learns the client
   is gone and decodes to `max_tokens`; each `BatchStrOutput` for that rid
   hits the deleted-state error path.

This is a regression of 71043b9dbb ("Revert parallel request lifecycle
tracking from #32588", #34160). Before the revert, #32588 handled this
correctly: `_discard_pending_req_states(obj, request_lifecycles)` dispatched
`AbortReq` for every rid whose state had `dispatched == True` **before**
removing the state. The revert deleted the `dispatched` markers and the
abort-then-remove ordering, leaving the orphan window. Presumably not covered
by CI because it requires killing a streaming client mid-generation.

(The `HEALTH_CHECK`-prefixed rid skip next to the error log is a different,
known race — unrelated, see #11925.)

Suggested minimal fix (verified in production, restores the pre-revert
invariant without reintroducing full lifecycle tracking):

1. In `generate_request`, treat cancellation separately and only discard
   state if the request was never dispatched:

```python
        dispatched = False
        try:
            ...
            self._send_one_request(tokenized_obj)
            dispatched = True
            async for response in self._wait_one_response(obj, request):
                yield response
        except (asyncio.CancelledError, GeneratorExit):
            # Client disconnect mid-request: keep the state of a dispatched
            # request so the delayed background abort still finds it; the
            # scheduler's abort echo deletes it cleanly. Discarding here
            # orphans the scheduler-side request, which then decodes to
            # max_tokens.
            if not dispatched:
                self._discard_pending_req_states(obj)
            raise
        except BaseException:
            self._discard_pending_req_states(obj)
            raise
```

2. Add a `force` flag to `abort_request` that bypasses the
   `rid not in self.rid_to_state` early-return, and pass `force=True` from
   `create_abort_task` (the scheduler's `abort_request` handler scans by rid
   prefix and no-ops unknown rids, so force-dispatching is safe — it just
   closes the window where the state was already deleted elsewhere):

```python
    def abort_request(self, rid: str = "", abort_all: bool = False, force: bool = False):
        if not abort_all and not rid:
            ...
            return
        if (
            not abort_all
            and not force
            and get_serving().tokenizer_worker_num == 1
            and rid not in self.rid_to_state
        ):
            return
```

With this patch: disconnect → decode stops within the 2s abort window, zero
error lines; normal streaming completions (`[DONE]`) unaffected.

### Reproduction

Any model; the bug is in the tokenizer-manager layer and is
hardware/model-independent.

1. Launch a server:

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server --model <any-model> --port 30000
```

2. Start a long streaming generation, then kill the client mid-stream:

```bash
curl -sN http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"<any-model>","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Count from 1 to 5000, one number per line."}],"max_tokens":16000,"stream":true}' &
sleep 10 && kill -9 %1
```

**Actual**: `sglang:num_running_reqs` stays 1 and the request decodes until
`max_tokens`; the log floods with the message above (same rid, repeated many
times per second).

**Expected**: the request is aborted shortly after the disconnect (within the
2s background-abort window) and decode stops.

### Environment

- sglang `main` (regression introduced by 71043b9dbb / #34160, still present
  as of a1f9508dd4; no commit has touched `tokenizer_manager.py` since —
  `except BaseException` cleanup and the guard are at current lines ~825
  and ~1952)
- single GPU, TP=1, `--max-running-requests 2`; speculative decoding enabled
  (DSPARK) on our instance, but nothing here is spec-specific
- reproduced and root-caused on a fork whose `tokenizer_manager.py` is
  unmodified upstream code

title: [Bug] MiniMax-M3 incorrectly routes Ascend FuseEP through the normal MoE path
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.

- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

In [`minimax_m3.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/models/minimax_m3.py), `MiniMaxM3MoE` checks only `is_deepep()` and omits `is_ascend_fuseep()` across its MoE forward dispatch and initialization logic.

When running MiniMax-M3 on Ascend NPU with `--moe-a2a-backend ascend_fuseep` and tensor parallelism (`--tp > 1`):
1. **Spurious TP all-reduce on globally combined output**: `MiniMaxM3MoE.forward()` falls through to `forward_normal()`. Inside `forward_normal()`, `FusedMoE.forward()` detects `_use_ascend_fuseep` and invokes `forward_fuseep()`, running `buf.fused_deep_moe(...)` across the EP/TP group. This means the routed MoE output is **already globally gathered across all ranks**. However, `forward_normal()` subsequently executes `tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce(final_hidden_states)`, multiplying routed activations by `tp_size` (e.g., 8× on TP=8) at every MoE layer.
2. **Broken shared expert partitioning**: Shared experts are configured with TP sharding instead of being replicated (`tp_size=1`). Because FuseEP does not perform an un-sharded layer all-reduce, this leaves an unreduced partial shared MLP output added directly to the combined routed output.
3. **Unset layer attributes**: `self.ep_size` and `self.top_k` are never initialized on the layer under `ascend_fuseep`.

### Expected behavior

When `--moe-a2a-backend ascend_fuseep` is used, `MiniMaxM3MoE` should:
- Route through `forward_deepep()`, bypassing the redundant `tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce`.
- Set `shared_experts_tp1 = True` so shared MLP weights are replicated (`tp_size=1`).
- Initialize `self.ep_size = get_parallel().moe_ep_size` and `self.top_k = config.num_experts_per_tok`.

### Code Trace and Invariant Violation

All three affected sites are in [`python/sglang/srt/models/minimax_m3.py`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/models/minimax_m3.py):

#### 1. Forward dispatch ([minimax_m3.py#L428-L440](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/models/minimax_m3.py#L428-L440))
```python
def forward(self, hidden_states, forward_batch, ...):
    if get_moe_a2a_backend().is_deepep():
        return self.forward_deepep(hidden_states, forward_batch)
    else:
        # ascend_fuseep enters here:
        return self.forward_normal(hidden_states, should_allreduce_fusion, use_reduce_scatter)
```
Inside `forward_normal` ([lines 466–471](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/models/minimax_m3.py#L466-L471)):
```python
# FusedMoE.forward -> forward_fuseep -> buf.fused_deep_moe (all-to-all communication across EP ranks)
final_hidden_states = self._forward_router_experts(hidden_states)

# Redundant all-reduce on already-combined tensor:
if self.tp_size > 1 and not should_allreduce_fusion and not use_reduce_scatter:
    final_hidden_states = tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce(final_hidden_states)
```

#### 2. Shared experts replication ([minimax_m3.py#L391-L403](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/models/minimax_m3.py#L391-L403))
```python
# DeepEP and FuseEP all-gather the layer output, so shared MLP must be replicated (tp_size=1)
shared_experts_tp1 = get_moe_a2a_backend().is_deepep()  # Evaluates to False for ascend_fuseep
self.shared_experts = MiniMaxM3MLP(
    ...,
    **(dict(tp_rank=0, tp_size=1) if shared_experts_tp1 else {}),
)
```

#### 3. EP metadata initialization ([minimax_m3.py#L419-L421](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/models/minimax_m3.py#L419-L421))
```python
if get_moe_a2a_backend().is_deepep():  # Evaluates to False for ascend_fuseep
    self.ep_size = get_parallel().moe_ep_size
    self.top_k = config.num_experts_per_tok
```

---

### Comparison with other models

Every other MoE model in SGLang supporting `ascend_fuseep` guards both backends consistently:

| Model | Guard | Location |
|---|---|---|
| **MiniMax-M2** | `not is_deepep() and not is_ascend_fuseep()` | [`minimax_m2.py#L583-L584`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/models/minimax_m2.py#L583-L584) |
| **DeepSeek-V2** | `is_deepep() or is_ascend_fuseep() or ...` | [`deepseek_v2.py#L845-L867`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v2.py#L845-L867) |
| **GLM-4 MoE** | `is_deepep() or is_ascend_fuseep()` | [`glm4_moe.py#L505, L572`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/models/glm4_moe.py#L505) |
| **Step-3.5** | `not is_deepep() and not is_ascend_fuseep()` | [`step3p5.py#L185`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/models/step3p5.py#L185) |
| **SDAR MoE** | `not is_deepep() and not is_ascend_fuseep()` | [`sdar_moe.py#L131`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/models/sdar_moe.py#L131) |
| **MiMo-V2** | `is_deepep() or is_ascend_fuseep()` | [`mimo_v2.py#L450, L469`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/models/mimo_v2.py#L450) |

## Reproduction

Target server launch command:
```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path MiniMax/MiniMax-M3 \
  --tp 8 \
  --moe-a2a-backend ascend_fuseep \
  --trust-remote-code
```

Tracing the forward pass confirms:
1. `get_moe_a2a_backend().is_deepep()` evaluates to `False`.
2. Execution branches into `forward_normal()`.
3. `tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce` runs at line 471 on activations that were already globally combined via `buf.fused_deep_moe(...)`.

---

## Proposed Fix

Add `or get_moe_a2a_backend().is_ascend_fuseep()` alongside `is_deepep()` in all three locations in `MiniMaxM3MoE`:

```diff
diff --git a/python/sglang/srt/models/minimax_m3.py b/python/sglang/srt/models/minimax_m3.py
--- a/python/sglang/srt/models/minimax_m3.py
+++ b/python/sglang/srt/models/minimax_m3.py
@@ -395,1 +395,4 @@
-            shared_experts_tp1 = get_moe_a2a_backend().is_deepep()
+            shared_experts_tp1 = (
+                get_moe_a2a_backend().is_deepep()
+                or get_moe_a2a_backend().is_ascend_fuseep()
+            )
@@ -419,1 +422,4 @@
-        if get_moe_a2a_backend().is_deepep():
+        if (
+            get_moe_a2a_backend().is_deepep()
+            or get_moe_a2a_backend().is_ascend_fuseep()
+        ):
@@ -435,1 +441,4 @@
-        if get_moe_a2a_backend().is_deepep():
+        if (
+            get_moe_a2a_backend().is_deepep()
+            or get_moe_a2a_backend().is_ascend_fuseep()
+        ):
```

## Environment

- SGLang branch: `main` (commit `367e3700cf`)
- Target hardware: Ascend NPU (e.g., 8× Ascend 910B) with `torch_npu`
- Note: Code analysis / architectural bug in `python/sglang/srt/models/minimax_m3.py`.

title: [Bug] PD retract rebootstrap is not pinned to the bound prefill DP rank unless the client supplied disagg_prefill_dp_rank
body:
## Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

## Describe the bug

This is a follow-up to #39357 ("[PD] Preserve the prefill rank during
rebootstrap", `5c2de3f355`), which fixed this for one deployment shape but not
for the general one.

When a PD decode worker performs a **true retraction**, the request's prefix KV
is gone and decode asks the prefill side to recompute it by POSTing
`Req.build_rebootstrap_payload()` to the prefill `/generate`
(`CommonKVManager.submit_prefill_recompute` /
`_run_prefill_recompute`, `python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/common/conn.py:792`
and `:859`). The decode-side KV receiver for that request is **not** rebuilt --
it stays bootstrapped against the prefill DP rank it was bound to.

#39357 added to the payload (`python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:2074`,
on `main` at `3f00fb7e2e`):

```python
"routed_dp_rank": self.disagg_prefill_dp_rank,
"disagg_prefill_dp_rank": self.disagg_prefill_dp_rank,
```

`Req.disagg_prefill_dp_rank` (`schedule_batch.py:1340`) is only ever the
client- or router-supplied hint from the original `/generate`. In every
deployment where the caller does not pin the prefill DP itself, it is `None`,
so the recompute request carries `routed_dp_rank: null`,
`DataParallelController.maybe_external_dp_rank_routing`
(`python/sglang/srt/managers/data_parallel_controller.py:752`) returns `False`,
and the recompute is dispatched by the prefill's normal load balancer.

### Why the rank matters

`CommonKVReceiver.init(prefill_dp_rank)`
(`python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/common/conn.py:1697`) is not a hint, it is a
binding:

- `_setup_bootstrap_infos` keys the connection pool by
  `f"{bootstrap_addr}_{prefill_dp_rank}_{cp_rank}_{tp_rank}"` and fetches the
  bootstrap info of exactly that prefill DP rank's TP/PP/CP ranks
  (`conn.py:1738-1767`);
- it then calls `_register_kv_args()` (`conn.py:1787`), which registers this
  decode rank's kv_args with **those** prefill ranks only.

Nothing re-resolves the rank after `init`, and the rebootstrap path
deliberately reuses the existing receiver.

So if the recompute lands on a different prefill DP rank, that DP's
`CommonKVSender` bootstraps for the room but finds no decode side registered
for it, while the bound decode receiver waits for a transfer that is never
started. Both sides only unblock on their timeouts
(`SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT` on prefill,
`SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_WAITING_TIMEOUT` on decode, both 300 s by default), after
which the decode side records
`Request <room> timed out after <N>s in KVPoll.WaitingForInput`
(`conn.py:1946`) and the request fails. With the defaults, that is a 5 minute
stall followed by a failed request.

There is a second, quieter effect. Because the recompute carries no
`disagg_prefill_dp_rank` either, the wrongly-routed prefill's `CommonKVSender`
takes the `_register_prefill_dp_rank()` branch (`conn.py:1507-1509`) and
overwrites the bootstrap server's `bootstrap_room -> dp_rank` entry with its own
rank, so the table no longer reflects the DP the decode receiver is bound to.

### Which routing configurations are affected

Decode resolves the prefill DP rank in `DecodePreallocQueue._resolve_prefill_dp_rank`
(`python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/decode.py:749`):

| decode resolves the rank via | prefill `--load-balance-method` | recompute routing today | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `req.disagg_prefill_dp_rank` (client/router hint) | any | pinned by #39357 | OK |
| `dp_size == 1` | any | single DP | OK |
| `bootstrap_room % dp_size` (`follow_bootstrap_room`) | `follow_bootstrap_room` | `follow_bootstrap_room_scheduler` recomputes `bootstrap_room % len(workers)` from the same room (`data_parallel_controller.py:788`) | OK by coincidence |
| `CommonKVReceiver.query_prefill_dp_ranks` against the bootstrap server (slow path, `decode.py:1118-1151`) | `round_robin`, `total_requests`, `total_tokens` | round-robin / load-aware, unrelated to the bound rank | **broken** |
| `query_prefill_dp_ranks` with `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_FORCE_QUERY_PREFILL_DP_RANK=1` | any, including mixed routing | not pinned | **broken** |

The reason this was not caught is the third row: with `--load-balance-method
auto` a PD **prefill** server defaults to `follow_bootstrap_room`
(`python/sglang/srt/arg_groups/serving_hook.py:200-211`), and there the DP
controller happens to re-derive the same rank from the unchanged
`bootstrap_room`. As soon as the prefill DP routing is load-aware -- which is
the point of running `--load-balance-method total_tokens` or `total_requests`
on prefill -- decode has to go through the bootstrap-server query, the resolved
rank has nothing to do with `bootstrap_room % dp_size`, and the pin is lost.

### How to reach the rebootstrap path

Three triggers exist on `main`:

1. `/pause_generation` with `mode: "retract"`. `Scheduler.pause_generation`
   (`python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py:5571`) retracts everything and,
   for `DisaggregationMode.DECODE`, sets `pd_rebootstrap_in_progress` and calls
   `disagg_decode_prealloc_queue.hold_rebootstrap(req)`
   (`scheduler.py:5627-5633`). This is the path an RL weight-sync pause takes,
   and it is available on any PD decode deployment.
2. A KV-pressure retraction on a pool that cannot back its KV up, i.e.
   `dsv41_dspark_needs_rebootstrap` (`python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/decode.py:694`).
3. The same path as 2, forced without memory pressure through the retraction
   fault injection `SGLANG_TEST_RETRACT=1` / `SGLANG_TEST_RETRACT_INTERVAL=N`
   on the decode server (`scheduler.py:4177-4179`).

## Reproduction

1P(dp>1)D, with the prefill DP routing made load-aware so decode has to resolve
the rank through the bootstrap server rather than from `bootstrap_room`:

Prefill (note `--load-balance-method total_tokens`; `round_robin` or
`total_requests` behave the same):

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path /path/to/model \
    --port 8000 --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --tp-size 8 --dp-size 4 --enable-dp-attention \
    --load-balance-method total_tokens \
    --disaggregation-mode prefill \
    --disaggregation-ib-device mlx5_0
```

Decode:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path /path/to/model \
    --port 8001 --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --tp-size 8 --dp-size 4 --enable-dp-attention \
    --disaggregation-mode decode \
    --disaggregation-ib-device mlx5_0
```

Then, with long-running generations in flight through the router, force a true
retraction:

```bash
curl -X POST http://<decode-host>:8001/pause_generation -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"mode": "retract"}'
curl -X POST http://<decode-host>:8001/continue_generation
```

Observed: the retracted requests do not resume. After
`SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_WAITING_TIMEOUT` (300 s) the decode log shows
`Some requests fail to receive KV Cache transfer done signal after bootstrapping`
and `Request <bootstrap_room> timed out after ~300.0s in KVPoll.WaitingForInput`,
and the requests fail. The prefill DP that received the recompute shows the
request bootstrapping and then timing out with no decode peer.

Expected: the recompute is dispatched to the prefill DP rank the decode
receiver is already bound to, and the request resumes.

Setting `--load-balance-method follow_bootstrap_room` on prefill (or passing
`disagg_prefill_dp_rank` on every request) makes it work again, which isolates
the missing pin as the cause.

Note: with `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_FORCE_QUERY_PREFILL_DP_RANK=1` on decode the
same failure appears even with `follow_bootstrap_room` prefill routing.

We first saw this on a v0.5.17-based 2P2D deployment (prefill and decode both
dp=4) with true retractions forced on the decode workers via
`SGLANG_TEST_RETRACT=1`: 53 of 100 recomputes in one run stalled this way until
the KV waiting timeout, and the other 47 happened to land on the DP the receiver
was bound to. The analysis above is against `main` at `3f00fb7e2e`; the
experiment itself has not been re-run on current `main`.

title: [Bug] PD decode scheduler crashes with NotImplementedError when retracting a request under --enable-hisparse
body:
## Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

## Describe the bug

A PD **decode** server started with `--enable-hisparse` dies with an uncaught
`NotImplementedError` as soon as the KV pool fills up and the scheduler has to
retract a running decode request. The exception escapes the scheduler event
loop, so the whole decode worker goes down and every in-flight request on it is
lost.

### Where it comes from

All line numbers below are on `main` at `3f00fb7e2e`.

1. `python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py:4190` calls `batch.retract_decode()`
   when decode memory runs out.
2. `ScheduleBatch.retract_decode` (`python/sglang/srt/managers/schedule_batch.py:3248`)
   releases the victim through `self.release_req(idx, len(sorted_indices))` at
   `schedule_batch.py:3285`. That call does **not** pass `offload_kv`, so it
   keeps the default `offload_kv=True` (`schedule_batch.py:3379`).
   (The two abort branches in the same loop, `schedule_batch.py:3282` and
   `:3320`, already pass `offload_kv=False`.)
3. The module-level `release_req` (`schedule_batch.py:2209`) therefore reaches
   `schedule_batch.py:2229`:

   ```python
   if get_disagg().disaggregation_mode == "decode" and offload_kv:
       backup_saved = retraction_backup(..., get_disagg().disaggregation_decode_retraction_backup)
   ```

4. On a HiSparse decode server the backup backend always resolves to
   `cpu_tensor`. `resolve_decode_retraction_backup`
   (`python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/kv_cache_builder.py:188`) only picks
   `host_pool` when the device pool is an `MHATokenToKVPool` or a `SWAKVPool`
   (`kv_cache_builder.py:210-215`); HiSparse uses
   `HiSparseDSATokenToKVPool(DSATokenToKVPool)` -> `MLATokenToKVPool`, so
   `supports_host_pool` is `False`.
5. `retraction_backup` (`python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/common.py:210`) with the
   `cpu_tensor` backend calls `req.offload_kv_cache(...)` at `common.py:225`.
6. `Req.offload_kv_cache` (`schedule_batch.py:1988`) calls
   `token_to_kv_pool_allocator.get_cpu_copy(...)` at `schedule_batch.py:1997`.
7. `HiSparseTokenToKVPoolAllocator`
   (`python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/allocator/hisparse.py:21`) extends
   `BaseTokenToKVPoolAllocator` and does not override `get_cpu_copy`, so the
   call lands on `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/allocator/base.py:223`:

   ```python
   def get_cpu_copy(self, indices, mamba_indices=None, req_pool_index=None):
       raise NotImplementedError()
   ```

   The underlying device pool refuses explicitly for the same reason
   (`python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/hisparse_memory_pool.py:144`:
   `NotImplementedError("HiSparseDevicePool does not support get_cpu_copy")`).

Nothing catches this, so the scheduler process exits.

### Implementing `get_cpu_copy` would not fix it

The ordering inside `release_req` makes a backup taken at that point
meaningless, not just unimplemented. `schedule_batch.py:2220` runs **before**
the backup:

```python
if hisparse_coordinator is not None and not req.finished():
    hisparse_coordinator.retract_req(req)
```

`HiSparseCoordinator.retract_req`
(`python/sglang/srt/managers/hisparse_coordinator.py:942`) dispatches to
`abort_staging_request` or `request_finished`, and `request_finished` frees the
request's HiSparse device buffer indices
(`free_hisparse_indices`), frees its allocated locations, and clears the
full-token -> HiSparse index mapping for that request row. By the time
`retraction_backup` runs at `schedule_batch.py:2229` the request's KV has
already been returned to the allocator, so a `get_cpu_copy` added here would
snapshot freed slots, i.e. it would produce a backup that cannot be trusted to
restore the request.

In other words, a retraction under HiSparse is inherently a *true* retraction:
the prefix KV is gone and has to be recomputed, exactly the situation
`dsv41_dspark_needs_rebootstrap` (`python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/common.py:197`)
already describes for the V4.1 DSPARK pool.

### Related issues

- #33385 reports the same crash shape for the DeepSeek V4 pool. The trigger is
  the same `retraction_backup` -> `get_cpu_copy` path; the pool differs.
- #36591 proposes implementing `get_cpu_copy` for the sparse pool. That would
  remove the `NotImplementedError` but, per the ordering above, the copy would
  run after `hisparse_coordinator.retract_req` has already freed the KV, so the
  request still could not be resumed from it. The retracted request needs to be
  rebootstrapped, not backed up.

### Secondary effect once the exception is gone

Even if the exception is suppressed, a HiSparse retracted request is pushed to
`DecodePreallocQueue.retracted_queue` (`python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/decode.py:709`),
whose resume path (`resume_retracted_reqs` -> `Req.load_kv_cache`) expects a
host backup that does not exist. The existing V4.1 DSPARK branch at
`decode.py:694` converts such requests into a rebootstrap instead; HiSparse
needs the same treatment.

## Reproduction

Any DSA model that supports `--enable-hisparse`, run as a 1P1D pair. Adapted
from `docs/docs/advanced_features/hisparse_guide.mdx`:

Prefill:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path /path/to/model \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --port 8000 --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --context-length 81920 \
    --chunked-prefill-size 65536 \
    --tp-size 8 --dp-size 8 --enable-dp-attention \
    --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
    --disaggregation-mode prefill \
    --disaggregation-ib-device mlx5_0,mlx5_1,mlx5_2,mlx5_3
```

Decode (HiSparse):

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path /path/to/model \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --port 8001 --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --context-length 81920 \
    --tp-size 8 --dp-size 8 --enable-dp-attention \
    --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
    --disable-radix-cache \
    --disaggregation-mode decode \
    --disaggregation-ib-device mlx5_0,mlx5_1,mlx5_2,mlx5_3 \
    --enable-hisparse \
    --hisparse-config='{"top_k": 2048, "device_buffer_size": 6144, "host_to_device_ratio": 10, "swap_in_block_size": 960}'
```

Then drive the pair hard enough that decode has to retract, i.e. long outputs
and a concurrency above what the decode KV pool can hold:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \
    --backend sglang \
    --dataset-name random \
    --random-input 40000 \
    --random-output 20000 \
    --random-range-ratio 1.0 \
    --num-prompts 200 \
    --max-concurrency 200 \
    --request-rate 40 \
    --model /path/to/model \
    --host 127.0.0.1 --port <router-port>
```

The first time the decode scheduler logs `retract_decode` the worker dies with
`NotImplementedError` raised from
`python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/allocator/base.py:223`.

A smaller decode KV pool (lower `--mem-fraction-static` or a lower
`--hisparse-config` `device_buffer_size`) makes it reproduce faster. In
practice HiSparse admission is conservative enough that natural KV pressure
rarely reaches `retract_decode`; the reliable trigger is the built-in
retraction fault injection on the decode server, `SGLANG_TEST_RETRACT=1`
(with `SGLANG_TEST_RETRACT_INTERVAL=N`, `scheduler.py:4177-4179`), which forces
the retract path every N forward steps regardless of memory. The first forced
retraction kills the worker.

We hit this crash on a v0.5.17-based 2P2D PD deployment (prefill and decode
both dp=4) with `SGLANG_TEST_RETRACT=1` on the decode workers: the first forced
retraction took the decode scheduler down with exactly this traceback. The call
chain above is unchanged on current `main`. There is no CPU-only reproducer for
the crash itself, since `--enable-hisparse` requires an accelerator; the two
code properties it depends on -- "the backup path calls `get_cpu_copy`" and
"`retract_req` runs before the backup" -- are both visible by reading the call
chain.

title: [Bug] `input_embeds` requests through `/open_session` crash the scheduler
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

A request that uses `input_embeds` works when sent directly, but the same input crashes SGLang when it is sent through a session created by `/open_session`. This affects both `streaming=true` and `streaming=false`. The client gets a disconnected connection and the server exits.

`input_embeds` requires `--disable-radix-cache`; the server is launched with that documented requirement. Neither startup nor the request reports this combination as unsupported.

### Reproduction

Tested with SGLang 0.5.20 and `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` (hidden size 896)
at revision `7ae557604adf67be50417f59c2c2f167def9a775`.

Start the server:

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \
  --dtype bfloat16 \
  --disable-radix-cache \
  --enable-streaming-session \
  --disable-prefill-cuda-graph \
  --cuda-graph-backend-decode disabled \
  --port 30000
```

Run with the script [repro.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32507829/repro_session_input_embeds.py):

```bash
python repro.py \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000 \
  --hidden-size 896 \
  --session-streaming true
```

The script runs these checks in order:

1. The embedding input without a session returns HTTP 200.
2. An `input_ids` request through `/open_session` returns HTTP 200, and the
   server remains healthy.
3. The same embedding input as the first request of a new session disconnects,
   and the server is no longer reachable.

The result is the same with a non-streaming session:

```bash
python repro.py \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000 \
  --hidden-size 896 \
  --session-streaming false
```

For this second run, the server was restarted without
`--enable-streaming-session`; ordinary sessions do not require that flag. This
rules out the streaming-session wrapper as the cause.

The server log ends with:

```text
File "sglang/srt/session/session_controller.py", line 293, in create_req
    if not abort and len(input_ids) == 0:
TypeError: object of type 'NoneType' has no len()
```

Full log is here: [server_input_session_embeds.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32507857/server_input_session_embeds.log)
Non-streaming also faces the same issue: [server_nonstreaming.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32507917/server_nonstreaming.log)

## Root cause

For a normal embedding-input request, `Scheduler.handle_generate_request()` creates placeholder token IDs from the embedding sequence length and passes `input_embeds` into `Req`. Requests carrying a `/open_session` ID bypass that logic and enter `Session.create_req()` directly. On a first-turn embedding
request, this path sets `input_ids = req.input_ids`, which is `None`, then calls `len(input_ids)`. The later `Req` constructor in this path also does not pass `input_embeds`, so this is not only a missing `None` guard: session request construction does not preserve the embedding input.

title: [Bug] Leaked sgl_shm_mm_* segments fill /dev/shm -> permanent crashloop (load snapshot SIGBUS / NCCL ENOSPC) after a scheduler crash
body:
## Summary

On deployments where `/dev/shm` is a **persistent per-pod volume** (e.g. k8s `emptyDir` with `medium: Memory` mounted at `/dev/shm` — the standard way to give NCCL more than the runtime's tiny default), a **single scheduler crash permanently wedges the pod**: leaked `sgl_shm_mm_*` segments from the crashed run fill the tmpfs, and every subsequent startup dies before serving. Observed fleet-wide on an internal serving fleet (~700 H20 GPUs, TP4 pods): **4 → 101 affected pods in ~30 minutes, none recover without pod deletion**, each cycle producing core dumps.

## The failure chain (all steps observed in production logs)

1. A scheduler dies at runtime (any cause; ours was a CUDA OOM under a traffic burst).
2. During teardown, the tokenizer-side workers keep processing queued multimodal requests. Each `ShmPointerMMData` (from #16402) creates an `sgl_shm_mm_<pid>_<rand>` POSIX segment (~9–300MB each for image/video features). With the scheduler dead, nothing calls `materialize()` → `close_and_unlink()`, and `__del__` explicitly never unlinks ("Unlinking is materialize()'s job"). Observed on one pod: **852 segments / 18GiB leaked in 5 minutes**.
3. Container restart does **not** clear the leak: `/dev/shm` is a per-pod `emptyDir`, and the sweep from #28089 is CI-only (`SGLANG_IS_IN_CI`), so production never reclaims dead-creator segments. Leaked files still carried PIDs from a process generation that had died hours and ~20 restarts earlier.
4. Every subsequent startup then dies in one of two ways:

   **(a) SIGBUS in the load snapshot writer** — the first fatal component to touch the full tmpfs:
   ```
   Fatal Python error: Bus error
     File ".../sglang/srt/managers/load_snapshot.py", line 370 in _write_payload
     File ".../sglang/srt/managers/load_snapshot.py", line 339 in __init__
     File ".../sglang/srt/managers/load_snapshot.py", line 649 in create_load_snapshot_writer
     File ".../sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 838 in init_ipc_channels
     File ".../sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py", line 552 in __init__
   ```
   The rank dies instantly (mmap write to a full tmpfs), and the remaining ranks then time out:
   ```
   torch.distributed.DistStoreError: Timed out after 601 seconds waiting for clients. 3/4 clients joined.
   ```
   → crashloop period ≈ 11 min, core dump every cycle.

   **(b) NCCL proxy shm ENOSPC** (when startup gets past the load snapshot):
   ```
   NCCL WARN Error: failed to extend /dev/shm/nccl-XXXX to 34210180 bytes, error: No space left on device (28)
   proxy.cc:1458 (proxyProgressInit) -> 2
   init.cc:2572 (ncclCommInitRank) -> 2
   ```
   Note the GPU-side NCCL setup (bootstrap, P2P/IPC channels, rings) fully succeeds — only the 32.6MiB×4 proxy segments fail to allocate.

5. A pod whose `/dev/shm` fills while it is **not** restarting keeps serving, but `_wrap_shm_or_inline` silently degrades mm transport to inline pickling:
   ```
   Failed to allocate shared memory for multimodal feature transport ([Errno 28] No space left on device); falling back to inline transport.
   ```
   This is both a throughput cliff (large tensors now go through pickling) and a ticking bomb — the pod's next restart converts it to the crashloop above.

## Why a container restart doesn't self-heal

- `/dev/shm` here is `emptyDir: {medium: Memory, sizeLimit: 18Gi}` at pod scope — its lifetime is the pod, not the container. (Verified: two pods on the same host see disjoint segment sets, and leaked files outlive dozens of container restarts.)
- With the runtime-default per-container `/dev/shm`, restart would indeed clear the leak — which is probably why this hasn't been reported by default-k8s users. Anyone using the (very common) emptyDir-at-/dev/shm pattern to size shm for NCCL is exposed.

## Proposed fix (minimal)

- Run the **pid-stamped sweep** from #28089 at every scheduler startup (top of `run_scheduler_process`, before `Scheduler(...)` construction), with orphan families still CI-only. The pid-stamped rule only unlinks `sgl_shm_*` / `multi_tokenizer_args_*` segments whose creator pid is dead — safe on a pod-private `/dev/shm`, and pid reuse only degrades to under-collection. This turns "one crash = pod permanently dead" back into "one crash = one restart".
- Deeper follow-ups (not required to stop the bleeding): unlink pending mm segments on request abort/error paths; quiesce tokenizer workers before scheduler teardown so the drain window cannot leak in-flight segments at all.

Happy to send a PR for the startup call site + de-gated pid-stamped rule + tests.

## Workarounds

- Delete the affected pods (fresh emptyDir) — a container restart alone never recovers.
- `SGLANG_LOAD_SNAPSHOT_USE_ZMQ=1` removes death mode (a) but not (b), and does not reclaim any space.

## Related

- #28089 added the sweep, CI-only by design ("pid-liveness is only a trustworthy ownership signal in single-tenant runner containers"). In a container/pod with a private `/dev/shm`, the pid check is authoritative, so the conservative rule can run in production.
- #16402 introduced `ShmPointerMMData` (the leaky segment lifecycle).
- #29010 — a different failure of the same component (unlink/open race).

`sglang` version: fork of v0.5.x mainline (post #28089), single-node TP4/DP4 VLM workload.
