[Bug] DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 on 2× H200: progressive output corruption under concurrency (dsv4 + DP attention)
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug


## Summary

Serving `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` with SGLang on 2× H200 produces
**corrupted output that scales with batch size**. It starts as subtly degraded
language, escalates to malformed/mis-channelled tool-call markup, and ends in
complete token soup. We reproduced it on **two configurations that share almost
nothing** except SGLang, the checkpoint, `--attention-backend dsv4` and DP
attention — including a self-built image carrying the #33098 patch — and we do
**not** see it with vLLM 0.26.0 on the same node, same checkpoint, same fp8 KV.

We suspect a KV/page-index issue in the DSA ("HiSparse") path under batching —
i.e. the same *class* of defect as #31482 / #31901, but on the non-PD code path.

## Environment

| | Config A (production node) | Config B (independent test) |
|---|---|---|
| SGLang | `v0.5.15.post1-cu130` (release) | `v0.5.16` **self-built with the #33098 patch** |
| GPUs | 2× H200 NVL | 2× H200 (different provider/host) |
| Parallelism | `--tp 2 --dp 2 --ep 2 --enable-dp-attention` | `--tp 2 --dp 2 --ep 2 --enable-dp-attention --enable-dp-lm-head` |
| Speculative | none | `--speculative-algorithm DSPARK` (num_draft_tokens 6) |
| HiCache | 3-tier (`--enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-ratio 4 --hicache-storage-backend file`) | none |
| mem-fraction | 0.92 | 0.90 |
| Common | `--attention-backend dsv4`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4`, `--chunked-prefill-size 4096`, `--max-running-requests 256`, `--reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 --tool-call-parser deepseekv4`, `--trust-remote-code`, DP attention | |

Full command line for A:

```
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --trust-remote-code \
  --tp 2 --dp 2 --ep 2 --enable-dp-attention \
  --attention-backend dsv4 --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --chunked-prefill-size 4096 --mem-fraction-static 0.92 \
  --disable-flashinfer-autotune --max-running-requests 256 \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \
  --enable-hierarchical-cache --hicache-ratio 4 --hicache-write-policy write_through_selective \
  --hicache-io-backend kernel --hicache-mem-layout page_first --hicache-storage-backend file \
  --enable-metrics --enable-cache-report
```

Full command line for B (image built from `v0.5.16` + #33098, needed because
DSpark × DP attention crashes on the plain release — see "Relation to #33098"):

```
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --trust-remote-code \
  --tp 2 --dp 2 --ep 2 --enable-dp-attention --enable-dp-lm-head \
  --attention-backend dsv4 --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --chunked-prefill-size 4096 --mem-fraction-static 0.90 \
  --disable-flashinfer-autotune --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \
  --max-running-requests 256 \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \
  --enable-metrics --enable-cache-report
```

Workload: agentic coding clients (Claude Code / OpenAI-compatible agents), long
contexts (50k–500k tokens), thinking enabled, 30–70 tools per request, streaming.


## Symptoms — one defect, three severity tiers

**Tier 1 — degraded language.** Grammatically fluent but semantically wrong
words, drifting register, occasional wrong-language insertions (our traffic is
mixed German/English, and corrupted turns swap between the two mid-sentence). Easy to dismiss
as model quality until the harder tiers show up in the same session.

**Tier 2 — tool-call markup emitted in the wrong channel / malformed.** DSML
markup appears as visible text, or a complete, well-formed DSML block is streamed
as `reasoning_content` while `</think>` never arrives, so the tool parser never
sees it and the turn ends `finish_reason: stop` with empty content and no tool
calls. From a byte-level capture in front of the server (1203 upstream chunks,
one turn):

- `<｜DSML｜tool_calls>` / `<｜DSML｜invoke name="Bash">` / closers arrive
  **exclusively in `delta.reasoning_content`**
- **no `</think>` anywhere** in the stream (neither reasoning nor content)
- zero `delta.tool_calls`, `content` deltas empty, final chunk `finish_reason: "stop"`

We initially read this as a reasoning/tool parser classification bug. Given tier 3
below, a corrupted or dropped `</think>` token is at least as likely an
explanation — which is why we are filing it here rather than as a parser issue.

**Tier 3 — total corruption.** Verbatim examples from production (German/English
mixed input):

```
Allen Kolleginnen und Kollegen großzügig nuts. Hier die Rücksicht genommen.</think>
```

(Reads as grammatical German with semantically random words: "To all colleagues
generously nuts. Here the consideration taken." The English word "nuts" is spliced
into an otherwise German sentence, and `</think>` lands in the visible answer.)

```
:** Which better move me taped the Lightness, the flip script se ker @ Verb's 0.</think>
Wie einfach regarding to the{ csvDiscovery: { React was gebraten. Damit nun m who
meint that she is. User turned adjected slight. And then got the safety influence
and in man mit. Gu easily.
```

The second sample mixes German and English mid-sentence with no semantic
connection to the request ("React was gebraten" = "React was fried"), and again
carries `</think>` inside the visible answer. A third sample degenerated into a
heading repeated eight times with fragmentary table rows ("## Fixed Jira
Configuration" / "| Column | B" / "-(follows | |" …), ending in the model's own
line "... Content has drifted far from the instructions.".

The model sometimes notices and apologises for its own output in the next turn —
"das war Unsinn — meine letzte Antwort war fehlerhaftes Zeug" ("that was nonsense —
my last answer was broken stuff") — i.e. the corruption is in the generated tokens,
not in client-side rendering.

## Load correlation

The reports clustered exactly in a window where the server ran **up to 8–9
concurrent requests per DP rank** (`sglang:num_running_reqs` from the Prometheus
metrics endpoint, per `dp_rank`).
Single-request smoke tests are clean; we could not reproduce any tier with
sequential synthetic requests, including 14 attempts spanning complex nested
tool schemas, thinking on/off, multi-turn tool histories, and contexts of
30k / 120k / 155k / 770k tokens with `reasoning_effort: max`. Corruption only
showed up under real concurrent production traffic.

## What we ruled out

- **HiCache / L2+L3 offloading** — config B has no host or disk tier (verified
  against the deployed container spec: no `--enable-hierarchical-cache`, no
  `--hicache-*`, no NVMe mount, no `SGLANG_HICACHE_*` env) and still corrupts.
  **Not** ruled out: the device-level radix/prefix cache, which was active in both
  configs (`--disable-radix-cache` is not set anywhere). A page-ID mismatch between
  the radix cache and the DSA indexer tiers is in fact one of our hypotheses below.
- **Speculative decoding** — config A has none and still corrupts.
- **PD disaggregation / Mooncake** — not used in either config.
- **#33098 as a sufficient fix** — config B *includes* that patch and still
  corrupts, so whatever remains is not (only) the DSpark draft-batch metadata.
- **The checkpoint and the hardware** — same node, same checkpoint, same
  `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` served by **vLLM 0.26.0** (TP=2 + EP, block-size 256,
  prefix caching, no offloading): no corruption observed in production traffic
  after the switch. This is what we are running now.
- **Client-side / proxy** — the corruption is present in the raw upstream SSE
  chunks captured in front of the server.

## Relation to #33098

Config B runs a self-built `v0.5.16` image with the #33098 patch ("Fix DSpark and
DP/EP"), because without it DSpark + `--enable-dp-attention` cannot start at all:
first `ValueError: DSpark with dp attention requires --enable-dp-lm-head`, and
with that flag a warm-up crash loop in the draft forward
(`decode_cuda_graph_runner.can_run_graph` → `TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not
iterable`, both DP ranks, ~24 min boot/timeout cycle). With the patch it boots and
serves — and then shows the corruption described above. So #33098 fixes the
startup/graph-admission problem but does not address this.

## Suspected area

The remaining common factors are `--attention-backend dsv4` (DSA/HiSparse) with
fp8 KV **and DP attention**, under batching. DeepSeek-V4 keeps several KV tiers (full / swa / c4 / c128
indexer). If page or batch indices for the indexer tiers can be mismatched while
several sequences share a batch — or across DP ranks, where token counts and
padding differ per rank —  sparse attention would select the wrong tokens —
which produces exactly this signature: locally fluent, semantically wrong output
that gets worse as batch size grows, up to complete token soup, and occasionally
destroys single structural tokens such as `</think>`.

That is the same class of defect as:

- **#31482** — "DeepSeek-V4 PD HiSparse shows lower accuracy on GPQA and SWE-Bench",
  including malformed/mixed DSML in failed turns
- **#31901** — fix for the PD/Mooncake path: host KV page indices were used for
  both host and device destination buffers because "HiSparse allocates host pages
  and logical device pages independently, so their page IDs are not guaranteed to
  match"

Our setups do **not** use PD, so #31901 cannot be the fix for us — but the
described independent-page-ID hazard would explain everything we see if it also
exists on the plain (non-PD) dsv4 path, e.g. between the device pools of the
different indexer tiers, or between radix-cache page IDs and indexer page IDs.

## Questions

1. Is there a known batch-size-dependent page/index hazard in the non-PD dsv4
   HiSparse path (device-side only, no host/disk tiers involved), in particular
   under `--enable-dp-attention` where per-rank token counts/padding differ?
2. Is `--attention-backend dsv4` + `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` on Hopper a tested
   combination for 0731, or is fp8 KV expected to be used only with specific
   indexer settings?
3. Anything we can enable to help localise this (per-tier page-ID assertions, a
   debug mode that validates indexer page mapping against the radix cache)?

## Side observation (may be unrelated)

On config A, `sglang:cache_hit_rate` reported `0.978` for `dp_rank=0` and exactly
`0.0` for `dp_rank=1`, while rank 1's host pool was 92 % full
(`hicache_host_used_tokens` 24.7M of 26.7M total) and rank 0's only 44 %. 

### Reproduction


**Model:** `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`, unmodified, from HF.

**How it manifests:** real production traffic only. Agentic coding clients
(Claude Code and OpenAI-compatible agents) with thinking enabled, 30–70 tools per
request, contexts of 50k–500k tokens, streaming, several users in parallel. First
corrupted answers appear within minutes of taking real traffic, and cluster where
`sglang:num_running_reqs` reaches 8–9 per DP rank.

**We have no deterministic reproducer.** Synthetic *sequential* requests stayed
clean across 14 deliberate attempts against the affected server (deeply nested tool
schemas, thinking on/off, multi-turn histories with tool results, contexts of
30k / 120k / 155k / 770k tokens, `reasoning_effort: max`) — so a single request,
however large, does not trigger it. 
We did **not** get to try synthetic *concurrent*
load against an affected server: by the time we understood the load correlation,
production had already been moved to vLLM to stop user impact, and we did not want
to put the corrupting configuration back in front of users. Reproducing under
synthetic concurrency is therefore still untested from our side.

What we can offer instead of a reproducer:

- both affected deployments still exist and can be resumed on the affected
  hardware, so we can run **instrumented builds or candidate patches** and report
  back.

### Environment

Config A: 

Python: 3.12.3 (main, Jun 19 2026, 12:46:00) [GCC 13.3.0]
CUDA available: True
GPU 0,1: NVIDIA H200 NVL
GPU 0,1 Compute Capability: 9.0

title: [Feature] Add FP8 SSM state pool (`--mamba-ssm-dtype float8`) for GDN hybrid models
body:
### Checklist

- [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Motivation

## Motivation

The Qwen3.8-27B cookbook's sizing formula prices the GDN state pool as the binding
constraint on consumer GPUs: *"the GDN state pool (sets the concurrency ceiling)"*, with
`state/slot = 153.9 MB` at float32. On a 32GB RTX 5090 at the default sizing, a bfloat16
state pool pins the ceiling the way the cookbook warns about — the server logs
*"max_running_requests is capped to 7 by the mamba state cache (max_mamba_cache_size=36,
5 state slots per request)"*. The `Mamba SSM Dtype` axis currently stops at
float32 / bfloat16 / float16+SR, so there is no in-engine way to buy back that concurrency.

We implemented and validated the next rung: **`--mamba-ssm-dtype float8`** — an opt-in
FP8 (e4m3) state pool with per-tile dynamic scales, which halves `state_bytes` in the
`--mamba-full-memory-ratio` formula (state/slot: 153.9 MB fp32 → 77 MB bf16 →
**38.8 MB fp8**) and doubles the concurrency ceiling at fixed memory.

## Proposal

- **Per-tile dynamic scales**: one fp32 scale per (head, 32-row V-tile × K) —
  `scale = amax / 240`, quantize to e4m3 on write, dequantize on read. This mirrors the
  semantics the chunk kernels already use for the final-state epilogue; the PR extends
  the same semantics to every other state write path.
- **Kernel-native FP8 I/O** in the FLA chunk / fused-recurrent path (no bf16 staging);
  MTP verify commits through a bf16-intermediate → FP8 requantize scatter.
- **Scale-aware track/cache paths** — a correctness requirement we learned the hard way
  (see Additional context): every state write path must carry the per-tile scales with
  the qdata; we fix three paths that silently dropped them.
- **GDN-only gating** initially: KDA and Mamba2 kernels do not have FP8 state I/O, so the
  dtype should be restricted to `hybrid_gdn_config` models at the config layer.

PR breakdown (happy to rebase onto latest main and split accordingly):

1. FP8 SSM state pool (subset of our fork patch): `mamba_utils` dtype entries,
   `memory_pool` scale tensors + FP8 pool, FLA kernel FP8 I/O, MTP requantize scatter,
   `kv_cache_configurator` adjustments, GDN-only gating.
2. Scale-aware state write/copy paths: `_track_mamba_state_extend`, the decode-time
   track kernels in `mamba_state_scatter_triton.py`, and the GDN backend call site.
3. Test kit extension: FP8-capable GDN attention fixture (the fixture currently
   hardcodes `temporal=fp32`, so the matrix has never exercised a quantized pool)
   + registered FP8 cases.
4. Validation data & repro scripts (the drift/NIAH harness is ~400 lines; happy to
   contribute it as an integration test if there's interest).

Not included (separate concerns): our NVFP4 GEMV work and other fork-local changes.

## Alternatives considered

- **bfloat16 (already on the axis)**: halves state_bytes vs fp32 but still caps
  concurrency at 7 on a 32GB card at default sizing — insufficient for the consumer/
  workstation segment the cookbook targets.
- **int8 `MambaCheckpointPool`**: compresses *cached (idle)* states on the radix side;
  orthogonal to the active pool. Its docstring argues int8 over fp8 for the cache side
  ("loaded ONCE on a hit... fp8 wastes bits on the exponent") — that argument does not
  extend to the active pool, where kernels read/write the state every chunk and every
  decode step and per-tile dynamic scaling makes e4m3 viable. The two compose:
  cache-side int8, active-side float8.
- **float16 + stochastic rounding**: ~2 bytes/slot, same ceiling problem as bf16.
- **Do nothing / larger GPUs**: leaves the concurrency ceiling pinned exactly where the
  cookbook's calculator shows it, on the hardware class the cookbook explicitly targets.

## Validation

Protocol in the cookbook's terms: two `Mamba SSM Dtype` cells
(**bfloat16** / **float8**), one hardware (RTX 5090 32GB), one checkpoint
(RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4, arch `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` — 16 full-attn +
48 GDN layers), no speculative decoding, greedy; every cell served and scored on the full
GSM8K (1314/1319 evaluated; `sglang.test.run_eval` holds 5 out as the few-shot pool;
`max_tokens 2048`, 16 client threads, server ceiling 11/7). Measured on a fork of
main @ 2026-08-18 (pre-v0.5.19); rebase in progress.

```bash
sglang serve \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --model-path RadixArk/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 \
  --quantization modelopt \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
  --max-running-requests 11 \
  --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer \
  --mamba-ssm-dtype float8     # the proposed axis value
```

| Mamba SSM Dtype | GSM8K | Wall clock | Eval throughput | state slots | concurrency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| bfloat16 | 96.80% | 1381 s | 458 tok/s | 36 | **7 (capped)** |
| float8 | 96.35% (<1 SE) | 925 s | **693 tok/s** | **71** | 11 |

**Long-context safety** (serving envelope: concurrency 1, greedy, ISL 2K→64K,
ShareGPT-derived filler, fixed ~2.3K-token probe, 256-token logprob window per depth) —
this is the coverage gap where quantized-state bugs hide, since the GSM8K envelope never
touches a >2K prefix-cache restore:

- Cold-prefix drift (pure FP8 recurrence), float8 vs bfloat16: mean |Δlogprob| 0.8–1.2,
  top-1 agreement 76–91%, flat across all depths — no error accumulation to 64K,
  directly addressing the documented *"per-token recurrent quantization accumulates
  errors"* concern.
- Prefix-cache restore path (the agent/multi-turn pattern): after the scale fixes,
  restored-state probe logprobs are **bit-identical to cold prefill** at every depth.
- NIAH retrieval, 16K/32K, 10 needles, shared-prefix cache hits: bfloat16 10/10 & 10/10;
  float8 9/10 & 10/10 (pre-fix: 1/10 & 1/10 — see below).
- 10-turn multi-turn loop × 3 sessions: 30/30 both dtypes.
- GDN attention unit matrix (official kit tolerances ATOL=RTOL=3e-2): 10/10 under both
  dtypes, via the kit extension in PR #3.
- AIME25: 3.33% = 3.33% (both at the model's floor; parity, low discriminating power).

## A correctness finding relevant to any quantized-state work

Every state write path
(chunk-kernel epilogue, extend-time track slots, decode-time track kernel) must carry
the per-tile scales with the qdata. We found three paths that silently dropped them;
the failure mode is a *silent* ~240× magnitude blowup on prefix-cache restores at ≥12K
context — GSM8K-style sweeps do not catch it (single-turn, <2K shared prefix), and the
unit kit does not either (`enable_mamba_extra_buffer=False`). This is why PR #2 exists
and why we'd like to contribute the drift/NIAH harness as an integration test.

## Limitations

One cell per dtype, one hardware
(RTX 5090 / SM120), one checkpoint; the GSM8K A/B is without speculative decoding (the
MTP-path FP8 has separate acceptance-length evidence: 2.41 vs 2.38 on 100 real-text
prompts); untested on the `UnifiedHybridReqToTokenPool` variant and under PD
disaggregation.

## Open questions

1. Interest in taking this as an opt-in axis value, given the int8-checkpoint-pool
   precedent and the dtype ladder?
2. Preferred gating: restrict `float8` to GDN models at the config layer, or
   warn-and-allow?
3. Target the current pool first, or land after the unified memory-pool migration
   settles?
4. Flag surface: extend `--mamba-ssm-dtype` (the cookbook axis) vs a dedicated
   `--mamba-state-quant` flag?

cc-ing folks from #23891 (mamba extra-buffer radix cache) and #30169 (SM100 CuteDSL
GDN/KDA state I/O) since the track-path and state-I/O changes touch that machinery.

### Related resources

_No response_

title: [Bug] Llama4 NVFP4 MoE crashes on SM120/SM121: apply_router_weight_on_input is not supported for Flashinfer
body:
### Checklist

- [x] 1. I have searched related issues but cannot get the expected help.
- [x] 2. The bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] 3. Please note that if the bug-related issue you submitted lacks corresponding environment info and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be challenging for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, reducing the likelihood of receiving feedback.
- [x] 4. If the issue you raised is not a bug but a question, please raise a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions/new/choose.
- [x] 5. Please use English, otherwise it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

Serving a Llama-4 Scout NVFP4 (ModelOpt) checkpoint on an SM120/SM121 GPU (Blackwell consumer / DGX Spark GB10) aborts during server warmup:

```
AssertionError: apply_router_weight_on_input is not supported for Flashinfer
```

This was reproduced on an **unmodified upstream `main` build** at commit `bfefdc52d7046bd5c3eae4f4b784a9e0ead2cd05` (2026-07-21), with no backend override: `--moe-runner-backend` was left at its default `auto`.

Three pieces of default behavior combine:

1. `python/sglang/srt/models/llama4.py` constructs its `FusedMoE` with `apply_router_weight_on_input=True` (Llama4 applies the router weight to the expert *input*).
2. On SM120/SM121, `auto` is rewritten to `flashinfer_cutlass` for `modelopt_fp4`, because the trtllm-gen MoE kernels are SM100-only. The server logs: `Use flashinfer_cutlass as MoE runner backend on SM120 for modelopt_fp4 (trtllm-gen MoE kernels are SM100-only)`.
3. The CUTLASS NVFP4 path then asserts the flag is unsupported — two sites in `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_cutlass.py` (the a2a=none and a2a=flashinfer fused funcs) and one in `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/modelopt_quant.py`.

So on SM120/SM121 there is no reachable NVFP4 MoE backend that honors `apply_router_weight_on_input`. Walking the NVFP4 `apply()` dispatch — `is_marlin()` → `enable_flashinfer_trtllm_moe` → `enable_flashinfer_cutedsl_moe` → `enable_flashinfer_cutlass_moe` → `NotImplementedError` — the Triton runner (which does support the flag) is not reachable for NVFP4. `flashinfer_cutedsl` asserts against the flag as well; `flashinfer_trtllm` is SM100-only; and `marlin` has no reference to the flag at all, so it silently ignores it (see "Additional context" — that path is numerically wrong, not a workaround).

### Reproduction

On an SM120/SM121 Blackwell GPU (reproduced on NVIDIA DGX Spark, 2 nodes x 1 GPU, TP=2), on unmodified upstream `main` at `bfefdc52d7046bd5c3eae4f4b784a9e0ead2cd05`:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path nvidia/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct-NVFP4 \
  --quantization modelopt_fp4 \
  --tp-size 2 \
  --page-size 16
```

The server aborts during warmup, before it accepts any request. Passing `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_cutlass` explicitly gives the same crash; the default `auto` resolves to it on this architecture.

Note on our run: the reproduction was captured with randomly-initialized weights (`--load-format dummy`) and `--context-length 36000`. The crash is triggered by the model's `apply_router_weight_on_input=True` plus the SM120 backend selection, so it is independent of the weight values — dummy weights simply make it cheap to hit.

Observed server config on the failing run: `moe_runner_backend='flashinfer_cutlass'`, `quantization='modelopt_fp4'`, `tp_size=2`, `enable_dp_attention=False`.

### Actual behavior

The server aborts during warmup with the traceback below, captured verbatim from the unmodified upstream run. The model cannot be served at all on this architecture at NVFP4.

```
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/models/llama4.py", line 143, in forward
    shared_out, routed_out = self._forward_core(
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/models/llama4.py", line 158, in _forward_core
    return self._forward_core_shared_routed_overlap(hidden_states)
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/models/llama4.py", line 181, in _forward_core_shared_routed_overlap
    routed_out = self.experts(hidden_states, topk_output)
  File "torch/nn/modules/module.py", line 1779, in _wrapped_call_impl
    return self._call_impl(*args, **kwargs)
  File "torch/nn/modules/module.py", line 1790, in _call_impl
    return forward_call(*args, **kwargs)
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py", line 1275, in forward
    return self.forward_impl(hidden_states, topk_output)
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py", line 1285, in forward_impl
    combine_input = self.run_moe_core(
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py", line 1323, in run_moe_core
    return self.quant_method.apply(
  File "/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/modelopt_quant.py", line 2598, in apply
    not moe_runner_config.apply_router_weight_on_input
AssertionError: apply_router_weight_on_input is not supported for Flashinfer
```

### Expected behavior

The server starts and serves the Llama4 NVFP4 checkpoint on SM120/SM121, applying the router weight to the expert input as the model requires — the same as on SM100, and the same as before the regression below.

### Regression

This is a regression. Bisected with the published nightly wheel index on fixed hardware, model, flags and dependency versions:

- last known good: `3b7a258f63165cbe627d7dae449a4dffb02bc0b9` (2026-06-04)
- first bad: `c6c1f1a29a2f026caf1ba95707ea28b4b91fb841` (2026-06-05)
- culprit in that range: `e76d36214b0f4a6d1cd7af6bab6e199c97bcddfa` — "Changes for SM120 perf and usability for NVFP4" (PR #26496)

PR #26496 added the SM120 NVFP4 routing to `flashinfer_cutlass` (item 2 above). It made NVFP4 usable on SM120 generally, but routed Llama4 into a backend that rejects the flag Llama4 needs. FlashInfer and CUDA were held fixed across the bisect boundary, so the failure tracks the sglang commit alone. The failure still reproduces on `main` as of `bfefdc52d` (2026-07-21).

Note: PR #32229 addresses `apply_router_weight_on_input` for the SM100 trtllm-gen path (MiniMax-M2). It does not touch the SM120 CUTLASS assert and does not fix this.

### Proposed fix (validated)

For **top-1** routing (Llama4 Scout-17B-16E is top-1: `top_k = num_experts_per_tok = 1`), applying the router weight to the expert input is exactly equivalent to pre-scaling the activations and passing unit final scales, because a single expert contributes per token and the expert function is positively homogeneous in that scalar. So instead of asserting, the CUTLASS runner can honor the flag:

```python
def _prescale_router_weight_on_input(dispatch_output, runner_config):
    if not runner_config.apply_router_weight_on_input:
        return dispatch_output
    topk_output = dispatch_output.topk_output
    topk_weights = topk_output.topk_weights
    # Activations already quantized + all-gathered upstream of the runner
    # (fp4 all-gather path): the multiply is no longer expressible here.
    if getattr(dispatch_output, "hidden_states_scale", None) is not None:
        raise NotImplementedError(
            "apply_router_weight_on_input is not supported when activations are "
            "quantized before dispatch (flashinfer_cutlass fp4 all-gather path)."
        )
    assert (
        topk_weights.dim() == 2 and topk_weights.shape[-1] == 1
    ), "apply_router_weight_on_input requires topk=1"
    hidden_states = dispatch_output.hidden_states * topk_weights.to(
        dispatch_output.hidden_states.dtype
    )
    unit_scales = torch.ones_like(topk_weights, dtype=torch.float32)
    return dispatch_output._replace(
        hidden_states=hidden_states,
        topk_output=topk_output._replace(topk_weights=unit_scales),
    )
```

Two constraints are deliberate. The `hidden_states_scale` guard preserves the existing rejection for the fp4 all-gather path (`should_use_flashinfer_cutlass_moe_fp4_allgather()`, which requires dp-attention), where activations are quantized before dispatch and the multiply is no longer expressible — the failing config above has `enable_dp_attention=False`, so it does not take that path. And `unit_scales` must be **float32**: `FusedMoeRunner::runMoe` in `flashinfer_cutlass_fused_moe_binding.cu` requires `token_final_scales.value().dtype() == dl_float32`. This mirrors existing precedent in `topk.py::apply_topk_weights_cpu`, which builds `torch.ones_like(topk_weights, dtype=torch.float32)`.

For topk>1 the assert should remain, since folding a per-expert weight into shared activations is not equivalent there.

### Validation evidence

The patch above was applied to the installed sglang inside the same upstream container, and the previously-crashing configuration was re-run end to end on the same hardware (2 nodes x 1 GPU, TP=2), with `--moe-runner-backend` left at `auto` so the SM120 CUTLASS selection is still exercised (`moe_runner_backend='flashinfer_cutlass'`, `quantization='modelopt_fp4'`). Same model, flags, launcher and hardware as the failing run above, so unpatched-fails / patched-passes is a controlled pair:

- Unpatched upstream `bfefdc52d`: aborts at warmup with the traceback above.
- Same build + this patch: server reaches ready state and both benchmark scenarios complete `5 valid requests and 0 errors`.
- `AssertionError`, `apply_router_weight_on_input is not supported`, `token_final_scales`, `Traceback`, `NotImplementedError` and `CUDA error` all grep to zero hits in the patched run log.
- Decode-side inter-token latency, which exercises the MoE runner on every token, improved versus a pre-regression run of the same benchmark (-6.78% and -2.19% across the two scenarios), so the pre-scale does not cost decode throughput. These runs used randomly-initialized weights, so they are liveness/performance figures only, not an accuracy claim.
- Offline, in fp64, the pre-scale is bit-exact against a reference implementation (max abs err 0.000e+00), whereas applying the router weight to the expert *output* — as the marlin path effectively does — gives max abs err 2.922e-02, roughly 35% relative error on a gated SwiGLU MLP.

### Second, separate bug found while validating this

A first validation attempt failed at the same call with a dtype error, which exposes an independent latent bug worth fixing regardless of the above.

`select_experts()` normalizes `topk_weights` to float32 on every built-in branch, but returns a `custom_routing_function`'s output dtype **verbatim** (`python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py`, ~line 2254). `Llama4MoE.custom_routing_function` casts back to bfloat16. Meanwhile `flashinfer_cutlass.py` passes `topk_weights` to the binding un-cast (lines ~225 and ~370), and `flashinfer_cutedsl.py` does the same (~401, ~463) — while the binding requires float32 as noted above.

So any model supplying a `custom_routing_function` that returns non-float32 weights can hit a dtype violation on these paths. Grepping for `custom_routing_function` users, the models sharing this exposure are: afmoe, cohere2_moe, gemma4_causal, grok, interns1pro, phimoe. A defensive `.to(torch.float32)` at the binding call sites (or normalizing the custom-routing return in `select_experts`) would close it.

### Additional context

Why pinning to another backend is not an acceptable workaround: `marlin` is the only NVFP4-reachable backend that does not reject the flag, but it does not implement it either — `fused_marlin_moe` passes `mul_topk_weights=False, top_k=topk` to GEMM1 and `mul_topk_weights=True, top_k=1` to GEMM2, i.e. it scales the expert *output*. With a gated non-linear MLP, `w * expert(x) != expert(w * x)`, so pinning to marlin converts a loud crash into silently wrong numerics (the ~35% figure above). That is why this needs to be fixed in the CUTLASS runner.

### Environment

Failing reproduction, from the container-recorded environment of the crashing run:

- sglang: `0.0.0.dev1+gbfefdc52d` — upstream `main` commit `bfefdc52d7046bd5c3eae4f4b784a9e0ead2cd05` (2026-07-21), source checkout, unmodified
- sglang-kernel 0.4.5, sgl-deep-gemm 0.1.4.post1
- flashinfer-python 0.6.14, flashinfer-jit-cache 0.6.14+cu130, flashinfer-cubin 0.6.14
- torch 2.11.0+cu130, torchvision 0.26.0+cu130, triton 3.6.0
- CUDA 13.0.1, NCCL 2.28.3-1
- Python 3.12.3, transformers 5.12.1, nvidia-modelopt 0.45.0
- GPU: NVIDIA DGX Spark (SM120/SM121 Blackwell), 2 nodes x 1 GPU, TP=2
- CPU: aarch64 Cortex-X925 (20 cores); OS Ubuntu 24.04; ~122.5 GB total memory per node
- Model: `nvidia/Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E-Instruct-NVFP4`, `--quantization modelopt_fp4`

Also reproduces on nightly wheels at and after `c6c1f1a29a2f026caf1ba95707ea28b4b91fb841` (2026-06-05); last good `3b7a258f63165cbe627d7dae449a4dffb02bc0b9` (2026-06-04).

title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + Engram: profiled SPS table (compact ragged verify) dies in CUDA-graph capture with "engram target-verify expects one equal block per request"
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (an Engram model), enabling DSpark compact ragged verify via a profiled SPS cost table makes the engine die **deterministically during CUDA-graph capture, on every rank**:

```
AssertionError: engram target-verify expects one equal block per request, got 42 tokens for 8 requests of 6
```

Removing the table (so the planner stays on the verify-all / static schedule) boots and serves fine, so weights, TP4/EP4, FP8 KV cache and the RDMA transport are all healthy.

**Suspected root cause.** The capture batch seems to get the wrong slot count. `DecodeCudaGraphRunner._ragged_capture_slots()` returns `min(num_tokens, self.max_bs)` (`model_executor/runner/decode_cuda_graph_runner.py:667-670`), while the per-tier token bucket is `bs * captured_req_width` (`_build_ragged_verify_token_buckets`, same file, line 569). For the tier `num_tokens = 42` (bs=7, width=6) with `max_bs = 8` this selects **8 slots**, so `build_capture_verify_lens(num_tokens=42, num_slots=8, num_draft_tokens=6)` returns `[6,6,5,5,5,5,5,5]` — 8 rows of unequal length summing to 42. `EngramHasher.forward()`'s target-verify branch (`srt/layers/engram.py:291-298`) requires one equal block per request (`num_tokens == bs * block` → `42 != 8*6`), so the capture batch is rejected. Only the largest tier (bs == max_bs → 48 tokens / 8 slots) survives; every smaller tier aborts. Dense-layout consumers elsewhere handle ragged layouts through `RaggedVerifyLayout.padded_to_bucket(padded_bs, cap)`, but the Engram hasher reads the raw `input_ids.shape[0]` / `req_pool_indices.shape[0]` pair before any padding.

The test escape hatch `SGLANG_TEST_RAGGED_VERIFY_FORCE_UNIFORM_CAPTURE=1` avoids the capture assertion but then dies on the first request (second traceback below), so compact ragged verify currently appears unusable for this model.

**Model:** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (native weights: MXFP4 experts / FP8 dense), Engram layer with per-rank shards on local NVMe.
**Hardware:** 4x NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, SM 12.1, 128 GB unified memory), TP4 + EP4, 200G RoCE.
**Image:** `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-dsv41`, `org.opencontainers.image.revision = e087e662ba1ac4ef7747537e2a9141085efd4561`.

The roadmap is based on the features and inference paths provided by the official SenseNova-U1 repository: [OpenSenseNova/SenseNova-U1](https://github.com/OpenSenseNova/SenseNova-U1). title: [Feature][MLX] Gemma 4 text generation on Apple Silicon
body:
## Motivation

Add correctness-first Gemma 4 text generation to SGLang's MLX backend on Apple Silicon, then incrementally add scheduler coverage, first-class radix-cache integration, larger variants, multimodal inputs, and MTP.

This tracks a concrete model contribution under the Apple Silicon roadmap in #19137 and cross-links the existing Gemma 4 roadmap in #26596. SGLang's existing Gemma 4 implementation targets the standard GPU model path; the MLX backend instead loads and executes models through `mlx-lm`.

## Why an incremental path is needed

`mlx-lm` already implements Gemma 4, but Gemma 4's cache and attention contracts cannot currently be represented by SGLang's uniform MLX radix pool. The model combines:

- sliding-window and full-attention layers;
- heterogeneous per-layer head dimensions and KV layouts;
- K=V attention variants without `v_proj`;
- Gemma-specific `v_norm`; and
- YOCO layers that reuse earlier K/V and do not own cache entries.

The proposed MVP therefore leaves cache semantics with `mlx-lm` while retaining SGLang's scheduler and HTTP APIs. This is a correctness bridge, not the final optimized cache design.

## Milestones

- [ ] E2B text-only MVP using model-native `mlx-lm` caches, with radix caching, overlap scheduling, and chunked prefill disabled.
- [ ] Scheduler hardening for cancellation, chunked prefill, overlap/chained decode, and multiple concurrent requests.
- [ ] Model-neutral per-layer KV specifications and YOCO cache ownership.
- [ ] First-class heterogeneous full/SWA cache and radix integration, coordinated with #30050, #30091, and #30156.
- [ ] Variant expansion: E4B, then 31B, then 26B MoE with per-checkpoint accuracy gates.
- [ ] Separate follow-ups for multimodal inputs and MTP speculative decoding.

## MVP acceptance criteria

- Cover the public `gemma4.Model` wrapper and text backbone with a tiny real architecture test.
- Match raw `mlx-lm` greedy decoding across a prompt longer than the synthetic sliding window.
- Preserve independent native cache state for multiple requests and release state when requests finish.
- Fail with actionable startup errors for unsupported radix/overlap/chunked configurations.
- Launch `mlx-community/gemma-4-e2b-it-4bit` and serve `/v1/chat/completions` on Apple Silicon.
- Match unmodified `mlx-lm` token-for-token on a real E2B checkpoint.
- Document the conservative 2,048-token validated configuration and all non-goals.

A local prototype currently meets these criteria: the real 4-bit E2B checkpoint loaded as 35 layers with 15 model-owned YOCO caches, matched 8/8 greedy tokens against raw `mlx-lm`, and returned correct OpenAI-compatible chat responses.

## MVP non-goals

Radix/prefix reuse, fused batched attention, long-context claims, Gemma 4 Unified, E4B/31B/26B support, multimodal inputs, MTP, and custom Gemma-specific Metal kernels.

## Related resources

- Apple Silicon roadmap: #19137
- SGLang Gemma 4 roadmap: #26596
- SGLang Gemma 4 GPU implementation: #21952
- `mlx-lm` Gemma 4: ml-explore/mlx-lm#1093
- vLLM Metal baseline E2B support: vllm-project/vllm-metal#251
- vLLM Metal heterogeneous 31B/26B KV layouts: vllm-project/vllm-metal#279
- vLLM Metal MTP roadmap (later work, not baseline support): vllm-project/vllm-metal#364

title: [Feature][MLX] Gemma 4 MTP speculative decoding on Apple Silicon
body:
## Goal

Track a correctness-first, experimental Gemma 4 Frozen-KV MTP path for the MLX backend on Apple Silicon.

Prerequisites:

- Gemma 4 MLX baseline roadmap: #32101
- Native-cache baseline PR: #32102
- Closed umbrella prototype retained as implementation evidence: #32252

The umbrella implementation is now split into six reviewable Draft PRs on the personal fork. Each branch is based on the preceding branch; the first starts from `feature/mlx-gemma4-native-cache`.

## Incremental prototype stack

- [ ] [1. One-draft verification and native-cache transactions](https://github.com/wirybeaver/sglang/pull/1)
- [ ] [2. Optional target feedback](https://github.com/wirybeaver/sglang/pull/2)
- [ ] [3. Gemma 4 assistant runtime](https://github.com/wirybeaver/sglang/pull/3)
- [ ] [4. Synchronous one-draft worker](https://github.com/wirybeaver/sglang/pull/4)
- [ ] [5. Guarded MLX serving enablement](https://github.com/wirybeaver/sglang/pull/5)
- [ ] [6. Observability, pinned E2E, and experimental docs](https://github.com/wirybeaver/sglang/pull/6)

## Level 1 contract

The initial supported shape is intentionally narrow:

- Apple Silicon with the MLX backend.
- Text-only Gemma 4 E2B target `mlx-community/gemma-4-e2b-it-4bit` at revision `238767527555cb75a05732a84dff5d6ba0dd6809`.
- Matching assistant `mlx-community/gemma-4-E2B-it-assistant-bf16` at revision `a7770799b560135ebdbfae8b7f468947415003bc`, loaded through `mlx-vlm==0.5.0`.
- `FROZEN_KV_MTP`, with compatible `NEXTN` alias resolution.
- Greedy requests with explicit `temperature=0`.
- One proposal, top-k 1, one speculative step, and verify width 2 (`root + draft`).
- Batch size and maximum running requests of one; synchronous scheduling.
- Radix cache, overlap scheduling, and chunked prefill disabled.
- Context length no greater than 2,048. If `max_total_tokens` is explicit, it must be at least the context length.
- No multimodal inputs, distributed execution, sampling penalties, logprobs, constrained decoding, sessions, LoRA, or custom logits processors.

This milestone makes no throughput or speedup claim.

## Acceptance criteria

- MLX never instantiates the Torch/CUDA Frozen-KV worker.
- Unit coverage exercises accept, reject, bonus-token, rollback, and rotating-cache behavior while preserving target-only greedy output.
- Optional hidden-state capture does not change target logits or tokens.
- Assistant target-KV views are read-only and generation checked.
- Scheduler commit accounting and finish/failure cleanup remain single-owner and leak free.
- Fresh pinned target-only and MTP servers return identical IDs, text, and finish reason for a 64-token cross-window `/generate` request.
- Real execution reports nonzero proposal and verification activity; per-request and worker counter deltas agree.
- Completion and cache flush return request/cache/view counts to zero, retain assistant generation, and allow a post-flush request.
- Offline Stage A coverage and the pinned Stage B test pass.
- Documentation labels the feature experimental and lists the exact constraints.

## Follow-up tracks

These are separate gates after Level 1:

- **Concurrency and mixed batches:** request isolation, ragged batches, mixed prefill/decode, and BS=2/4.
- **Heterogeneous paged/radix KV:** per-layer local/global layouts, YOCO ownership, scheduler-managed pages, radix reuse, and read-only assistant views.
- **Performance and overlap:** reduce copies and synchronization, integrate overlap, benchmark larger targets, and publish results only while exact-token parity remains green.

The paged/radix and native-cache performance tracks may proceed in parallel.

## Related work

- Apple Silicon roadmap: #19137
- Gemma 4 roadmap: #26596
- Speculative decoding roadmap: #24436
- Speculative decoding v2: #27607
- vLLM Metal MTP roadmap: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-metal/issues/364

title: [Bug] --quantization marlin is accepted by CLI but missing from the registry
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

`marlin` is accepted as a value for `--quantization` (it is listed in `QUANTIZATION_CHOICES`), but it is not a direct key in `QUANTIZATION_METHODS`.

Argument parsing therefore accepts the value, while direct quantization-config resolution later rejects it. The value currently appears to be interpreted only through checkpoint-specific `override_quantization_method` paths (e.g. in `marlin_utils.py`, `gptq/gptq.py`, `awq/awq.py`), so it does not resolve on its own.

This makes the public CLI and the quantization registry inconsistent: a value the CLI advertises as valid cannot be resolved unless the checkpoint metadata happens to select it.

### Reproduction

Reproduced against `upstream/main` at:

```text
a2ddf92e616c6b47f8a166aece71d3c0bc5976af
```

```python
from sglang.srt.layers.quantization import (
    QUANTIZATION_METHODS,
    get_quantization_config,
)
from sglang.srt.server_args import QUANTIZATION_CHOICES

print("marlin in QUANTIZATION_CHOICES:", "marlin" in QUANTIZATION_CHOICES)
print("marlin in QUANTIZATION_METHODS:", "marlin" in QUANTIZATION_METHODS)

get_quantization_config("marlin")
```

Actual output:

```text
marlin in QUANTIZATION_CHOICES: True
marlin in QUANTIZATION_METHODS: False
exception type: ValueError
exception message: Invalid quantization method: marlin. Available methods: ['fp8', 'mxfp8', 'blockwise_int8', 'modelopt', 'modelopt_fp8', 'modelopt_fp4', 'nvfp4_online', 'modelopt_mixed', 'w8a8_int8', 'w8a8_fp8', 'awq', 'awq_marlin', 'bitsandbytes', 'gguf', 'gptq', 'gptq_marlin', 'moe_wna16', 'compressed-tensors', 'w4afp8', 'petit_nvfp4', 'quark', 'quark_mxfp4', 'auto-round', 'auto-round-int8', 'modelslim', 'quark_int4fp8_moe', 'humming', 'mxfp_w4a8', 'mxfp4']
```

The advertised "Available methods" list does not contain `marlin`.

### Expected behavior

A value accepted by `--quantization` should resolve deterministically. Either:

- `marlin` should resolve to a supported registered configuration, or
- it should not be exposed as a direct CLI choice when it is only intended for checkpoint-conditional detection.

title: [Bug] DFlash aux hidden state capture fails when target_layer_ids includes the last decoder layer (qwen3_5 IndexError)
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [ ] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug


### Checklist

- [x] 1. I have searched related issues but cannot get the expected help.
- [x] 2. The bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] 3. Please note that if the bug-related issue you submitted lacks corresponding environment info and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be challenging for us to reproduce and resolve the issue, reducing the likelihood of receiving feedback.

### Describe the bug

When `--spec-capture-aux-layer-ids` contains the **last decoder layer** (`num_hidden_layers - 1`), the DFlash aux-hidden-state capture crashes at server startup on the Qwen3.5 model path:

```
File ".../sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py", line 1034, in init_aux_hidden_state_capture
    self.model.set_dflash_layers_to_capture(self.dflash_target_layer_ids)
  File ".../sglang/srt/models/qwen3_vl.py", line 1309, in set_dflash_layers_to_capture
    self.model.set_dflash_layers_to_capture([val + 1 for val in layer_ids])
  File ".../sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py", line 1210, in set_dflash_layers_to_capture
    setattr(self.layers[layer_id], "_is_layer_to_capture", True)
IndexError: index 32 is out of range
```

**Root cause.** The CLI layer ids are HF-style "capture the *output* of layer k". SGLang captures "before layer i", so the wrapper shifts every id by +1 to capture the hidden state entering layer k+1 (= output of layer k). This convention is intentional and documented in #30204.

The problem: for `k = num_layers - 1` (the last decoder layer), the shifted id is `num_layers`, which does not exist as a module:

- `qwen3_5.py` / `qwen3_vl.py`: `set_dflash_layers_to_capture` does `setattr(self.layers[num_layers], ...)` → **IndexError** (crash at startup).
- `qwen2.py` / `qwen3.py` use a `layers_to_capture` list checked inside the forward loop (`for i in range(start_layer, end_layer)`), so the id `num_layers` **silently never matches** — the server starts but the last layer's output is never captured, producing fewer aux hidden states than the draft config expects. This silent variant is arguably worse: training/serving proceeds with a mismatched feature set.

This is triggered by any DFlash/Domino draft config whose `dflash_config.target_layer_ids` includes the final layer. Existing published configs never hit it (e.g. Qwen3-8B has 36 layers and uses `[3, 11, 19, 27, 31]`), but the Qwen3.5-4B Domino/DFlash draft configs (32 layers, `target_layer_ids=[3, 11, 19, 27, 31]`) require the output of layer 31 and crash on startup. Found while running SpecForge online disaggregated training (server-capture mode) for Qwen3.5-4B on Ascend NPU; the code path is device-independent and reproduces identically on current `main`.


(Qwen3.5-4B has 32 decoder layers; id 31 + the internal +1 shift = index 32 → IndexError. Any 32-layer Qwen3.5/VL target with id 31 in the list reproduces it; `--attention-backend` is irrelevant to the crash.)

### Expected behavior

Capturing the last decoder layer's output should work: `num_layers` in the shifted list is a valid capture position meaning "the hidden state entering the final norm" (= output of the last decoder layer), consistent with the documented "capture before layer i" convention in `qwen3.py` ("SGLang captures 'before layer i'. To capture the hidden state after target layer `k` (HF-style), we capture before layer `k + 1`").

### Suggested fix

In the model forward pass, treat a capture id of `num_layers` as "append the pre-final-norm hidden state after the decoder loop", e.g. for `qwen3_5.py`:

```python
def set_dflash_layers_to_capture(self, layers_to_capture: list[int]):
    self.layers_to_capture = layers_to_capture
    self._capture_after_last_layer = False
    for layer_id in self.layers_to_capture:
        if layer_id >= len(self.layers):
            self._capture_after_last_layer = True  # capture output of the last decoder layer
            continue
        setattr(self.layers[layer_id], "_is_layer_to_capture", True)

# in forward(), after the decoder loop and before the final norm:
if getattr(self, "_capture_after_last_layer", False):
    aux_hidden_states.append(
        hidden_states + residual if residual is not None else hidden_states
    )
```

This matches the value captured by `layer_communicator.prepare_attn_and_capture_last_layer_outputs` for in-range layers (residual-stream input of the next layer) and keeps `aux_hidden_states` ordered by layer id. The `qwen2.py`/`qwen3.py` list-based implementations additionally need the same after-loop capture so the `num_layers` id stops being silently dropped. Happy to open a PR with this change plus a boundary test if the approach looks right.


### Related

- #30204 — documents the +1 capture-offset convention (DSpark/Qwen3)
- #28261 — open PR fixing another Qwen3-VL DFlash capture setup bug
- #19952 — earlier (closed, unmerged) Qwen3.5 DFlash support PR; only validated on 27B, which is why this boundary went unnoticed


### Reproduction

python -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B \
    --dtype bfloat16 \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --skip-tokenizer-init \
    --tp-size 1 \
    --context-length 1031 \
    --chunked-prefill-size -1 \
    --disable-radix-cache \
    --enable-spec-capture \
    --spec-capture-method dflash \
    --spec-capture-aux-layer-ids 3 11 19 27 31 \
    --attention-backend ascend \
    --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000

### Environment

- sglang: v0.5.14 (also reproduced on current `main`; the relevant code is byte-identical)
- Platform: Ascend NPU (910C), but device-independent
- Model: Qwen3.5-4B (32 decoder layers), DFlash/Domino spec-capture training with SpecForge

title: [Bug] Speculative draft auto load format does not resolve object-storage paths
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] This report includes environment information and a minimal reproduction.
- [x] This is a bug report, not a general discussion question.
- [x] This issue is written in English.

### Describe the bug

When a speculative draft model is stored in S3-compatible object storage and `--speculative-draft-load-format auto` is set explicitly, the draft model is loaded with `DefaultModelLoader` instead of `RunaiModelStreamerLoader`.

The target model's `--load-format auto` is resolved from the target model path during `ServerArgs` post-processing. The draft path is not processed independently. During draft worker initialization, the scheduler copies the literal draft value `auto` into the shared `server_args.load_format`. `build_load_config()` therefore creates `LoadConfig(load_format="auto")`, and `get_model_loader()` falls through to `DefaultModelLoader`; it only selects `RunaiModelStreamerLoader` when the format is explicitly `runai_streamer`.

Actual loader selection:

```text
draft S3 path + draft load format auto
  -> LoadFormat.AUTO
  -> DefaultModelLoader
```

Expected loader selection:

```text
draft S3 path + draft load format auto
  -> LoadFormat.RUNAI_STREAMER
  -> RunaiModelStreamerLoader
```

The draft load format should be resolved against the draft model path on draft-specific server arguments. This should not mutate the target model's shared `ServerArgs`. An unspecified draft format should continue to inherit the target format, and explicit non-auto draft formats should remain unchanged.

### Reproduction

Launch speculative decoding with both models in S3-compatible object storage and explicitly request `auto` for the draft:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path s3://bucket/target-model \
  --load-format auto \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
  --speculative-draft-model-path s3://bucket/draft-model \
  --speculative-draft-load-format auto
```

Observe that the target path resolves `auto` to `runai_streamer`, while the draft value remains literal `auto` and reaches `DefaultModelLoader`.

The same mismatch can be verified from the loader-selection path without loading weights:

1. `ServerArgs._handle_load_format()` resolves only `self.model_path`.
2. `Scheduler.maybe_init_draft_worker()` assigns `speculative_draft_load_format` to the shared `load_format`.
3. The draft worker passes that value through `build_load_config()`.
4. `get_model_loader()` selects `RunaiModelStreamerLoader` only for `LoadFormat.RUNAI_STREAMER`; `LoadFormat.AUTO` falls through to `DefaultModelLoader`.

### Environment

- SGLang: latest `origin/main`, commit `a25164bda3`
- Model storage: S3-compatible object storage
- Deployment where observed: 2 nodes, TP=8, PP=2, NVIDIA H20
- The failure occurs deterministically during loader selection, before hardware-specific model execution.

python3 -m sglang.check_env output can be attached from the target deployment environment when filing the issue.

title: [RFC][PD] Seamless P-to-D handoff via token replay
body:
# [RFC][PD] Seamless P-to-D Handoff via Token Replay

## Summary

This RFC proposes an opt-in seamless handoff mode for PD-disaggregated serving.
While the immutable prompt KV cache is transferred from the Prefill worker to
the Decode worker, the Prefill worker temporarily continues decoding and emits
tokens to the client. The Decode worker then replays the emitted token log as a
short extend to reconstruct only the post-prefill KV tail, catches up with the
Prefill worker, and atomically becomes the sole output owner.

The proposal does not replace Mooncake KV transfer and does not change
attention math. It removes the transfer handoff bubble by replacing
post-prefill delta-KV migration with a small token log plus deterministic
replay.

## Motivation

The current disaggregated Prefill lifecycle is:

```text
prefill forward
  -> sample one handoff token
  -> transfer prompt KV
  -> wait for transfer completion
  -> release Prefill KV
  -> return/continue on Decode
```

SGLang already overlaps parts of KV transfer with chunked prefill and supports
incremental transfer. Those optimizations reduce the remaining transfer tail,
but Decode still cannot continue until the required KV state is available.

The proposed path is:

```text
Prefill:
  prompt forward
    -> emit t1, t2, ... while prompt KV transfer is in flight
    -> append emitted token IDs to a monotonic handoff log
    -> stop only after Decode acknowledges the exact committed prefix

Decode:
  receive frozen prompt KV
    -> replay t1..tn with a short extend
    -> catch up with newly appended tokens
    -> atomically acquire output ownership at token boundary n
    -> generate t(n+1)
```

Token replay is useful because the token log is tiny, while the corresponding
per-layer KV tail is larger. More importantly, a short extend can process
multiple replay tokens in parallel and may catch up with token-by-token source
decoding.

## Relationship to Existing SGLang Work

This proposal is intentionally narrower than a generic adaptive PD runtime.

| Existing work | What it does | Difference in this RFC |
|---|---|---|
| Layerwise KV transfer | overlaps layer/chunk transfer with Prefill compute | emitted tail KV is reconstructed from token IDs |
| Incremental PD transfer | avoids retransmitting a Decode-resident prefix | still transfers KV; this RFC replays the live post-prefill tail |
| Optimistic Prefill | starts Prefill before bootstrap fully completes | does not keep Prefill as temporary output owner |
| Runtime role switching | changes an entire idle instance between P and D | this RFC transfers one live request |
| PD true-retraction rebootstrap (#25372) | recomputes a retracted Decode request through Prefill | provides reusable replay/commit semantics, but is not an online P-to-D catch-up |

The implementation should reuse the correctness lessons and data structures
from PD true-retraction rebootstrap instead of creating a second incompatible
token replay contract.

## Goals

1. Hide the remaining P-to-D KV handoff tail when Prefill has temporary Decode
   headroom and Decode can replay faster than Prefill emits.
2. Preserve exactly-once token streaming with an explicit output owner.
3. Preserve the standard Mooncake transfer path for immutable prompt KV.
4. Fail back to source-side continuation before commit.
5. Keep the feature default-disabled and make normal PD behavior unchanged.

## Non-goals

- Eliminating prompt KV transfer.
- Supporting different P/D model versions or KV layouts in the first version.
- Moving arbitrary sampling, grammar, or speculative-decoding state in the
  first PR.
- Providing Decode failback after ownership has committed.
- Claiming that the mode improves throughput for every workload.

## Protocol

### Request identity

Every handoff attempt is identified by:

```text
(request_id, bootstrap_room, handoff_epoch)
```

Messages from an older epoch are ignored. Retrying a failed handoff increments
the epoch.

### Monotonic token log

The Prefill owner publishes:

```text
TokenLogAppend {
  request_id
  handoff_epoch
  first_output_index
  token_ids[]
}
```

The receiver accepts an append only when `first_output_index` equals its current
log length. Duplicate appends are idempotent only when the payload matches;
gaps or conflicting payloads fail the attempt.

### Replay acknowledgement

Decode publishes:

```text
ReplayAck {
  request_id
  handoff_epoch
  replayed_output_count
}
```

`replayed_output_count` is cumulative and monotonic. It means Decode has
materialized KV for exactly that many already-emitted output tokens.

### Commit

Decode can request commit only when:

```text
replayed_output_count == Prefill.produced_output_count
```

Prefill compares the requested count against its current log length. If another
token was emitted after the ACK, commit is rejected as `BEHIND` and Decode
replays the new suffix. On success:

1. Prefill stops emitting after output index `n - 1`.
2. Prefill publishes `Commit(epoch, n)`.
3. Decode becomes the sole owner and generates output index `n`.

The client-facing stream must be owned by one side at all times. A router may
proxy both workers, but it must deduplicate by `(request_id, output_index,
handoff_epoch)` and accept data only from the current owner.

## KV Snapshot Boundary

The prompt KV transferred to Decode must be immutable while Prefill performs
bridge Decode. Paged KV allocators make the last prompt page important:
Prefill may otherwise append the first output token into the same physical page
that Mooncake is reading.

The first implementation must use one of:

1. freeze the final prompt page and allocate a fresh page for bridge Decode; or
2. copy-on-write the final partial page before the first bridge token.

This is a correctness requirement, not a performance optimization.
Until freeze/COW exists, an initial experimental path may reject
`page_size > 1` and run only with token-granular pages. It must fail closed
rather than silently enabling the handoff on paged MLA backends.

## Catch-up Admission

Let:

- `R_p` be Prefill bridge Decode tokens/s;
- `R_r` be Decode replay tokens/s;
- `T_copy` be remaining prompt KV transfer time.

At replay start the expected backlog is approximately:

```text
B0 = R_p * T_copy
```

Catch-up requires:

```text
R_r > R_p
```

and the idealized additional catch-up time is:

```text
T_catch = B0 / (R_r - R_p)
```

The runtime should use measured EWMA values, include fixed replay startup and D
queue delay, and enforce a maximum bridge-token budget. If admission fails, the
request follows normal PD handoff.

## Failure Semantics

| Failure point | Required behavior |
|---|---|
| Prompt KV transfer fails before commit | P remains owner and continues or returns the existing transfer error policy |
| Token-log transport fails | abort handoff attempt; P remains owner |
| Decode replay fails | abort handoff attempt; P remains owner |
| Stale/duplicate ACK | ignore without changing ownership |
| EOS before commit | finish on P and cancel outstanding transfer when supported |
| Commit succeeds | P must never emit another token for this epoch |
| Decode fails after commit | out of scope for v1; use existing request failure policy |

## MVP Scope

The first implementation is limited to:

- Mooncake transfer backend;
- 1P1D;
- identical P/D model, TP size and KV layout;
- greedy decoding;
- no speculative decoding;
- no multimodal input;
- feature flag default off.

The existing PD path remains the fallback.

## Proposed Implementation

### Step 1: protocol and deterministic tests

- Add a private handoff state model with epoch fencing, monotonic append/ACK and
  exact-count commit.
- Add deterministic race, duplicate, stale epoch, cancel and failure tests.
- Add a cost-model helper used by benchmarks and later admission policy.

### Step 2: restricted end-to-end path

- Preserve the Prefill request after its first token and place it in a
  bridge-decode queue while Prompt KV transfer remains in flight.
- Freeze/COW the Prompt KV boundary.
- Let Decode schedule an actual extend over token-log suffixes after Prompt KV
  commit; replay logits are discarded.
- Add atomic output-owner switch and E2E exact-output tests.

The current disaggregated Prefill loop cannot be reused unchanged: it limits
the request to one new token, parks the request in the transfer-inflight queue,
and releases its KV as soon as transfer succeeds. The experimental path needs
a bounded bridge-decode queue, must retain the source KV until commit, and must
not make generic PDMux a prerequisite.

### Step 3: production compatibility

- Counter-based sampling RNG keyed by request and output index.
- Grammar/logprob/stop-state transfer.
- Speculative decoding and multi-rank compatibility.
- Adaptive admission and observability.

## Evaluation

### Correctness

- Exact greedy-output parity with normal PD.
- No duplicate/missing token under randomized append/ACK ordering.
- Fault injection at transfer, replay and pre-commit stages.
- KV/page leak and repeated bootstrap-room reuse tests.

### Performance

Report:

- TTFT;
- first-to-second-token latency;
- P50/P95/P99 ITL;
- Prefill goodput impact;
- Prompt KV transfer latency and bytes;
- replay throughput and bridge-token count;
- GPU and NIC utilization.

Use 8K/32K/64K prompts, 1/8/32/64 replay tokens, low and saturated load, and
separate RDMA from TCP results.

## Open Questions

1. Should bridge Decode run in the Prefill scheduler event loop or through a
   small role-agnostic generation subqueue?
2. Can the existing page allocator expose a cheap freeze/COW primitive for the
   last partial prompt page?
3. Should token-log control messages reuse the bootstrap channel or use the
   router stream?
4. What is the minimum sampling state needed after the greedy MVP?
5. Should a future Mooncake intent mark the frozen Prompt KV transfer as
   latency-critical while making cancellation best-effort after early EOS?

title: [Bug] InternVL2_5-2B fails to start: 'CLIPImageProcessor' object has no attribute 'tokenizer' in get_tokenizer_from_processor
body:
### Summary

Serving `OpenGVLab/InternVL2_5-2B` crashes at startup while building the tokenizer/processor. `get_processor()` resolves the model to a bare **`CLIPImageProcessor`** (an image-only processor with no `.tokenizer` attribute), and `get_tokenizer_from_processor()` then does an unguarded `return processor.tokenizer`, raising `AttributeError`. The server never becomes ready, so any workload using this model errors out before inference.

This is **device-independent** — it is pure `transformers`/HF processor-resolution logic with no CUDA/HIP involvement.

### Reproduction

Boot a server for `OpenGVLab/InternVL2_5-2B` (e.g. `sglang.launch_server --trust-remote-code`, or a VLM MMMU eval harness). The server fails during tokenizer/processor init.

### Traceback

```
File ".../srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py", line 374, in init_tokenizer_and_processor
    _processor = _get_processor_wrapper(server_args)
File ".../srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py", line 3220, in _get_processor_wrapper
    processor = get_processor(...)
File ".../srt/utils/hf_transformers/processor.py", line 271, in get_processor
    tokenizer = get_tokenizer_from_processor(processor)
File ".../srt/utils/hf_transformers/common.py", line 529, in get_tokenizer_from_processor
    return processor.tokenizer
AttributeError: 'CLIPImageProcessor' object has no attribute 'tokenizer'
```

(The log also shows HF remote-code download of InternVL2.5's `tokenization_internlm2.py`, i.e. the tokenizer ships separately from the image processor.)

### Root cause

`get_tokenizer_from_processor` (`python/sglang/srt/utils/hf_transformers/common.py:524`) assumes any processor that is not itself a tokenizer exposes a `.tokenizer`:

```python
def get_tokenizer_from_processor(processor):
    from transformers import PreTrainedTokenizerBase
    if isinstance(processor, PreTrainedTokenizerBase):
        return processor
    return processor.tokenizer          # <-- unguarded; fails for image-only processors
```

For InternVL2.5, `AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(...)` inside `get_processor` does not return a combined multimodal processor — it returns a bare `CLIPImageProcessor`. InternVL2.5's config does not bundle a proper `AutoProcessor` that HF can assemble (its tokenizer is a separate remote-code `InternLM2` tokenizer), so `AutoProcessor` falls back to the image processor alone. `processor.tokenizer` then raises.

Notably, sglang already handles this exact case correctly in the *runtime* multimodal processor `python/sglang/srt/multimodal/processors/internvl.py` (`InternVLProcessor.__init__`, line 76):

```python
if hasattr(self._processor, "tokenizer"):
    tokenizer = self._processor.tokenizer
else:
    tokenizer = self._processor
```

but the generic startup helper `get_tokenizer_from_processor` has no equivalent guard.

### Suggested fix (for discussion)

The caller `get_tokenizer_from_processor(processor)` only receives the processor object and has no `model_path`, so it cannot re-load a tokenizer on its own. The clean place to fix is in `get_processor` (`processor.py`), where `tokenizer_name`, `revision`, and `trust_remote_code` are all in scope — mirroring the existing `_TOKENIZERS_BACKEND` reload branch immediately after line 271:

- After resolving `processor`, detect the image-only case (e.g. the object is a `BaseImageProcessor`/`*ImageProcessor` with no `tokenizer` attribute) and load the tokenizer separately via `get_tokenizer(tokenizer_name, tokenizer_mode=..., trust_remote_code=..., tokenizer_revision=...)` instead of calling `get_tokenizer_from_processor(processor)`.

Optionally, also harden `get_tokenizer_from_processor` itself with a `hasattr(processor, "tokenizer")` guard that raises a clear, actionable error (naming the model and processor class) rather than a bare `AttributeError`, so future image-only-processor models fail loudly and legibly.

### Scope / risk note

This touches core processor-resolution code shared by all image-only-processor models, so the fix should be validated against a couple of other VLMs to make sure the image-only detection doesn't mis-fire on models whose combined processor legitimately exposes `.tokenizer`.

cc VLM / multimodal processor maintainers.

title: [Bug] /v1/loads undercounts running requests with pipeline parallelism
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

On commit `d6ef68881e263812d4901f632786015005c4d050`, `num_running_reqs` returned by `/v1/loads` does not account for all active requests when pipeline parallelism (PP) is enabled. The same counting path is still present on the current `main` branch.

With 16 concurrent, long-running generation requests:

| Configuration | Active requests | `num_running_reqs` | `num_waiting_reqs` |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `TP=2, PP=4, DP=1` | 16 | `1`, `3`, or `6` | `0` |
| `TP=8, PP=1, DP=1` | 16 | `16` | `0` |

All 16 requests were accepted and remained active during the observation interval. The workload and relevant scheduling settings were unchanged between the two cases except for the TP/PP configuration.

The source path appears to explain the difference. `SchedulerLoadInquirer.get_loads()` counts only the batch returned by `get_running_batch`:

```python
num_running_reqs = len(self.get_running_batch().reqs)
```

The callback returns the mutable `Scheduler.running_batch` pointer:

```python
get_running_batch=lambda: self.running_batch
```

In the PP event loop, `self.running_batch` is rebound to one PP slot at a time:

```python
for mb_id in range(self.pp_loop_size):
    self.running_batch = self.running_mbs[mb_id]
    # ...
    self.running_mbs[mb_id] = self.running_batch
```

Since `pp_loop_size = pp_size + pp_async_batch_depth`, requests retained in the other `running_mbs` slots are not included in a snapshot that reads only `self.running_batch`.

This makes `num_running_reqs` phase-dependent in PP mode and can cause load balancers or admission controllers to overestimate available capacity.

A possible fix is to expose an explicit per-DP-rank running-request count and, in PP mode, count unique active request IDs across all `running_mbs` slots. The count should deduplicate request IDs rather than summing `mbs`, `last_mbs`, and `running_mbs`, which may contain overlapping references.

### Reproduction

1. Start SGLang on one 8-GPU node with `TP=2`, `PP=4`, `DP=1`, and `pp_async_batch_depth=0`.
2. Send 16 concurrent generation requests that remain active long enough to sample the engine. Streaming requests with a 512-token generation limit were used in this reproduction.
3. Ensure that no unrelated inference traffic is present.
4. While all 16 requests remain active, repeatedly query `/v1/loads`.
5. Observe that `num_running_reqs` reports only a subset of the 16 requests while `num_waiting_reqs=0`.
6. Repeat the same workload with `TP=8`, `PP=1`, and `DP=1`.
7. Observe that `num_running_reqs=16` remains stable until the requests complete.

Expected result after admission in both configurations:

```text
num_running_reqs=16
```

title: [Kernel] Optimize triton decoding kernels for long context
body:
We noticed the current triton decoding kernel is very slow on long context. This is due to a missing flash decoding like optimization.

## Reproduce
We test the decoding speed with a context length of 200 and 2,000.

triton backend: The decoding speed drops from 147.64 token/s to 126.41 token/s
```
$ python3 -m sglang.bench_offline_throughput --model meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct --dataset-name random --num-prompt 1 --random-input 128 --random-output 2048 --random-range 1 --attention-backend triton

[2024-11-30 05:10:04 TP0] Decode batch. #running-req: 1, #token: 234, token usage: 0.00, gen throughput (token/s): 147.64, #queue-req: 0
... 
[2024-11-30 05:10:18 TP0] Decode batch. #running-req: 1, #token: 2154, token usage: 0.00, gen throughput (token/s): 126.41, #queue-req: 0
```

flashinfer backend: The decoding speed only drops from 144.17 token/s to 143.35 token/s
```
$ python3 -m sglang.bench_offline_throughput --model meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct --dataset-name random --num-prompt 1 --random-input 128 --random-output 2048 --random-range 1

[2024-11-30 05:11:40 TP0] Decode batch. #running-req: 1, #token: 234, token usage: 0.00, gen throughput (token/s): 144.17, #queue-req: 0
...
[2024-11-30 05:11:54 TP0] Decode batch. #running-req: 1, #token: 2154, token usage: 0.00, gen throughput (token/s): 143.35, #queue-req: 0
```

## Possible solutions
We can learn from the flash decoding triton kernel from lightllm and improve the [current triton decoding kernel](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/triton_ops/decode_attention.py). Related links:
- https://github.com/ModelTC/lightllm/blob/main/lightllm/models/llama/triton_kernel/gqa_flash_decoding.py
- https://pytorch.org/blog/flash-decoding/
- https://arxiv.org/pdf/2311.01282

title: [Roadmap] Pipeline parallelism roadmap
body:
### Motivation
Pipeline parallelism is an important feature that can effectively reduce Long Context (e.g., 1M input tokens) TTFT, and it is also a promising optional parallel strategy for improving throughput.

### Pipeline Parallelism Roadmap
 - [x] Long context prefill + PD Disaggregation @ShangmingCai @XucSh @alpha-baby @whybeyoung
   - [x] Achieve almost linear scaling by doing chunked pipeline parallelism with prefill on a long context (e.g., 1M)
   - [x] Compatible with different tp degree on decode (e.g., PP8TP8 on prefill +TP4 on decode, PP8TP1 on prefill + TP8 on decode)
 - [ ] High throughput decoding @ShangmingCai  @bluecoffee8 


***
Currently, SGLang has supported Pipeline parallelism (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/5724) in the main branch, and also made it compatible with the PD Disaggregation feature (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/8846), but the implementation is not perfect, and there remains a lot of space for performance improvements. In other words, there still exist many pipeline bubbles (e.g., GPU's idle time) in the whole cluster for the current implementation.

To reduce PP bubbles, the refactoring works can be divided into the following sub-tasks:

### Refactoring the PP communication strategy

- [x] Use async send for PP stages communication in the new event loop (proposed by @alpha-baby  in #7979, adapted in the implementation of the new PP event loop by @merrymercy)
- [x] Use async micro batch buffer and async P2P communication to allow overlapping the GPU computation and CPU processing, and avoid the last PP rank staggler (done by @merrymercy)
- [x] Adapting the new event loop in the main branch @XucSh @ShangmingCai  https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/11852
- [x] Detailed profiling and performance evaluation @whybeyoung @alpha-baby
