title: [Feature][MPS] Better memory management for Apple Silicon Macs
body:
### Checklist

- [ ] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [ ] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Motivation

## Problem

On Apple Silicon Macs, GPU and CPU share Unified Memory Architecture (UMA). Several places in SGLang use `psutil.virtual_memory().total` or `.available` to determine how much memory is available for model loading and KV cache allocation on the MPS device:

- **`python/sglang/srt/utils/common.py` – `get_available_gpu_memory()`** (line 604–605):
  ```python
  elif device == "mps":
      free_gpu_memory = psutil.virtual_memory().available
  ```
- **`python/sglang/_mps_stub.py` – `get_device_properties()`** (line 131–132):
  ```python
  _cached_props = _MPSDeviceProperties(
      total_memory=psutil.virtual_memory().total,
  )
  ```
- **`python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/platforms/mps.py` – `MpsPlatform.get_available_gpu_memory()`** (line 86):
  ```python
  free_memory = psutil.virtual_memory().available
  ```

However, **Metal cannot use all of system RAM**. Apple exposes a per-device limit via [`MTLDevice.recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/mtldevice/2369280-recommendedmaxworkingsetsize), which is typically **~65–75% of total RAM** depending on the chip and macOS version. Allocating beyond this limit causes the system to start paging GPU-resident memory, leading to:

- Severe performance degradation (GPU stalls waiting for page-ins)
- System instability
- **Machine reboots** (I have personally experienced this)

This was also flagged in a code review: *"What is our OOM behavior here? (I don't want you to OOM your Mac haha, but we should have a guardrail around this)"*

## Expected Behavior

Memory reporting for MPS should be capped to Metal's recommended max working set size, not the full system RAM. This ensures SGLang never tries to allocate more memory than the GPU subsystem can safely handle.

## Reference Implementation

The [vllm-metal plugin](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-metal) already handles this correctly using MLX's API:

```python
# vllm-metal/vllm_metal/utils.py
device_info = mx.metal.device_info()
max_wired = int(device_info.get("max_recommended_working_set_size", 0))
```

It also sets the wired memory limit to prevent paging:

```python
# vllm-metal/vllm_metal/utils.py
mx.set_wired_limit(max_wired)
```

And uses this value to cap prefix cache and KV cache budgets:

```python
# vllm-metal/vllm_metal/v1/model_runner.py
device_info = mx.metal.device_info()
total = int(device_info.get("max_recommended_working_set_size", 0))
max_bytes = int(total * fraction)
```

title: [Roadmap] Prefill-Decode Disaggregation Roadmap (2026 Q2)
body:
## Motivation
Prefill-Decode Disaggregation has been an important and widely adopted feature for LLM inference production.
Although we have almost made it compatible with different model architectures, all parallel strategies, and almost all advanced features, there are always new models/features coming up, which we also want to support in PD mode.

This issue will act as a roadmap or a tracker for those who are interested in the latest progress of this feature (at least it will include some related experimental features we will conduct in 2026 Q2).

## Interface refactoring
- [x] Support query dp rank from bootstrap server, which allows us to achieve better DP load balance https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/19168
- [x] Refactor PD decode KV receiver bootstrap for better readability and bugfix https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/21680 https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/21299  @weireweire 


## Advanced feature and usage
 - [x] Context parallel compatibility after refactor https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/19504 https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/19765
 - [x] GPU staging buffer for accelerating heterogeneous TP KV transfer https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/19890 @YAMY1234 
   - For MHA/GQA models, there are many small pieces of KVCache transfer for a heterogeneous TP setup of PD, which will slow down the transfer process. This feature will gather the KV heads at prefill, then send the kvcache to decode by uniting them as a large piece through a ring-based staging buffer (really helpful for GB platforms).
 - [x] Compatibility with Hisparse https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/21591 @hzh0425 
   - This feature will allow us to send kvcache from prefill HBM to decode host memory when enabling hisparse for NSA models (DeepSeek V3.2/GLM 5). It will help us to get a much bigger batch size on the decode side since we only keep the topk sparse KVCache in HBM, and make all other KVCache stored in the host memory.
 - [x] Prefill send delta KVCache while Decode fetch prefix from Hicache for agentic use cases https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/26227 @hzh0425  
 - [x] Decode RadixCache https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/19746 @ishandhanani 
   - For agentic scenarios, decode can now use radix cache to reuse shared prefixes and request only the delta KV from prefill instead of transferring the full prefix on every turn.
 - [x] Optimistic prefill for better TTFT https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/26780 @cctry 
   -  the prefill worker may start computing before bootstrap is fully finalized. If bootstrap completes in time, the request proceeds normally. If bootstrap is still pending or fails, the request retries or falls back to the normal bootstrap path.
 - [ ] Better compatibility with Spec decode: support heterogeneous target/draft model architectures https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/20698
   - This feature will allow us to use different draft architectures from target models when enabling speculative decoding or MTP (specforge/torchspec might need it).
 - [ ] Layerwise KVCache transfer https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/19931 @zhangxiaolei123456 @UNIDY2002 https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23515
 - [ ] Support Prefill PP + MTP for PD Disaggregation mode
 - [ ] Runtime role transitions https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28403

## Routing strategy enhancement for agentic serving
 - [x] Support heterogeneous instances in the same (Prefill/Decode) pool while simultaneously enabling seamless pairing with heterogeneous (Decode/Prefill) instances. (We have supported this from the very beginning.)
 - [ ] Support extended roles in RBG, (long context prefill instance, short context prefill instance, long context decode instance, short context decode instance) @cheyang Do we support this now?
 - [ ] Support session-based load-balanced-aware routing strategy in sglang router @Kangyan-Zhou @whybeyoung 

## EPD Performance / Architecture / Observability Enhancements
 - [ ] EPD Enhancements Roadmap https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/24945 @Abatom 

## New model support:
 - [x] Qwen3.5: hybrid linear attention support PP+PD https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/21448 https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/19254 @zhangxiaolei123456 @sufeng-buaa 

More will be added. Feel free to comment any feature requests down here.

title: [Roadmap]  — SGLang Simulator
body: ### Motivation As LLM inference scales, tuning performance (TTFT, TPOT, throughput) demands exploring a vast space of models × hardware × engine configurations × cache strategies. Traditional benchmarking on real GPU clusters is expensive, slow to iterate, and hard to reproduce — making it impractical to efficiently evaluate the many possible deployment configurations. **SGLang Simulator** is a CPU-based simulation system that intercepts SGLang at runtime, replacing GPU computation with hardware-aware latency prediction. It is **zero-GPU, high-fidelity, non-invasive, fast, and supports production trace replay**. ### Architecture SGLang Simulator intercepts SGLang through a **two-level hook system** (`builtins.__build_class__` + `sys.meta_path`) without any source modification: + **Hook Layer** — class hooks + module hook that replace Scheduler, ModelRunner, TokenizerManager, HiCacheController, RadixCache, StorageBackend, and GPU kernel loading + **Time Prediction** — AIConfigurator computes per-batch latency from hardware specs and operator profiling data + **Mock Memory Pools** — MockTokenToKVPool / MockTokenToKVPoolHost / MockHiCacheStorage track KV cache allocation without real memory The benchmark client talks to the mock server via the same HTTP API as real SGLang, and output metrics are fully compatible with `sglang bench_serving`. ### Accuracy Validated against real SGLang deployments on **H20** GPUs. All prediction errors are below **5% MAPE**. **Qwen3-8B on H20** | Case | Mean TTFT | Mean TPOT | Mean ITL | Input Throughput | Duration | Prefix Hit Ratio | | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | | no_cache | 3.42% | 1.64% | 1.78% | 1.41% | 1.39% | 0.0% | | L1 | 4.15% | 3.47% | 3.54% | 2.4% | 2.33% | 0.04% | | L2 | 2.38% | 4.05% | 4.07% | 2.35% | 2.29% | 0.0% | **Qwen3-32B-FP8 on H20** | Case | Mean TTFT | Mean TPOT | Mean ITL | Input Throughput | Duration | Prefix Hit Ratio | | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | | no_cache | 2.77% | 0.58% | 0.52% | 0.52% | 0.51% | 0.00% | | L1 | 2.40% | 1.03% | 1.02% | 1.04% | 1.03% | 0.04% | | L2 | 3.05% | 1.11% | 1.02% | 1.13% | 1.12% | 0.00% | > `no_cache` = no KV cache hits; `L1` = GPU HBM hits only; `L2` = HBM + host DRAM hits. Error metric: MAPE. > ### Roadmap + Current Support @zhuzi-z @LinSiyuan814 @littlefatfat PR: #33824 #22250 - [x] Validated models: Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-32B-FP8 (< 5% MAPE) - [x] Hardware: all platforms supported by [AIConfigurator](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/aiconfigurator/tree/main/src/aiconfigurator/systems/data) - [x] HiCache: `--disable-radix-cache` (no cache), default (L1 HBM), `--enable-hierarchical-cache` (L2 DRAM), `--hicache-storage-backend file` (L3 Disk) - [x] Simulation modes: BLOCKING (real-time) / OFFLINE (10–1000x speedup) - [x] Production trace collection & replay + Model & Hardware Expansion - [x] GLM5, DeepSeek v3.2, Qwen3.5, MoE models, multimodal models — primarily via collaboration with [AIConfigurator](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/aiconfigurator) for operator profiling data + HybridRadixCache Support + Multi-Instance Simulation - [ ] PD (Prefill-Decode) disaggregation with data transfer modeling - [ ] Integration with SGLang Gateway for request dispatching: Random, Round Robin, Power of Two, Cache-Aware + Accuracy Improvements - [ ] Enable zero-overhead batch schedule simulation - [ ] HiCache management under complex workloads (concurrent L2 writeback and eviction) + Simulation Speed Optimization - [ ] High-efficiency latency predictor - [ ] Inference iteration compression (reduce decode-stage `TimePredictor` invocations) + Miscellaneous - [ ] Micro-batch parallelism (dp-attention, two-batch overlap) - [ ] `bench_serving` concurrency mode support - [ ] Additional `--hicache-storage-backend` and `--prefetch-policy` options - [ ] "best_effort" prefetch strategies support ### Related resources _No response_

title: [Feature] Free-Threaded Python (3.14t / nogil) Support for SGLang
body:
## Motivation

CPython 3.13 introduced an experimental free-threaded build (PEP 703) that removes the Global Interpreter Lock (GIL). CPython 3.14t is the first release where this build is stable enough for production use, and the ecosystem of packages with free-threading wheels is growing rapidly.

vLLM has demonstrated ([vllm-project/vllm#28762](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/28762)) that a large-scale CUDA-accelerated serving framework can run under a free-threaded interpreter. SGLang shares a similar dependency footprint and architecture. Enabling free-threaded support would unlock true CPU-level parallelism in the Python layer — benefiting the tokenizer manager, scheduler, HTTP server, disaggregation controller, and other asyncio + thread-pool components that today serialize behind the GIL.

This RFC tracks the dependency readiness, identifies the internal code changes needed, and proposes a phased plan to make `uv pip install sglang` work out of the box in a clean Python 3.14t environment on Linux x86-64 (CPU and CUDA).

## Background

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **3.14t** | The free-threaded (no-GIL) CPython 3.14 build, identified by the `t` suffix in the ABI tag (`cp314t`). |
| **cp314** | The regular (with-GIL) CPython 3.14 build. |
| **Stable ABI** | A subset of the CPython C API that is ABI-compatible across Python versions (PEP 384). Extensions built against the stable ABI only need one wheel per platform, not one per Python minor version. |
| **`Py_GIL_DISABLED`** | The compile-time macro set in free-threaded builds. C extensions must check this to use thread-safe reference counting and data structures. |

### Why 3.14t and not 3.13t?

- CPython 3.14t itself is significantly more stable than 3.13t.
- Key packages (cffi, aiohttp, etc.) support 3.14t but will not back-port to 3.13t.
- PyTorch 2.10.0 (January 2026) will ship full cp314t wheels; PyTorch 2.9.0 already has "preview" wheels.

### Prerequisites

Free-threaded Python support depends on SGLang first supporting regular Python 3.14 (with-GIL). This RFC assumes that prerequisite is met or being tracked separately.

## Dependency Audit

The following tables categorize every SGLang dependency with compiled (C/C++/Rust/CUDA) code by its current free-threading readiness. Pure-Python packages are omitted — they work automatically.

### Core Dependencies (from `pyproject.toml` `dependencies`)

| Package | Current Version | cp314t Wheels on PyPI | Builds from Source | Tracking Issue | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `torch` | 2.9.1 | Preview (2.9.0); full in 2.10.0 | Yes | — | Core dependency. 2.10.0 (Jan 2026) is the target. |
| `torchaudio` | 2.9.1 | Follows torch | Yes | — | |
| `torchvision` | latest | Follows torch | Yes | — | |
| `torchao` | 0.9.0 | Follows torch | TBD | — | |
| `sglang-kernel` | 0.4.1 | ❌ No | ❌ Needs work | — | **SGLang-owned**. Uses stable ABI (cp310). Needs `Py_GIL_DISABLED` audit. See below. |
| `flash-attn-4` | ≥4.0.0b4 | ❌ No | TBD | — | CUDA extension. |
| `flashinfer_python` | 0.6.7.post2 | ❌ No | Resolved |https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/1687| Uses stable ABI; fix was to not use limited API with free-threaded Python. |
| `flashinfer_cubin` | 0.6.7.post2 | ❌ No | TBD | — | Binary CUDA kernels, may need rebuild only. |
| `cuda-python` | 12.9 | TBD | TBD | — | NVIDIA-maintained. |
| `xgrammar` | 0.1.32 | ✅ Yes (≥0.1.31) | ✅ Yes | [xgrammar#500](https://github.com/mlc-ai/xgrammar/issues/500) | Full support. |
| `llguidance` | ≥0.7.11 | ✅ Yes (≥1.6.0) | ✅ Yes | [llguidance#256](https://github.com/guidance-ai/llguidance/issues/256) | Full support. |
| `msgspec` | latest | ✅ Yes (≥0.20.0) | ✅ Yes | — | Full support. |
| `outlines` | 0.1.11 | TBD (outlines-core) | ✅ Yes | [outlines-core#248](https://github.com/dottxt-ai/outlines-core/issues/248) | Depends on outlines-core. |
| `sentencepiece` | latest | TBD | TBD | — | C++ extension. |
| `tiktoken` | latest | TBD | TBD | — | Rust extension. |
| `orjson` | latest | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes | — | Rust extension, typically early adopter. |
| `pyzmq` | ≥25.1.2 | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes | — | |
| `numpy` | latest | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes | — | |
| `scipy` | latest | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes | — | |
| `aiohttp` | latest | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes | — | Supports 3.14t. |
| `pybase64` | latest | TBD | TBD | — | C extension. |
| `setproctitle` | latest | TBD | TBD | — | C extension. |
| `nvidia-ml-py` | latest | Pure Python | N/A | — | |
| `pillow` | latest | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes | — | |
| `pydantic` | latest | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes | — | Rust-compiled core. |
| `uvloop` | latest | TBD | TBD | — | C extension (libuv). Critical for asyncio perf. |
| `soundfile` | 0.13.1 | TBD | TBD | — | CFFI-based. |
| `compressed-tensors` | latest | TBD | TBD | — | |
| `quack-kernels` | ≥0.3.0 | ❌ No | TBD | — | CUDA extension. |
| `kernels` | latest | TBD | TBD | — | |
| `smg-grpc-servicer` | ≥0.5.0 | TBD | TBD | — | gRPC bindings. |

### Optional Dependencies (diffusion, ray, tracing)

| Package | cp314t Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `ray` | ❌ No 3.14 support at all | Made optional in vLLM. SGLang already has it as optional (`[ray]`). Not blocking. |
| `opencv-python-headless` | ❌ No | Diffusion extra only. Tracking: [opencv/opencv#27933](https://github.com/opencv/opencv/issues/27933), build fix PR: [opencv-python#1051](https://github.com/opencv/opencv-python/pull/1051). |
| `xformers` | ✅ Yes (≥0.0.35) | Resolved by removing CPython C API dependency. |

### SGLang-Owned Compiled Components

| Component | Language | Build System | Free-Threading Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sgl-kernel` | C++17 / CUDA | scikit-build-core + CMake | ❌ Uses stable ABI (`cp310`). Needs `Py_GIL_DISABLED` audit and potentially per-version builds. |
| `cpp_radix_tree` (radix cache) | C++ | pybind11 (torch extension) | ❌ Needs thread-safety audit. |
| `ngram_corpus_ffi` | C++ | pybind11 (torch extension) | ❌ Needs thread-safety audit. |
| `hf3fs_utils` | C++ | pybind11 (torch extension) | ⚠️ Uses `py::gil_scoped_release`. Needs `Py_GIL_DISABLED` review. |
| `sgl-model-gateway` (router) | Rust (PyO3) | maturin | ✅ PyO3 has free-threading support. |
| `multimodal_gen` CUDA kernels | C++ / CUDA | setuptools | ❌ Needs audit. |

## Internal Code Audit

### GIL-Dependent Patterns

The following patterns in SGLang's Python code rely on the GIL for correctness and must be reviewed:

1. **Explicit GIL assumptions.** `staging_handler.py` documents: *"CPython GIL guarantees ordering"* for flag visibility between threads. Under free-threading, this needs an explicit memory barrier or `threading.Event`.

2. **`py::gil_scoped_release` in C++ extensions.** `hf3fs_utils.cpp` uses `py::gil_scoped_release` to release the GIL during memcpy. Under free-threading, pybind11's `gil_scoped_release` is a no-op, but the surrounding data structures must be thread-safe without the GIL.

3. **Shared mutable state across threads.** The following areas use thread pools or daemon threads that share mutable Python objects:
   - `TokenizerManager`: `ThreadPoolExecutor` for tokenization with shared request queues
   - `CacheController`: background threads for cache management
   - `KVEvents`: daemon threads for ZMQ event distribution
   - `weight_utils.py`: multi-threaded safetensors loading with shared iterators

4. **Module-level mutable globals.** Several modules use module-level dicts/lists as registries (model registry, format registry, etc.). Under free-threading, concurrent imports or first-access initialization can race.

5. **asyncio + ThreadPoolExecutor interaction.** `run_coroutine_threadsafe` and `call_soon_threadsafe` are used throughout the disaggregation layer. These are asyncio-safe but the callbacks they schedule may access shared state without locks.

### Thread-Safety Classification

| Risk Level | Pattern | Example Locations | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **High** | GIL-ordering assumptions | `staging_handler.py:192` | Replace with `threading.Event` or `atomics` |
| **High** | Shared mutable containers across threads | `weight_utils.py` (iterator sharing) | Add `threading.Lock` or use `queue.Queue` |
| **Medium** | Module-level mutable registries | Model/format registries | Use `threading.Lock` for lazy init |
| **Medium** | `concurrent.futures` with shared closures | `async_dynamic_batch_tokenizer.py` | Audit closure captures |
| **Low** | `py::gil_scoped_release` in C++ | `hf3fs_utils.cpp` | Verify data is not shared with Python threads |
| **Low** | Pure asyncio code (single-threaded event loop) | HTTP server, tokenizer manager main loop | Safe by design (single-threaded) |

## Proposed Plan

### Phase 0: Python 3.14 (with-GIL) Support

**Goal:** `pip install sglang` works on regular Python 3.14.

### Phase 1: Dependency Readiness Tracking

**Goal:** All dependencies are installable in a 3.14t environment.

### Phase 2: sgl-kernel Free-Threading Support

**Goal:** `sglang-kernel` builds and passes tests under 3.14t.

### Phase 3: Internal C++ Extension Audit

**Goal:** All SGLang-owned C++ extensions are thread-safe without the GIL.

### Phase 4: Python-Level Thread-Safety Fixes

**Goal:** SGLang's Python code does not rely on GIL for correctness.

### Phase 5: CI and Release

**Goal:** Free-threaded builds are tested and released.

### Phase 6: Performance Validation and Optimization

**Goal:** Quantify the benefit of free-threading for SGLang workloads.

## References

- [vLLM free-threaded Python tracking issue (vllm-project/vllm#18937)](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/18937)
- [PEP 703 – Making the Global Interpreter Lock Optional in CPython](https://peps.python.org/pep-0703/)
- [CPython 3.14 free-threaded howto](https://docs.python.org/3.14/howto/free-threading-python.html)
- [PyTorch free-threading support](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/130249)

title: [Roadmap] Extended Adapter support for Multimodal LLM
body:
Current Status and motivation
------------------------------------
Only LoRA adapter has been supported. But for diffusion models and multimodal there are also popular LoKr adapters and other.
Need to support various type of adapter for SGLang for diffusion  and multimodal.

Design 
------------------------------------
Adapters have been applied for layers with commutative property. $`func(X, W + \Delta w) = func(X, W) + func(X, \Delta w)`$
BaseLayerWithLoRA replace with BaseTunedLayer


```mermaid
classDiagram

class BaseTunedLayer
BaseTunedLayer: +required_adapter_type
BaseTunedLayer: +forward(Tensor)

class Adapter
Adapter: +Enum adapterType
Adapter: +forward(Tensor)

class LoRAAdapter
LoRAAdapter: +forward(Tensor)
LoRAAdapter: +forwardBatch(Tensor)

class LoKrAdapter
LoKrAdapter: +forward(Tensor)

class Mergeable
Mergeable: +can_merge()
Mergeable: +merge_weights()
Mergeable: +unmerge_weights()

class Shardable
Shardable: +slice_weights()

class Iterateable
Iterateable: +forward(Tensor)

class BatchIterateable
BatchIterateable: +forwardBatch(Tensor)

Mergeable<|.. LoRAAdapter
Shardable<|.. LoRAAdapter
Iterateable<|.. LoRAAdapter
BatchIterateable<|.. LoRAAdapter

Mergeable<|.. LoKrAdapter
Shardable<|.. LoKrAdapter
Iterateable<|.. LoKrAdapter

Adapter <|-- LoRAAdapter
Adapter <|-- LoKrAdapter
BaseTunedLayer o-- Adapter 
BaseTunedLayer .. Mergeable
BaseTunedLayer .. Shardable
BaseTunedLayer .. Iterateable
BaseTunedLayer .. BatchIterateable
```

Cuda Graph Design 
------------------------------------
Currently LoRA support for Multimodal is used torch native api and doesn't use custom operator 
There 3 possible implementation multi-typed adapters support:
1. One adapter per layer: validate used adapters per layer, if for one layer has been used only one adapter type, then generate 
2. One adapter type per batch: In case different adapter types, generate and call graph also by the adapter type, not only batch size
3. Many adapter types per batch: custom operators or graph should contain all possible adapters

Features
------------------------------------
- Adapter type detection. Some adapter doesn't have valid adapter_config.json files and store in Safetensor format.
  For example, Ostris AI-Toolkit framework doesn't provide adapter_config.json. [Link: ai-toolkit](https://github.com/ostris/ai-toolkit.git)
- Generalize config settings for general type adapter.
- Cuda support for different adapter types.
- Multi-types multi-adapters support

title: [RFC] Agent-Aware KV Cache Phase 1 for Agentic Workloads
body:
## Summary

This RFC proposes Phase 1 of agent-aware KV cache support in SGLang.

The goal of this phase is to add a minimal, backward-compatible metadata path for agentic workloads so workflow information can flow from the API layer into runtime requests and KV cache nodes, and optionally affect radix cache eviction.

This is intentionally a foundation/prototype phase, not a full workflow-aware cache system.

## Motivation

Current KV cache eviction policies such as LRU, LFU, and SLRU treat requests mostly independently. That works well for standard chat/completion workloads, but it misses reuse opportunities in agentic workflows, where requests often share:

- repeated prompt prefixes across planner/tool/worker steps
- parent/child step relationships
- short-term reuse after tool calls
- workflow-level TTL or reuse intent

Without workflow-aware signals, cache entries that are likely to be reused by upcoming steps may be evicted too early.

## Proposal

Phase 1 introduces:

- an optional `agent_hints` field in OpenAI-compatible requests
- propagation of `agent_hints` through the internal request pipeline
- lightweight workflow DAG tracking in the scheduler
- radix cache node annotation with workflow metadata
- a new optional radix eviction policy: `agent_aware`

Initial `agent_hints` fields include:

- `workflow_id`
- `agent_id`
- `step_id`
- `step_index`
- `total_steps`
- `parent_step_id`
- `children_step_ids`
- `tool_name`
- `expected_tool_duration_ms`
- `cache_ttl_ms`
- `shared_prefix_hash`
- `reuse_hint`

## Scope

Phase 1 is intended to cover:

- request schema support
- metadata plumbing
- scheduler-side workflow tracking
- cache node metadata annotation
- a prototype workflow-aware eviction strategy

Phase 1 does **not** attempt to fully solve:

- `shared_prefix_hash`-driven reuse
- HiCache / storage-layer metadata inheritance
- cross-process workflow coordination
- production-tuned scoring for all agent topologies

## Backward Compatibility

- `agent_hints` is optional
- existing clients do not need to change
- existing eviction policies continue to work unchanged
- the new behavior is opt-in

## Testing

Expected validation for Phase 1:

- schema tests for `agent_hints`
- propagation tests from API request to internal request objects
- workflow DAG tests for step registration and distance computation
- radix cache node annotation tests
- eviction ordering tests for `agent_aware`
- backward-compat tests when `agent_hints` is omitted

How to Run
Start SGLang with the new eviction policy:
```
curl http://127.0.0.1:30000/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "default",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hello"}],
    "agent_hints": {
      "workflow_id": "wf-1",
      "agent_id": "planner",
      "step_id": "step-1",
      "children_step_ids": ["step-2"],
      "cache_ttl_ms": 60000,
      "reuse_hint": "keep"
    }
  }'
```

Prototype validation already exists with dedicated unit tests for the metadata path.

## Open Questions

- Should `shared_prefix_hash` remain a hint, or become a stronger reuse primitive in a later phase?
- Should TTL be a hard protection or only a ranking signal?
- How should workflow-aware metadata eventually interact with HiCache and storage backends?
- What observability should be added next: workflow hit rate, protected eviction count, step-distance metrics?

## Requested Feedback

Feedback is especially useful on:

- the proposed `agent_hints` schema
- whether scheduler-local DAG tracking is the right Phase 1 boundary
- whether `agent_aware` should land as an experimental eviction policy first
- what should be included in Phase 2

title: [Feature] Investigate CUTLASS 4.6 dynamic Epilogue Fusions and IKET profiling
body:
### Checklist

- [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Motivation

NVIDIA recently released CUTLASS 4.6 (https://github.com/NVIDIA/cutlass/pull/3362). Here are two features that are interesting:

1. Dynamic Epilogue Fusions (EFC): The new Operator API allows defining custom epilogues (such as specific activation and bias combinations) as plain Python functions. The API parses the Python AST and JIT-compiles it directly into the CuTe DSL GEMM kernel via MLIR. We can directly integrate it with our own kernels. (https://github.com/NVIDIA/cutlass/blob/main/operators/examples/002_bring_your_own_kernel.ipynb)

2. In-Kernel-Event-Tracing (IKET) Profiler: CUTLASS 4.6 introduces run-iket, an experimental profiler that allows placing markers and timing ranges inside CuTe DSL kernels. This generates a Perfetto-compatible timeline of intra-kernel activities, which can help when profiling asynchronous, warp-specialized persistent kernels. This might help us further optimize Cute-DSL kernels.

title: [Bug] launch_server hangs forever with no error when /tmp is noexec (NUMA wrapper script cannot be executed)
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

On a host where `/tmp` is mounted `noexec` (common in managed containers and hardened images), `sglang.launch_server` **hangs forever with no error**:

1. With NUMA binding enabled (the default, `SGLANG_NUMA_BIND_V2`), `configure_subprocess` writes a wrapper script `exec numactl <args> python "$@"` to a **hard-coded** `/tmp/sglang_temp_file_<ts>_<rand>.sh` (`_create_numactl_executable` in `srt/utils/numa_utils.py`) and makes it the multiprocessing spawn executable.
2. The kernel refuses to execute it (`Permission denied`), so the scheduler and detokenizer processes die immediately, before Python starts, leaving **no traceback in the log**.
3. The launcher never notices: it keeps waiting for the children to report readiness. The children stay as zombies (`<defunct>`) and the server never comes up and never exits.

Two things make this hard to diagnose:

- `_probe_numactl_args` dry-runs `numactl <args> true`, which succeeds, but it never checks that the *wrapper script itself* can be executed from its location.
- The path ignores `TMPDIR` / `tempfile.gettempdir()`, so pointing `TMPDIR` at an executable directory does not help. Only `SGLANG_NUMA_BIND_V2=0` works around it. (#25314 proposed an env var for this directory but was closed.)

### Expected behavior

- The launcher should fail fast with a clear error if a scheduler/detokenizer subprocess exits during startup, instead of waiting forever.
- The NUMA wrapper should be written somewhere executable (e.g. honor `TMPDIR` / `tempfile`, or fall back to no NUMA binding with a warning when the wrapper cannot be executed). Probing by actually executing the wrapper once would catch this.

### Reproduction

Any model; the failure happens before model loading.

```bash
# /tmp mounted noexec, e.g. inside a container:
#   tmpfs on /tmp type tmpfs (rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,relatime,inode64)
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path <model> --port 8000
```

Log stops right after the spawn-executable switch and nothing else is printed:

```
[2026-09-21 18:33:27] Compiled-kernel caches now live under SGLANG_CACHE_DIR (...)
[2026-09-21 18:33:28] mp.set_executable .../.venv/bin/python -> /tmp/sglang_temp_file_1790015608.0013747_6994139.sh (script='#!/bin/sh\nexec numactl --cpunodebind=0 --membind=0 .../.venv/bin/python "$@"')
```

Minutes later the children are zombies and the parent is still waiting:

```
$ pstree -p <launch_server pid>
python(128137)-+-python(128376)   # <defunct>
               |-python(128377)   # <defunct>
               ...
$ /tmp/sglang_temp_file_1790015608.0013747_6994139.sh -c "print(1)"
bash: /tmp/sglang_temp_file_1790015608.0013747_6994139.sh: Permission denied
$ numactl --cpunodebind=0 --membind=0 true; echo $?
0
```

Workarounds: `SGLANG_NUMA_BIND_V2=0` (setting `TMPDIR` does not help because the path is hard-coded).

### Environment

- sglang 0.5.20 (the relevant code is unchanged on `main` as of today), torch 2.13.0+cu130, flashinfer 0.6.18
- 1x NVIDIA B200, driver 580.95.05, CUDA 13.1, Ubuntu 24.04 container (cgroup v2, 8 CPUs)
- `/tmp`: `tmpfs (rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec)`

### Describe the bug

I noticed that `flashinfer` is gated again in [srt/layers/attention/attention_registry.py#L391](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/attention_registry.py#L391).

I encountered this while running [verl's Delta Weight Sync example](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/blob/main/verl/experimental/one_step_off_policy/shell/grpo_0.6b_gsm8k_fsdp2_sglang_delta_sharded_2_6.sh) with `sglang==0.5.17` and `torch==2.11.0+cu130` on **`sm_103` Blackwell GPUs (more precisely, B300)**.

title: [Feature][weight-cache] Support DeepSeek-V4-Flash MXFP4 IPC loading
body:
## Motivation

Track DeepSeek-V4-Flash MXFP4 support under #33522, following #39762.

In our earlier 8× H200 / TP=8 tests, daemon preloading succeeded, but client loading failed with 172 shape/dtype mismatches across 43 MoE layers. Both standalone and engine-managed daemon modes showed the same failure.

#39762 concerns rejecting unsupported configurations early. This issue tracks enabling safe IPC loading.

## Gaps to address

1. **Final tensor layouts:** the client must accept validated, backend-specific post-processed MXFP4 layouts instead of requiring checkpoint-time shapes/dtypes.

2. **Safe post-load lifecycle:** #38306 introduces post-load handling, but calling `post_load_weights()` alone may not be safe for DSV4. For example, `ape_converted` is client-local state; failing to restore it could cause an already-transformed APE tensor to be transformed again through shared storage.

3. **Runtime state outside registered tensors:** backend-owned tensors such as `_swiglu_limit_tensor` also need reconstruction on the correct device.

The layout mismatch was reproduced on GPUs. Items 2–3 are follow-up risks identified from code inspection, not yet GPU-validated failures.

## Suggested approach

Start with the H200 / FlashInfer CUTLASS MXFP4 path:

- Extend existing IPC metadata with the layout identity and required post-processing state.
- Validate and bind the daemon's final tensors.
- Restore client-local runtime state without rerunning weight-mutating transformations.

This could build on the manifest and post-map rebuild work in #33522, alongside #38306.

## Validation

- Tensor/layout parity and inference accuracy against ordinary loading.
- Successful client restart while reusing resident weights.
- Unchanged daemon-owned weight hashes after client attach and inference.

I have 8× H200 available and can help run these tests. Is this a reasonable initial scope, and is anyone already working on the DSV4-specific reconstruction path?

title: [Bug] DFLASH draft layout is assumed, not validated: anchor-first checkpoints shift every position silently
body:
# [Bug] DFLASH draft layout is assumed, not validated: anchor-first checkpoints shift every position silently

### Summary

`DFLASH` draft checkpoints carry an implicit block-layout convention, and SGLang assumes
one of the two conventions in common use without checking which one a checkpoint was
trained with. A checkpoint trained with the *anchor-as-first-prediction* layout — where
every position in the block predicts — is served without any error and produces draft
tokens shifted by one position. The server reports healthy; acceptance collapses to
roughly `1.0` (only the anchor/bonus token survives).

Isolated on a Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (`Qwen4Exp`) target with the official DeepSpec drafter
`dflash_block7_qwen38_flash_next` on 8×A800 (SM80): **accept length @ 4-token window =
1.0621** over 47,411 verify steps. The same checkpoint's card reports a *served* accepted
length of **2.7562 at block 4** and **2.9837 at its native block 7** under vLLM, where the
layout it was trained for is honoured. No warning, no assertion here — the service starts
and answers normally, at a fraction of that acceptance.

### The two conventions

| | anchor-as-first-prediction | 1+N (SGLang's assumption) |
|---|---|---|
| block positions | all `K` positions predict | position 0 is the seeded anchor/bonus token; positions `1..N` are the drafts |
| marker, when present | `sample_from_anchor: true` | `sample_from_anchor: false` |
| drafter | DeepSpec `dflash_block7_qwen38_flash_next` | speculators-format drafts |

The marker is a **speculators** config field (`DFlashSpeculatorConfig.sample_from_anchor`,
default `False`; `DSparkSpeculatorConfig` defaults `True`). The convention also determines the
token count: `False` → `block_size - 1` speculative tokens, `True` → `block_size`.

**It is not a reliable discriminator across the ecosystem, which is part of the problem.**
The official anchor-first checkpoint above carries **no `sample_from_anchor` field at all** —
neither top-level nor inside its `dflash_config`; its config exposes `num_anchors: 512` and
nothing else about the layout. So a marker-based check would read the sglang default and wave
exactly the checkpoint that mis-serves through.

**But the layout *is* declared — under a name SGLang does not read.** The upstream serving repo
ships a config override (the README notes the checkpoint's own `config.json` "does not carry the
`dflash_config` block the engine reads"). That override's `dflash_config` contains:

```json
"dflash_config": {
  "target_layer_ids": [3, 15, 23, 35, 43],
  "mask_token_id": 248077,
  "use_aux_hidden_state": true,
  "causal": false,
  "query_zero_predicts_next": true
}
```

`query_zero_predicts_next: true` is a direct, explicit statement of the anchor-first convention.
SGLang's `DFlashDraftConfig` (`speculative/dflash_utils.py:529-548`) has no field for it and
`parse_dflash_draft_config` never reads it — a tree-wide search for the identifier returns zero
hits. So the declaration exists, is unambiguous, and is silently dropped.

> **Inference, not a confirmed contract.** I am reading `query_zero_predicts_next` as "the
> query at position 0 predicts the token *after* the anchor", i.e. the anchor-first layout —
> that is what the field name says and it is consistent with the extra `block_size`-th
> prediction the layout implies, but I have not verified it against the trainer source and am
> labelling it as a hypothesis rather than a spec. If the maintainers confirm the field's
> meaning, a check on it is the natural fix; if not, the layout still has to be established
> some other way. It should not be shipped as a hard gate on my reading alone.

### Where SGLang assumes 1+N

`DFlashWorkerV2` slices the draft's hidden states to drop position 0:

```python
# python/sglang/srt/speculative/dflash_worker_v2.py:158-160
# draft tokens are block positions 1: (pos 0 is the seeded bonus token)
bs = hidden_states.shape[0] // self.block_size
hs = hidden_states.view(bs, self.block_size, -1)[:, 1:, :].reshape(
    -1, hidden_states.shape[-1]
)
```

The same slice appears in the in-worker draft path (`dflash_worker_v2.py:278`,
`# pos 0 = anchor`) and in the selector path (`:1378`, `:2572`).

A checkpoint trained anchor-first produces `K` meaningful predictions per block, but only
`K-1` of them are read, and each one is read from the *wrong* slot — a uniform off-by-one
across every draft position.

### The layout field is already parsed — just not for this

`dflash_utils.py` already reads `sample_from_anchor` off the draft config:

```python
# python/sglang/srt/speculative/dflash_utils.py:504-507
sample_from_anchor = dflash_config.get(
    "sample_from_anchor", _cfg_get(config, "sample_from_anchor", True)
)
return sample_from_anchor is False
```

Two things follow from that snippet. First, the field is already parsed at config-parse time.
Second, **its default is inverted for this purpose**: `_cfg_get(..., True)` reads the sglang
default as `True`, but the speculators default for the DFlash family is `False`. So "absent"
means *opposite* things to the two sides, which is why absence cannot be treated as safety.

Today the read is confined to `is_nemotron_35_draft_config` (`dflash_utils.py:470`), and even
there it is one of six conjunctive conditions identifying one specific published checkpoint —
it is not a general layout gate. The value is available on the DFLASH path and simply not
consulted there.

### Suggested fix (fail fast, matching vLLM)

vLLM's DFlash speculator raises on this exact layout
(`ValueError: sample_from_anchor=True is not supported for DFlash`). SGLang currently does
something worse than raising: it serves, silently, at ~1.0 acceptance.

Three options, in increasing order of how much they depend on my unverified reading above:

1. **Minimal, no inference needed for the check itself:** fail fast on the checkpoints that *do*
   declare a layout — anything SGLang can currently see (`sample_from_anchor` where present).
   Wiring up `query_zero_predicts_next` would extend this to the official checkpoint, but **that
   rests on my unverified reading of the field (hypothesis, see above) — it should only be
   treated as a gate once the semantics are confirmed.** As it stands this option would not have
   caught the official checkpoint, because SGLang reads neither field today; it is a strict
   improvement over the current state and commits to nothing uncertain.
2. **Require an explicit declaration** on the DFLASH draft config going forward, and refuse to
   serve a checkpoint that omits it. Catches everything, including this checkpoint — at the
   cost of breaking checkpoints that are in the wild today.
3. **Honour the layout** — read all `K` positions when the checkpoint is anchor-first. The most
   useful outcome, and a bounded change at the four slice sites above, but it is downstream of
   the layout actually being established.

Either way the checkpoint stops being served at a wrong-but-plausible acceptance rate.

The design constraint worth flagging: **an explicit check on `sample_from_anchor` alone would
not have caught this checkpoint** — it declares neither that field nor `speculative_tokens`
(the identifier does not appear anywhere in its config). Whatever is chosen has to *establish*
the layout rather than default it.

Two things I'd be glad to be corrected on: whether `query_zero_predicts_next` means what I read
it to mean, and whether there is a better discriminator for layout than anything proposed here
— I've only looked at one checkpoint family and would rather defer to the maintainers than guess.

### Reproduction

**Prerequisite:** this needs the Qwen4-Exp capture guard from **#38642** (rebased onto current
main). On bare main the Qwen4-Exp DFLASH path never reaches the draft at all — the server dies
during decode CUDA-graph capture (`ValueError: too many values to unpack (expected 2)`, see
#38589). With the guard, the server comes up and the numbers below reproduce.

SM80 (8×A800), main + #38642, official DeepSpec drafter, `--speculative-num-draft-tokens 4`:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path <Qwen3.8-Flash-Next target> \
  --speculative-algorithm DFLASH \
  --speculative-draft-model-path <DFlash2 draft, block 4, 24 heads, taps [1,7,14,20,26,32,39,45]> \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --tp 8 \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 8 --mem-fraction-static 0.85
```
(8xA800 SM80, driver 550.144.03, torch 2.11.0+cu130. On SM80 the tilelang/nvcc header
check also needs `NVCC_PREPEND_FLAGS=-DCCCL_DISABLE_CTK_COMPATIBILITY_CHECK`.)

Note that `--speculative-num-draft-tokens 4` is not a free choice here: Qwen4-Exp's QSA
caps the window at its compression ratio
(`layers/attention/qwen_sparse_attn_backend.py:240`, `_require_chain_speculation`), so a
`block_size=7` checkpoint cannot even be launched at its training block size.

### Measured acceptance (4-token window)

| concurrency | requests | failures | accept length | accept rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 300 | 0 | **1.0621** | 0.0184 |
| 24 | 300 | 0 | 1.0643 | 0.0190 |
| 48 | 300 | 0 | 1.0629 | 0.0186 |

An earlier independent run at concurrency 8 gave 1.0604 (47,377 steps), i.e. run-to-run spread
at fixed concurrency is ~0.002.

Per-position, pooled over 47,411 verify steps (concurrency 8):

| position k | P(accept at k \| prefix matched) | P(accept length ≥ k) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.0497 | 0.0497 |
| 2 | 0.1024 | 0.0051 |
| 3 | 0.3485 | 0.0018 |

95.0% of verify steps accept **zero** draft tokens; the bottleneck is position 1. The
6×-concurrency sweep moves accept length by <0.4%, so this is steady-state behaviour, not
a load artifact.

### Related

- #38589 — the sibling report on this target: Qwen4Exp cannot emit DFlash aux hidden
  states at all. That is a prerequisite failure; this one is what remains once a drafter
  *can* be served.
- Same shape of problem, one layer down: the block-size mismatch between a draft's training
  `block_size` and the served `--speculative-num-draft-tokens` is warned about
  (`dflash_worker_v2.py:468`) and then silently forced (`:472`). DFLASH's convolution
  indexes by `position % block_size`, so a mismatch shifts positions too. Fail-fast there
  would have caught this class of problem earlier.

Happy to test either fix on the SM80 rig.

title: [Bug] Abort cleanup hook has no well-defined ordering vs. cache_finished_req: FlexKV needs it before, LMCache needs it after (session leak)
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [ ] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

## Summary

`LMCRadixCache` does not implement `release_aborted_request`, so aborts fall through to the
no-op default in `base_prefix_cache.py:371`. Nothing raises, so the gap is silent.

In MP mode, `match_prefix` opens an LMCache session and may leave a pending lookup holding
daemon-side read locks; `init_load_back` is what consumes them. A request aborted between
those two points leaks, for the lifetime of the server:

- `_mp_load_back_markers[rid]` (`lmc_radix_cache.py:231`, consumed at `:303`);
- the connector-side pending lookup;
- daemon-side read locks, which block eviction of the entries they cover;
- an LMCache session that never receives `END_SESSION`.

The straightforward fix — calling `end_session(handle.rid)` from `release_aborted_request` —
is **not safe in general**, and the abort hook also cannot simply be moved later, because
another backend depends on the current ordering. Details below. Verified on `76f9213a41`.

Related closed PR (not merged): #40334, closed by me after finding the ordering problem.

## Analysis

### Why the obvious fix is unsafe

Three of the six abort call sites (`scheduler.py:3260`, `:3359`, `:5478`) never reach
`cache_finished_req`, so for those the hook is the only possible cleanup point. The other
three (`:3573`, `:5422`, `:5458`) do reach it via `release_kv_cache` (`common.py:272`).
Most notably the disaggregated-decode waiting-queue abort passes the default `is_insert=True`:

```text
scheduler.py:5422  _release_aborted_request(req)
scheduler.py:5431  release_kv_cache(req, self.tree_cache)      # is_insert=True
                     -> cache_finished_req
                        -> store_kv       (lmc_radix_cache.py:489)
                        -> end_session    (lmc_radix_cache.py:493)
```

Adding `end_session` to the abort hook turns that into `end_session -> store_kv -> end_session`.

That relies on the external LMCache implementation treating `end_session` as idempotent.
SGLang declares no `lmcache` dependency at all (it is not in `python/pyproject.toml`), so that
contract is unpinned and unverifiable from this repository. It also permits a STORE after the
session has been closed — and MP `store_kv` blocks until the daemon signals, so the failure
mode is not necessarily a silent no-op.

Tracking active sessions inside SGLang would prevent the second call, but cannot fix the
ordering: the first `end_session` still precedes the STORE.

### Why the abort hook cannot simply be moved later

Backends differ in whether they tolerate running abort cleanup after `cache_finished_req`:

- `hiradix_cache.py` does not override `cache_finished_req`, and the base implementation never
  touches `ongoing_prefetch` / `prefetch_loaded_tokens_by_reqid` that its
  `release_aborted_request` (:2014) cleans — order-independent.
- `unified_radix_cache.py:961` does override it, but does not touch the prefetch, linker or
  buffer-pipeline state cleaned by its `release_aborted_request` (:2458) — order-independent.
- `flexkv_radix_cache.py` **requires the current order**. `cache_finished_req` (:388) may
  `inc_lock_ref` a source node, launch an async store on `store_stream`, and register it in
  `_inflight_store_nodes` (:448); `release_aborted_request` (:488) pops that registration and
  `dec_lock_ref`s the node. Running cleanup afterwards would drop the lock of a store still in
  flight, letting eviction free its source slots — exactly what the comment in `evict()` guards
  against.

So the hook must run before `cache_finished_req` for FlexKV, and would need to run after it for
LMCache.

## Design gap

`release_aborted_request(handle)` conflates two lifecycle operations:

1. cancel pending lookup/prefetch work left by the aborted attempt;
2. perform final request/session cleanup after any required KV release or STORE.

It has neither the phases nor the context to know whether `cache_finished_req` will run
afterwards. A possible direction:

```text
cancel_aborted_request_work
  -> release_kv_cache / cache_finished_req / optional STORE
  -> finish_request_session
```

This preserves FlexKV's required ordering while letting LMCache close its session after the
final STORE, or immediately when no KV finalization happens.

A secondary observation: LMCache keys this state by `rid`, while the attempt lifecycle
introduced in #39318 is keyed by `CacheRequestHandle(rid, attempt_id)`. This is correct today
because the scheduler retires an attempt before starting the next, but it does not give LMCache
the attempt-level isolation FlexKV has.

## Related issues (searched, distinct)

- #37160 — key isolation, not lifecycle
- #34539 — store length, not lifecycle
- #31445 — same class of problem, different backend and state; closed

### Reproduction

No single command reproduces the runtime leak; it needs an LMCache MP daemon plus an abort
landing in a specific window. Trigger conditions:

- LMCache enabled (`enable_lmcache`), MP mode (the default on non-XPU), i.e. `LMCRadixCache`
  is selected in `registry.py:118`;
- a request whose `match_prefix` reports `host_hit_length > 0`, so `_mp_match_prefix` records
  a marker and keeps the lookup locks (`lmc_radix_cache.py:231`);
- the request is aborted before `init_load_back` runs — e.g. `AbortReq` while it is still in
  the waiting queue (`scheduler.py:5422`), or `retire_unadmitted_request` (`:3260`).

The leak itself is directly reproducible in a unit test: drive `_mp_match_prefix` with a fake
connector that models the pending-lookup / read-lock bookkeeping, then call
`release_aborted_request` and observe that nothing is released. #40334 contains such a
CPU-only test (4 cases, no GPU and no `lmcache` install required).

The disaggregated-decode ordering path (abort followed by `cache_finished_req` and a STORE)
is not covered yet.

### Environment

The report is based on code-path analysis and unit tests against `76f9213a41`, not on an
observation from a production deployment; the machine below is the one used for that review,
and does not have `lmcache` installed.


### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists on current `main`.
- [x] A minimal reproducible demo and environment information are included below.
- [x] This is a bug report, not a general question.

### Describe the bug

`POST /v1/responses/{response_id}/cancel` accepts a stored response that was not created in background mode.

A response created with `store=true` and `background=false` (or with `background` omitted, whose default is `false`) is a foreground response. `store` makes the response retrievable, but does not make it eligible for cancellation. The Responses API contract states that only responses created with `background=true` can be cancelled.

After the foreground request completes, calling its cancel endpoint currently returns HTTP 200 with the unchanged `completed` response. The request should instead be rejected as invalid, without invoking abort or changing response state.

The stored `ResponsesResponse` currently does not retain the original `background` value, and the cancel path gates only on status. This makes a stored foreground terminal response indistinguishable from an eligible background terminal response.

Reference: https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/cli/resources/responses/methods/cancel

### Reproduction

From a source checkout, run the following against current `main`. It exercises the request lifecycle directly, so no model or GPU is required.

```python
import asyncio
from unittest.mock import Mock

from utils import make_serving

from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.protocol import ResponsesRequest, ResponsesResponse


serving = make_serving()
serving.tokenizer_manager.abort_request = Mock()

response = ResponsesResponse.from_request(
    ResponsesRequest(
        model="x",
        input="hi",
        background=False,
        store=True,
    ),
    sampling_params={},
    model_name="x",
    created_time=0,
    output=[],
    status="completed",
    usage=None,
)
serving.response_store[response.id] = response

result = asyncio.run(serving.cancel_responses(response.id))

print("http_status:", getattr(result, "status_code", 200))
print("response_status:", getattr(result, "status", None))
print("abort_called:", serving.tokenizer_manager.abort_request.called)
```

Run it with:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python:test/registered/unit/entrypoints/openai \
  python /path/to/repro.py
```

Actual output on `main` at `f3b2725609d9a733cad13eb3bd4ee3d802d4c167`:

```text
http_status: 200
response_status: completed
abort_called: False
```

Expected result: HTTP 400 because the response was not created with `background=true`; the response state remains unchanged and abort is not invoked.

The valid background behavior should remain unchanged:

- `background=true` with `queued` or `in_progress`: transition to `cancelled` and abort the request.
- `background=true` with a terminal status: preserve the existing idempotent response behavior.

### Environment

Relevant `python -m sglang.check_env` output from the CPU-only reproduction environment:

```text
Python: 3.11.15
macOS Version: 26.5.2
Apple Silicon: Apple M4
PyTorch: 2.14.0
pydantic: 2.13.5
orjson: 3.12.0
```

- SGLang source commit: `f3b2725609d9a733cad13eb3bd4ee3d802d4c167`
- Model/GPU: not required; this reproduces in the request lifecycle and cancel handler.

body:
### Checklist

- [x] This tracks upstream integration work and outstanding fixes.
- [x] Written in English.

### Motivation

Track the fixes needed to serve GLM-5.3-Flash on two 96 GB RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs (SM120), using TP2, W4A16 routed experts, FP8 KV, vision and native MTP. Upstream main alone does not yet provide this complete configuration.

### Release and validation status

Updated 2026-09-08 for [v0.4.2](https://github.com/ormandj/sglang-glm53-flash-sm120/releases/tag/v0.4.2). The release uses official SGLang main `afe90a8bc9` and FlashInfer main `9c10d2e8f2`, with checksummed integration patches. [The release lock](https://github.com/ormandj/sglang-glm53-flash-sm120/blob/v0.4.2/stack.lock.json) identifies the exact inputs and resulting trees.

Author validation of the combined build covers changed-path CPU/GPU regressions and sanitizers, full GSM8K, C1-C4 engine measurements, cold prefill, long-context controls, forced HiCache restoration, sampled startup, and a 7680x4320 image followed by four independent cold text requests. The GHCR image was built separately from the same pinned inputs and was not separately benchmarked. [Measured behavior and limitations](https://github.com/ormandj/sglang-glm53-flash-sm120/blob/v0.4.2/BENCHMARKS.md) report the new fixed-MTP comparisons; the serving launcher retains adaptive MTP.

The release retains a 524,288-token shared device token pool. Compact native GLM FP8 rows use 528 rather than 656 bytes without requantizing values. Four concurrent requests share that pool. Host KDA lengths avoid repeated device scalar reads, and small prefill tails can use breakable graphs. These changes do not establish an isolated speedup for any individual PR.

### Submitted fixes and validation scope

- #38212 at `230102db83` includes the checkpoint-boundary, component key-cap and standalone compressed-index repairs previously reviewed at `a754a55e7b`. Its standalone CPU scope is 81 tests and 106 subtests. On the combined build, a 320-token-chunk profile passed device and confirmed host reuse at 512/768-token prefixes, plus four naturally completed coding-tool requests. Exact saved-state regressions establish checkpoint correctness; the model logprob comparisons are numerical smoke checks with unchanged control-relative bounds.
- #38213 at `342fba81d1` remains an opt-in metadata optimization with eager-reference and fallback tests. The standalone CPU checks passed three tests and six subtests. No isolated serving speedup is claimed.
- #38164 at `6fa7b61c81` retains disaggregated preallocation timeouts, empty-batch prefill-only cleanup and pending health-signal draining. Its 66 CPU tests and two subtests use mocked transport status and clocks, including two-process Gloo; they do not validate live RDMA or a standalone full model.
- The integration now uses #35645 from @imReese with tests from @Kangwenqiao, plus the published [mixed-decode sub-page follow-up](https://github.com/ormandj/sglang/commit/3878952b1bd298cbd57d792bceff083b0748e169). It replaces the earlier narrower overlapping admission guard while preserving contributor credit.

All 19 owned PR branches were rebased onto the release's audited SGLang or FlashInfer main and validated within their stated scope. The final SGLang main change was documentation-only; exact Python and test trees were checked where CPU results preceded that rebase. PR bodies identify tested heads, commands and limits. Combined-image results are separate from standalone PR validation.

## Carried upstream changes

SGLang #36507 is supplied by main through merge `97c6978369`, including the #37548 multimodal NEXTN embedding fix. [FlashInfer #4802](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4802) is supplied by main through merge `453aa7c729`. #38212 replaces #38161, #38213 replaces #38162, and #38214 replaces #37539 after deletion of the merged GLM base branch. #37625 preserves Benjamin Oldenburg's (@bold84) co-author credit.

Additional adapted prior work includes #36904 (`436a89b06f`) for the raw-layout TileLang fallback and #37375 (`b6478a7400`) for the mHC pipeline handoff. Both PRs closed without merging. #37744 was refiled as #38254 (`4664a013c5`); the retained KDA fusion additionally covers FP8 qkv with BF16 gates and is not an unchanged copy of that PR. These heads were included in the pre-freeze fetch and status audit.

### Native KV integration

On 2026-09-10, [FlashInfer #5022 was closed](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5022#issuecomment-5626514390) in favor of combining the work in [#5075](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5075). The remaining contributions are submitted directly against Gabriel's branch in [lucifer1004/flashinfer#3](https://github.com/lucifer1004/flashinfer/pull/3). Author-run validation of the final changed files over the combined integration passed 64 CPU tests (17 GPU cases skipped), 696 FP8 GPU cases, 171 Compute Sanitizer cases with zero errors, and six SGLang adapter cases on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q. These are source-integration results, not qualification of a new public image. The existing #38430 review head below still uses the earlier capability check; its canonical-payload adaptation is included in the new source integration and will be reflected in that PR before release.

The next integration is based on official SGLang `dc5f59c3a2` and FlashInfer `19a103e6e6`, carrying the exact contribution head `e7cad40ef1`. Its build and full release qualification are in progress; v0.4.2 remains the published release described above.

The current #38430 review head requires the complete [FlashInfer #5022](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5022) changes, including dedicated-zero-row masked reads and compatible eight-head scratch. The model-specific contract-version field has been removed. Runner construction checks the existing `compact_bytes_per_token == 528` layout capability, which excludes the initial padded-only API. This check does not independently verify correctness fixes, and partial cherry-picks of compact-row support are unsupported. The compact-capable kernels accept both 528- and 656-byte inputs. #37625 supplies the finite top-k selection correction.

Author CPU validation on 2026-09-09 passed 35 FlashInfer dispatch tests at `a47c44ec32` and 18 SGLang tests with 21 subtests at `a36002eba6`, using the paired sources with CUDA hidden. These follow-ups leave CUDA/C++ sources and GPU tests unchanged; the GPU results below retain their release-time source scope.

Release-time author standalone validation passed 18 CPU tests and 21 subtests for #38430, 24 CPU tests for #38431, and 35 CPU dispatch plus 570 GPU sparse-attention tests for FlashInfer #5022. The refreshed graph-ownership, top-k and vision PRs passed three GPU tests, 297 JIT tests plus 38 subtests, and nine combined CPU/GPU tests, respectively. FlashInfer #4827 passed eight mocked CPU workspace-lifetime tests with CUDA hidden. GPU checks used RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q (SM120). PR bodies retain historical sanitizer and full-model results under their original source scopes.

Removing unused RoPE storage reduces each affected GLM NoPE row from 656 to 528 bytes, with unchanged FP8 values and FP32 scales: 19.5% fewer bytes, or 24.2% more rows per fixed row-memory budget before allocator padding. Other pools and configured context limits still apply. Kernel and adapter checks do not establish whole-model accuracy or an isolated serving speedup.

### Work still downstream

MHC auxiliary-tensor lifetime handling for breakable graphs remains downstream. Its source and validation are separate from the native KV PRs.

The mixed-row HiCache sidecar implementation and the later checkpoint and standalone-index repairs are included in the released integration. The sidecar path supports one draft runner; mismatched multiple runners remain unsupported. FP4 MLA KV storage is rejected before allocation because these transfers do not support its separate scales. Draft sidecars add host memory beyond the target host-pool budget.

Other retained downstream pieces include SM120 model/backend selection, ModelOpt E4M3-K32 preparation, the W4A16 route-prefix optimization, static Mamba admission/accounting, adaptive-MTP buffer lifetime, GLM video/DP/media-order handling, PCIe IPC all-reduce wiring, mixed-precision KDA gate fusion, optional FP8 lm_head support, recurrent-kernel tuning, and diagnostics. Hardware-specific memory/concurrency defaults need not become universal upstream defaults. FlashInfer's native backend merge does not by itself upstream the SGLang integration.

### Associated reports and remaining gaps

| Report | Current relationship |
|---|---|
| #38031, output corruption after host-cache loadback | #38212 restores missing DSA index state and separates compressed prefix ownership. #37534 alone only fixes row geometry. The PR links author before/after serving results and independent H100 confirmation with exact revision scopes. |
| #36830, FP8 KV with KPool on CUDA | #38430 with [flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5022](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5022) provides a native scaled-FP8 NoPE path on SM120. This does not resolve the original SM90 report. #36904 closed without merging; its raw-layout TileLang fallback remains separate adapted work. |
| #36906, pipeline-parallel residual KeyError | The #37375 mHC handoff correction remains adapted downstream; its PR did not merge. |
| #37548, invalid multimodal NEXTN embedding index | Fixed before #36507 merged. The cause was multimodal sentinel IDs, not TP8 vocabulary sharding. |
| #37105 / #29738, SM120 startup/backend failures | [FlashInfer #4802](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4802) merged; #38430 submits the native GLM NoPE backend/layout integration; other SM120 selection and defaults remain downstream. |
| #37892, DeepSeek-V4 paged top-k illegal access | #37625 covers the selector family with bounds/correctness tests. The GB300 reproduction has not been validated with it. |
| #37712, large fp8_mqa_logits prefill allocation | Not fixed by #37535's KDA workspace limit. |
| #36653, #36669, #36711, #36886 | Separate draft loading, tool/prompt behavior, MoE loading and DCP issues. The HiCache fix is not a blanket fix for these reports. |

Long-prompt input-logprob requests can still exceed runtime memory headroom. DCP, other GPU architectures, generic noncontiguous hybrid-layer layouts and BF16 full-model serving are not established by the SM120 TP2 validation. DCP is not enabled in this release.

Review-branch update, 2026-09-11: #38212 is rebased onto main `833bce9df5` at `0ee51670a7`. CPU checks ran at this head. The GPU sanitizer run used `5ea9a412d3`; radix checks and initial fault injections preceded formatting and test-file relocation, with matching runtime/test logic verified. The final head moves the GPU test into the regular PR suite and strengthens CPU checkpoint-lifetime coverage. The test consolidation retains 20 registered GPU transfer cases and adds the DSA index-buffer cleanup correction exposed by running them together. Author checks passed 124 CPU tests/111 subtests, 26 targeted radix cases and the 20 GPU cases under Compute Sanitizer; 20 deliberate faults were detected by assertions. These results do not update the released source references or establish a new full-model run.

### Upstream coordination

Remaining maintainer decisions are where to place SM120 backend selection and defaults, how to sequence the cross-repository KV changes, and which optional optimizations should remain separate. Each submitted PR states the behavior changed, test scope and relevant dependencies. The tables describe the released source separately from the moving review branches.
