title: [Bug] HiCache staged write-back: the 128 KiB batch path passes registered host VAs to cudaMemcpyBatchAsync and faults where CanUseHostPointerForRegisteredMem == 0
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

HiCache backup copies device KV into the host pool through the JIT kernel `python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/kvcacheio/staged_write_back.cuh`. The kernel has two D2H strategies and picks between them by copy granularity: per-page `cudaMemcpyAsync` for small copies, and one `cudaMemcpyBatchAsync` for `src_ptrs.size() * num_pages` descriptors once `first_page_bytes = page_size * src_stride(0) * item_size >= kLargeCopyThresholdBytes` (128 KiB, defined at `:106`, branch at `:154`, call at `:170`, call sites `:274` MLA and `:279` MHA).

For the batch call the kernel passes **the raw host virtual addresses** of the host pool as the destination pointers (`dst_ptrs[t].data_ptr() + dst_indices[...] * stride * elem`). On a platform where `cudaDevAttrCanUseHostPointerForRegisteredMem` is **0** — i.e. registered host memory is
*not* accessible at the same virtual address on the device — those addresses are not valid device-space addresses, and the copy fails with an **asynchronous `cudaErrorIllegalAddress`**. The fallback path in the same kernel uses `cudaMemcpyAsync` over the *same* addresses and works,
because that API translates host pointers for you.

**Minimal demonstration.** One program, one descriptor, 128 KiB; only the destination form varies:

| `dst` passed to `cudaMemcpyBatchAsync` | submission | sync | bytes |
|---|---|---|---|
| host VA of `mmap()` + `cudaHostRegister()` — **what the kernel does today** | `no error` | **`an illegal memory access was encountered`** | not copied |
| `cudaHostGetDevicePointer()` alias of the *same* buffer | `no error` | `no error` | correct |
| `cudaHostAlloc()` buffer | `no error` | `no error` | correct |
| host VA of plain pageable `mmap()` (never registered) | `no error` | `no error` | correct |
| per-copy `cudaMemcpyAsync()` into the registered buffer | — | `no error` | correct |

Observed on the machine described under *Environment*:

```
$ ./repro_host_va_vs_alias va
cudaDevAttrCanUseHostPointerForRegisteredMem = 0
mode=va      dst=0x72be8c02b000
  submission -> no error
  sync       -> an illegal memory access was encountered
  host[0]    = 0x00 (expected 0x11)

$ ./repro_host_va_vs_alias alias
cudaDevAttrCanUseHostPointerForRegisteredMem = 0
host VA = 0x74371c101000, device alias = 0x204c00000 (same=NO)
mode=alias   dst=0x204c00000
  submission -> no error
  sync       -> no error
  host[0]    = 0x11 (expected 0x11)
```

The same holds at the kernel's real geometry (2 host tensors x 4 pages = 8 descriptors, 128 KiB each): host VAs -> illegal memory access; the two aliases -> success with `k=0x11`, `v=0x22` verified at both the first and the last byte of both buffers.

 `cudaDevAttrCanUseHostPointerForRegisteredMem` is documented as "Device can access host registered memory at the same virtual address as the CPU". On this machine it is `0`, and it is consistent with what the runtime reports for the two host-memory flavors:

```
mmap + cudaHostRegister : host VA 0x74371c101000 != device alias 0x204c00000   (same = NO)
cudaHostAlloc          : host VA == device alias                              (same = YES)
```

On typical native Linux x86_64 with UVA the attribute is `1`, so a host VA *is* a valid device address and the raw-address usage happens to be correct. That is consistent with #21631's benchmark (~48 GiB/s through this same API) and with the absence of earlier reports. Note that
sglang already encodes this exact concept for ROCm — `_resolve_device_accessible_ptr_fn()` in `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/pool_host/common.py` documents that "on HIP they differ" and `get_device_accessible_ptr` exists to translate; the batch destination is the one place where the translation is not applied.

The two conditions are the default combination in production: the default host pool is `mmap`-backed and registered (`ALLOC_MEMORY_FUNCS` defaults to `alloc_with_host_register`, which calls `cudart.cudaHostRegister(ptr, size, 0)`, on buffers from `HostTensorAllocator.allocate -> alloc_mmap`; only `npu`/`musa` use `alloc_with_pin_memory`), and essentially any real checkpoint exceeds 128 KiB per page (e.g. `page_size=64`, 32 layers, 8 KV heads x 128 dim, bf16 -> 4 MiB). So the batch path is the *default* path, and whether a deployment survives depends on a device attribute that differs by platform/driver — including WSL2, which is where I hit it.

The batch call returns `cudaSuccess`; the error is asynchronous and sticky, so it is only observed at the next synchronization point. In our runs the first symptom was a stream query inside the HiCache ready-count logic:

```
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
  unified_radix_cache.py:3069 _count_ready_acks -> torch/cuda/streams.py query()
  reached via _produce_buffer_l3 -> _buffer_backup_and_wait -> _pump_hicache_until
           -> check_hicache_events -> _sync_hicache_ready_counts
```

The frame in that traceback is not the faulting call, and under `retry()` the test retries until the budget is exhausted, so it presents as a flaky test rather than a broken D2H.

End-to-end confirmation at the sglang level (same test, same geometry, only the host pool backing changed):

| configuration (`test_buffer_only_load_back_drops_on_sibling_published_span`, page_size=32, num_layers=16) | result |
|---|---|
| default: host pool = `mmap` + `cudaHostRegister` | **FAIL** — illegal memory access |
| host pool = `cudaHostAlloc` (`torch.empty(..., pin_memory=True)`) | **PASS** |
| default, with `cudaMemcpyBatchAsync` forced to return `cudaErrorNotSupported` via `LD_PRELOAD` (kernel then takes its existing fallback) | **PASS** |

**Note**

1. **Size / count.** The standalone program faults with 1 descriptor and 4 KiB per copy; the 128 KiB threshold only decides whether sglang enters the batch path.
2. **A memory limit.** Buffers are ~1 MiB, `cudaMemGetInfo` reports 5 GiB free, `ulimit -l` is 1 GiB.
3. **Relayout/staging kernel, or the address arithmetic.** `copy_page_first_pages_fallback()` (`:64`) uses the identical `src_ptr`/`dst_ptr` expressions and succeeds — the LD_PRELOAD row above removes only the batch call.
4. **The relayout kernel's pointer table / missing `get_device_accessible_ptr`.** This wheel (0.4.7) lacks the op, so `make_kernel_ptr_table()` hands the kernel raw addresses; injecting the real alias (confirmed to take effect by tracing the call: 2 calls, `n=16, registered=True`) leaves
   the crash identical. That table addresses the *kernel*, not the D2H descriptor, whose destination comes from the host tensor's `data_ptr()`. (The missing op does matter for any fix built on the alias helper — it would need a wheel built from `python/sglang/kernels/aot`.)
5. **`cudaMemcpyAttributes`.** The fault is identical for `srcAccessOrder` = `cudaMemcpySrcAccessOrderStream`, `...DuringApiCall` and `...Any`, with and without `srcLocHint`/`dstLocHint`, so there is no attribute-level workaround.
6. **`cudaHostRegister` flags.** `Default`, `Mapped`, `Portable` and `Mapped|Portable` all fault.
7. **Compile-time vs runtime `cudaMemcpyBatchAsync` ABI (#36302, #23136, #21869).** The JIT objects here come from `/usr/local/cuda-13.2/.../cuda_runtime.h` (nvcc 13.2) and `cudaRuntimeGetVersion()` returns 13020, so both sides use the 8-parameter signature; the standalone program is compiled the same way and faults.
8. **Mooncake/RDMA storage (#21044).** No storage backend at all here.
9. I cannot separate "WSL2/GPU-PV" from "this driver version" with a single machine, and I cannot tell whether the intended contract of `cudaMemcpyBatchAsync` is that host destinations must already be device-visible. The batch API documentation describes pointer-to-pointer copies and does not state this explicitly. What I can show is that passing the alias makes the identical copy work, so this is fixable on the sglang side regardless of how the driver question is resolved.

### Reproduction

**(1) Standalone, no sglang.** Save as `repro.cu` and run the three modes:

```cpp
// nvcc -O2 -std=c++17 -o repro repro.cu
// ./repro va | alias | pinned
#include <cuda_runtime.h>
#include <sys/mman.h>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstring>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#define CK(x) do { cudaError_t e_ = (x); if (e_ != cudaSuccess) { \
  printf("  %s -> %s\n", #x, cudaGetErrorString(e_)); return 1; } } while (0)

int main(int argc, char** argv) {
  const std::string mode = argc > 1 ? argv[1] : "va";
  const size_t page_bytes = 128 * 1024;

  int attr = -1;
  cudaDeviceGetAttribute(&attr, cudaDevAttrCanUseHostPointerForRegisteredMem, 0);
  printf("cudaDevAttrCanUseHostPointerForRegisteredMem = %d\n", attr);

  CK(cudaSetDevice(0));
  void* dev = nullptr;
  CK(cudaMalloc(&dev, page_bytes));
  CK(cudaMemset(dev, 0x11, page_bytes));

  void* host = nullptr;
  if (mode == "pinned") {
    CK(cudaHostAlloc(&host, page_bytes, cudaHostAllocDefault));
  } else {
    host = mmap(nullptr, page_bytes, PROT_READ | PROT_WRITE,
                MAP_PRIVATE | MAP_ANONYMOUS, -1, 0);
    if (host == MAP_FAILED) return 1;
    CK(cudaHostRegister(host, page_bytes, 0));   // what the default HiCache pool does
    memset(host, 0, page_bytes);
  }

  void* dst = host;
  if (mode == "alias") {
    CK(cudaHostGetDevicePointer(&dst, host, 0));
    printf("host VA = %p, device alias = %p (same=%s)\n", host, dst,
           host == dst ? "YES" : "NO");
  }

  std::vector<void*> dsts{dst};
  std::vector<const void*> srcs{dev};
  std::vector<size_t> sizes{page_bytes};
  cudaMemcpyAttributes attrs{};
  attrs.srcAccessOrder = cudaMemcpySrcAccessOrderStream;
  size_t attrs_idxs[1] = {0};

  cudaStream_t stream = nullptr;
  CK(cudaStreamCreate(&stream));
  printf("mode=%-7s dst=%p\n", mode.c_str(), dst);
  cudaError_t err = cudaMemcpyBatchAsync(dsts.data(), srcs.data(), sizes.data(), 1,
                                        &attrs, attrs_idxs, 1, stream);
  printf("  submission -> %s\n", cudaGetErrorString(err));
  fflush(stdout);
  cudaError_t serr = cudaStreamSynchronize(stream);
  printf("  sync       -> %s\n", cudaGetErrorString(serr));
  printf("  host[0]    = 0x%02x (expected 0x11)\n", ((unsigned char*)host)[0]);
  return serr == cudaSuccess ? 0 : 2;
}
```

**(2) In-tree.** `CacheConfig` in `test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py`
(line 131) defaults to `page_size: int = 1` (line 134) and `num_layers: int = 24` (line 138) — about
6 KiB per page, below the threshold, which is why the stock test passes here. With

```python
    page_size: int = 32
    num_layers: int = 16
```

the L3 buffer-backup test crashes (I drove the same suite with an equivalent widened configuration,
one subprocess per configuration, because an illegal access aborts the process):

```
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered
RESULT ps=32 layers=16 test=test_buffer_only_load_back_drops_on_sibling_published_span -> FAIL (err=2)
```

and the two controls described above turn it into `-> PASS` (default host pool with
`cudaMemcpyBatchAsync` made to return `cudaErrorNotSupported` via LD_PRELOAD; or host pool switched
to `cudaHostAlloc`).


### Environment


```
$ python3 -m sglang.check_env
Python: 3.12.12 (main, Feb 12 2026, 00:42:14) [Clang 21.1.4 ]
CUDA available: True
GPU 0: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Laptop GPU
GPU 0 Compute Capability: 8.6
CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda-13.2
NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 13.2, V13.2.51
CUDA Driver Version: 596.49
PyTorch: 2.13.0+cu130
sglang: Module Not Found
sglang-kernel: 0.4.7
flashinfer_python: 0.6.18.post1
triton: 3.7.1
transformers: 5.17.0
numpy: 2.3.5
Hypervisor vendor:: Microsoft
ulimit soft: 1048576
```

Relevant properties of this machine, measured with `cudaDeviceGetAttribute`:

```
CanMapHostMemory                            = 1
UnifiedAddressing                           = 1
PageableMemoryAccess                        = 0
PageableMemoryAccessUsesHostPageTables      = 0
ConcurrentManagedAccess                     = 0
CanUseHostPointerForRegisteredMem           = 0     <-- the predicate that makes this fail
driver = 13020, runtime = 13020
```

**Note**

- Platform: WSL2 (`6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2`, GPU-PV via `/dev/dxg`; the only driver library
  present is `/usr/lib/wsl/lib/libcuda.so.1`, i.e. no native Linux driver). Single laptop GPU,
  6144 MiB. I believe this is *why* the attribute is 0, but I cannot prove that the attribute is
  0 only on WSL2 — hence the one-line check above.
- The `get_device_accessible_ptr` warning printed by this build (wheel 0.4.7 lacks the op) is a
  separate environment gap; see *Ruled out* item 4.
- I could not run the CUDA CI suites (`test/run_suite.py --hw cuda ...`); they target 1-GPU-H100-class
  hardware and this box is not representative. The report rests on the standalone CUDA program and
  the widened in-tree unit test.

title: [Bug] MooncakeHostTensorAllocator wraps a null pointer from the host allocator instead of failing at the allocation site
body:
## Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

## Describe the bug

`MooncakeHostTensorAllocator.allocate` in
`python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/mooncake_store/mooncake_store.py` passes the raw
return value of `MooncakeHostMemAllocator.alloc(size)` straight into
`(ctypes.c_byte * size).from_address(...)` and `torch.frombuffer(...)`:

```python
ptr_int = self.allocator.alloc(size)
self.ptr = ptr_int
c_type = ctypes.c_byte * size
c_array = c_type.from_address(ptr_int)

tensor = torch.frombuffer(c_array, dtype=torch.uint8, count=size)
```

When the underlying allocator cannot map the host segment (for example an `mmap`
failure because host memory is exhausted or the requested segment is larger than what
is available) it returns a null pointer. `ctypes.from_address(0)` and
`torch.frombuffer` both accept that without complaint, so `allocate()` returns a
perfectly normal-looking tensor of the requested shape whose `data_ptr()` is `0`.

Nothing fails at the point where the allocation actually failed. The error only
surfaces much later and far from the cause:

- pinning the host pool calls `cudaHostRegister` on address 0, which fails with
  `cudaErrorInvalidValue` — an error message that says nothing about host memory;
- or the process segfaults on the first real access to the buffer.

In a prefill deployment we observed exactly this: a `cudaHostRegister`
`cudaErrorInvalidValue` during HiCache host pool setup, which cost a long detour
through the CUDA side of the stack before the real problem — the mooncake host
allocator failing to map its segment — was identified.

The allocation site should refuse a null pointer and say how much memory it was
trying to get.

## Reproduction

This is CPU-only and needs no mooncake install: `__init__` (which constructs the real
`MooncakeHostMemAllocator`) is bypassed with `__new__`, and the underlying allocator is
mocked into reporting a failed mapping.

```python
from unittest import mock

import torch

from sglang.srt.mem_cache.storage.mooncake_store.mooncake_store import (
    MooncakeHostTensorAllocator,
)

# Bypass __init__ so no real mooncake install / host segment is needed, and
# make the underlying allocator report a failed mapping (null pointer).
allocator = MooncakeHostTensorAllocator.__new__(MooncakeHostTensorAllocator)
allocator.allocator = mock.Mock(alloc=mock.Mock(return_value=0))
allocator.ptr = None

tensor = allocator.allocate((1024, 1024), dtype=torch.uint8)
print("allocate() returned a tensor:", tensor.shape, tensor.dtype)
print("data_ptr =", tensor.data_ptr())
```

Actual output on current `main`:

```
allocate() returned a tensor: torch.Size([1024, 1024]) torch.uint8
data_ptr = 0
```

The failed allocation is silently converted into a 1 MiB tensor backed by address 0.
Touching that tensor is where things go wrong; replacing the two `print` calls with
`print(int(tensor[0, 0]))` gives:

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<string>", line 9, in <module>
RuntimeError: The tensor has a non-zero number of elements, but its data is not allocated yet.
If you're using torch.compile/export/fx, it is likely that we are erroneously tracing into a custom kernel. ...
```

which is what a user has to work backwards from. In a real deployment the same tensor
reaches `cudaHostRegister` first and the failure is reported as
`cudaErrorInvalidValue`.

Expected behaviour — raising at the allocation site, naming the requested size:

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "repro.py", line 15, in <module>
    tensor = allocator.allocate((1024, 1024), dtype=torch.uint8)
  File ".../sglang/srt/mem_cache/storage/mooncake_store/mooncake_store.py", line 57, in allocate
    raise RuntimeError(
RuntimeError: MooncakeHostMemAllocator.alloc returned a null pointer for 0.001 GB (1048576 bytes); the mooncake host memory allocator could not map the segment (check host memory availability and the mooncake allocator logs).
```

title: [Bug] Hardcoded fp32 dtypes in KDA short-convs cause 2x bandwidth waste
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

### Describe the bug

SGLang hardcodes `params_dtype=torch.float32` for Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) short-convolution weights, regardless of the checkpoint's native data type. This silently up-casts native `bf16` checkpoints to `fp32`. Up-casting doubles the convolution weight bandwidth during decoding without adding any true precision to the weights.

#### Root cause
The hardcoded definitions exist in the following locations (as of commit `95521da18d`):
- `python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_linear.py:400` — `qkv_conv1d` uses `MergedColumnParallelLinear(..., params_dtype=torch.float32, ...)`.
- `python/sglang/srt/models/glm5_next.py:520-526` — `qkv_conv1d` is hardcoded to `torch.float32`.
- `python/sglang/srt/models/bailing_moe_v3.py:888-928` — `BailingKDA` subclasses `KimiDeltaAttention`, inheriting the `fp32` hardcode.
- `python/sglang/srt/models/kimi_k3.py:1726` — Kimi-K3 does not inherit from `kimi_linear.py` but has its own `MergedColumnParallelLinear(..., params_dtype=torch.float32)` for a third, separate KDA `qkv_conv1d`.

The type casting is silent because the loader uses in-place `param_data.copy_(loaded_weight)`. 

*History & Context:* The `fp32` cast was introduced in the original Kimi Linear PR. However, the original Kimi-Linear-48B checkpoint is natively `bf16`, meaning the engine's `fp32` allocation never matched the checkpoint. Contrast this with `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/dsa/dsa_indexer_kpool.py:142`, which performs a similar up-cast but includes a clear, explicit comment justifying it: `# Keep weights_proj in FP32 because its accumulation/scale path requires FP32; checkpoint BF16 weights are cast on load.` The lack of any such justification for KDA strongly suggests an oversight rather than a deliberate choice. 

Note that vLLM has the exact same bug at `vllm/model_executor/models/bailing_moe_v3.py:697-716`.

#### Reference implementations
The original model implementations do not require `fp32`:
- `moonshotai/Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct` (`modeling_kimi.py:471-483`): Instantiates `fla.modules.ShortConvolution(...)` using the model's default dtype.
- `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` (`modeling_kimi_linear.py:504-518`): Uses `ShortConvolution(...)` with no dtype override.

#### Measured dtype ledger
Reading the safetensors headers directly reveals that most models ship `bf16` convolutions. SGLang forces these to `fp32`.

| Checkpoint | conv tensor | file dtype | shape | SGLang builds | Result |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| moonshotai/Kimi-K3 | `q/k/v_conv1d.weight` | F32 | `[12288,1,4]` | fp32 | match |
| nvidia/Kimi-K3-NVFP4 | `q/k/v_conv1d.weight` | F32 | `[12288,1,4]` | fp32 | match |
| moonshotai/Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct| `q/k/v_conv1d.weight` | BF16 | `[4096,1,4]` | fp32 | **UP-CAST** |
| moonshotai/Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Base | `q/k/v_conv1d.weight` | BF16 | `[4096,1,4]` | fp32 | **UP-CAST** |
| zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash | `q/k/v_conv1d.weight` | BF16 | `[8192,1,4]` | fp32 | **UP-CAST** |
| nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4 | `q/k/v_conv1d.weight` | F32 | `[8192,1,4]` | fp32 | match |
| inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash | `q/k/v_conv1d.weight` | BF16 | `[4096,1,4]` | fp32 | **UP-CAST** |
| inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash-fp8 | `q/k/v_conv1d.weight` | BF16 | `[4096,1,4]` | fp32 | **UP-CAST** |
| inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-tiny | `q/k/v_conv1d.weight` | BF16 | `[2048,1,4]` | fp32 | **UP-CAST** |
| Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct | `linear_attn.conv1d.weight` | BF16 | `[8192,1,4]` | bf16 | match |
| Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B (and -FP8) | `linear_attn.conv1d.weight` | BF16 | `[10240,1,4]`| bf16 | match |
| Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (and variants)| `linear_attn.conv1d.weight` | BF16 | `[10240,1,4]`| bf16 | match |
| internlm/Intern-S2-397B | `linear_attn.conv1d.weight` | BF16 | `[12288,1,4]`| bf16 | match |
| internlm/Intern-S2-Mobius | `linear_attn.conv1d.weight` | BF16 | `[8192,1,4]` | bf16 | match |
| TaichuAI/ZDTaichu5.0-9B | `linear_attn.conv1d.weight` | BF16 | `[8192,1,4]` | bf16 | match |
| nex-agi/Nex-N2.5-Pro | `linear_attn.conv1d.weight` | BF16 | `[12288,1,4]`| bf16 | match |
| nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Lightning-30B-A3B | `mixer.conv1d.weight` | BF16 | `[6144,1,4]` | bf16 | match |
| nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-12B-v2 | `conv1d.weight` | BF16 | `[12288,1,4]`| bf16 | match |
| ibm-granite/granite-4.0-h-small | `conv1d.weight` | BF16 | `[8448,1,4]` | bf16 | match |
| thinkingmachines/Inkling (and -NVFP4) | `k_sconv.weight` | BF16 | `[2048,1,4]` | bf16 | match |
| thinkingmachines/Inkling-Small | `k/v_sconv.weight` | BF16 | `[1024,1,4]` | bf16 | match |

#### Kimi K3 Exception
`moonshotai/Kimi-K3` intentionally ships `fp32` convolutions. Within a single KDA block, small parameters (`A_log`, `dt_bias`, `q/k/v_conv1d.weight`) are `fp32`, while projections remain `bf16`. The checkpoint parser should respect this deliberate choice (when specified).

#### Up-casting to fp32 is pure waste
Up-casting a `bf16` weight to `fp32` adds no actual information to the weight itself because it was already rounded when saved. 

Note on numerics: Applying a fix to load `bf16` natively is not strictly bit-exact to the current `fp32` cast due to how the Triton kernel is written. In `causal_conv1d_triton.py:366`, the multiply-accumulate is:
`acc += matrix_x * matrix_w` (no explicit cast)
- **Today (x is bf16, w is fp32):** `matrix_x` promotes, the product is computed and kept in `fp32`, and added to the `fp32` accumulator.
- **After fix (x is bf16, w is bf16):** The product is computed in `bf16` and rounded *before* it reaches the `fp32` accumulator.

The observable difference comes entirely from the kernel's uncast multiply, not the weights. If need to keep exact bit-for-bit equivalence with the old behavior while saving weight bandwidth, it is a two-line change in the Triton kernel to cast `matrix_x` and `matrix_w` to `tl.float32` prior to the multiplication. 

#### Impact
At batch=1 decode, the convolution is weight-bandwidth bound. For GLM-5.3-Flash, the activation slice is ~48 KB per layer compared to ~393 KB for the current `fp32` weights.

Conv weight bytes streamed per decode token, unsharded:

| Model | KDA layers | conv_dim | fp32 (current waste) | bf16 (if fixed) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash | 34 | 3 x 8192 = 24576 | 13.4 MB | 6.7 MB |
| inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash | 35 | 3 x 4096 = 12288 | 6.9 MB | 3.4 MB |
| moonshotai/Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B | 20 | 3 x 4096 = 12288 | 3.9 MB | 2.0 MB |
| moonshotai/Kimi-K3 | 69 | 3 x 12288 = 36864 | 40.7 MB | *(keeps fp32, correctly)* |

Removing `fp32` weights against `bf16` activations also eliminates a mixed-dtype promotion directly from the Triton inner loop.

#### Proposed fix
Probe the checkpoint's convolution weight dtype during configuration resolution and pass it dynamically as `params_dtype`. It should not need an override configuration to change the dtype; the engine should automatically respect the checkpoint. 

Precedent exists in-tree: `python/sglang/srt/model_loader/weight_utils.py:90-131` (`probe_routed_expert_weight_dtype`).

**Implementation hazard:** The dtype must be resolved before module construction. Currently, SGLang captures a view of the weights at `__init__` time (`conv_weights = self.qkv_conv1d.weight.squeeze(1)`). If `param.data` is swapped post-initialization, these views will point to uninitialized memory.

#### NVIDIA Quant
NVIDIA's repacks disagree with original authors: `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` is BF16, but `nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` is F32. NVIDIA baked their engine-side up-cast directly into the file. The engine should simply respect the checkpoint provided. (But seems wrong).



### Reproduction


```python
import json, struct, sys

with open(sys.argv[1], "rb") as f:
    n, = struct.unpack("<Q", f.read(8))
    hdr = json.loads(f.read(n))
    
for k, v in hdr.items():
    if "conv1d" in k or "sconv" in k:
        print(v["dtype"], v["shape"], k)
```

1. Run the script on `moonshotai/Kimi-K3` shard 1: It prints `F32 [12288, 1, 4]` for `language_model.model.layers.0.self_attn.{q,k,v}_conv1d.weight`.
2. Run the script on `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash`: The equivalent keys print `BF16 [8192, 1, 4]`.
3. Load either model in SGLang and check the parameters: Every KDA `qkv_conv1d.weight` is forcibly allocated as `torch.float32`.

### Environment

title: [Bug] GLM-5.3-Flash on RTX PRO 6000 (sm_120): two DSA backend blockers after the deep_gemm NameError
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

Serving `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` on **8x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (sm_120)** fails at
startup. After working around the known `deep_gemm` NameError (#29738), **two further blockers**
appear, both in the DSA attention backend. Neither is reachable by configuration.

This mirrors #33194 (same model family, SM80/Ampere): the DSA/MHC kernels appear to assume
**datacenter-class** GPUs (sm_90 Hopper / sm_100 Blackwell DC). sm_120 is a workstation part with
**half the shared memory and no TMEM/tcgen05**.

### Environment

```
GPU            8x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (sm_120)
shared mem     102,400 B / SM   (H200 sm_90: 227 KB)
driver         610.43.02
image          lmsysorg/sglang:glm-5.3-flash   (base aa8c950a3d)
model          zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash  (index_kpool=4, 45 layers, 288 experts)
launch         --tp-size 8 --data-parallel-size 8 --enable-dp-attention
               --expert-parallel-size 8 --disable-shared-experts-fusion
               --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16
               --mm-enable-dp-encoder --context-length 1048576
```

### Blocker 0 (pre-existing, #29738) — triggered automatically on sm_120

`configurer.py` deliberately excludes sm_120:

```python
# python/sglang/srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/configurer.py
# "DeepGEMM requires TMEM/tcgen05 (SM100+datacenter), not available on SM120"
if sm_version == 120:
    return False        # -> ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM = False
                        # -> entrypoint.py:19 `if ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM: import deep_gemm` is skipped
```

but `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM` is hardware-independent:

```python
# python/sglang/srt/environ.py
SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM = EnvBool(True)   # always True
```

so `mhc.py` still takes the deep_gemm branch and `entrypoint.py` calls it unguarded:

```
NameError: name 'deep_gemm' is not defined
  at srt/layers/deep_gemm_wrapper/entrypoint.py  tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm()
  <- kernels/ops/layernorm/mhc.py  mhc_pre
  <- srt/models/glm5_next.py  hc_attn_pre
```

Measured on this host: `ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM=False` while `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM=True`.

**On sm_120 these two flags are always inconsistent** — #29738 required setting an env manually;
here it happens out of the box. Suggest gating `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM` on
`ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM`, or guarding the call site.

**Workaround:** `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM=0` (takes the non-deep_gemm branch in `mhc_pre`).
This works — and exposes the next two blockers.

### Blocker 1 — auto-selected `trtllm` DSA decode backend is unsupported on sm_120

```
Set DSA backends for bfloat16 KV Cache: prefill=flashmla_sparse, decode=trtllm
Capture cuda graph failed: Error in function 'TllmGenFmhaRunner'
  at /workspace/include/flashinfer/trtllm/fmha/fmhaRunner.cuh:37: Unsupported architecture
```

The auto-selector picks `trtllm` for Blackwell, but the TRT-LLM Gen FMHA kernel only supports
sm_100. `prefill=flashmla_sparse` itself passed — the failure is decode-side only.

### Blocker 2 — `tilelang` needs more shared memory than sm_120 has

Forcing both ends to tilelang (the combination used successfully on H20, and the one required by
the fp8-KV gate in #36904):

```
Set DSA backends for bfloat16 KV Cache: prefill=tilelang, decode=tilelang
tvm.error.InternalError: Failed to set the allowed dynamic shared memory size to 206848
```

```
requested   206,848 B  = 202 KB
available   102,400 B  = 100 KB   (hardware limit on sm_120)
```

This is a hard hardware limit, not configuration. It also means the **fp8 KV path of #36904 is
unreachable on sm_120**, since that gate requires tilelang on both ends.

### Reproduction

```bash
docker run --rm --gpus all --network host --ipc host --shm-size 32g \
  -v /path/to/GLM-5.3-Flash:/model:ro \
  -e SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM=0 \
  lmsysorg/sglang:glm-5.3-flash \
  python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path /model --trust-remote-code \
    --tp-size 8 --data-parallel-size 8 --enable-dp-attention --expert-parallel-size 8 \
    --disable-shared-experts-fusion --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm \
    --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 --mm-enable-dp-encoder --context-length 1048576
```

### Questions

1. Is sm_120 (RTX PRO 6000 / RTX 5090 class) intended to be supported for GLM-5.3-Flash?
2. If yes, is there a DSA backend combination that fits within 100 KB shared memory?
   `prefill=flashmla_sparse` works; which decode backends are validated on sm_120?
3. Should `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM` default be derived from `ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM`
   so the sm_120 exclusion is self-consistent?

title: [RFC] Decouple the SWA sidecar page size from the full-attention page size (DSv4, Hybrid Models)
body:
### Checklist

- [x] If this is not a feature request but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Motivation

#### Summary

Allow the sliding-window-attention (SWA) KV sidecar pool to use a physical page size that differs from the full-attention pool's `page_size`. Concretely, add a `swa_page_size` so a hybrid model can keep `page_size = 256` for full layers while paging the SWA sidecar at 128.

#### Motivation

For hybrid models (full-attention layers + sliding-window layers), SGLang splits the KV cache into a full pool and a SWA sidecar pool. Today the sidecar inherits the full pool's `page_size` (paged SWA mode requires `page_size == 256`).

A sliding window only keeps the most recent `W` tokens. When the sidecar is paged coarser than the window, capacity is rounded up to whole pages, and both the SWA KV pool and any per-page state pools are over-allocated. With a 128-token window paged at 256, that is ~2x over-allocation of the SWA-side pools — memory that could otherwise be effective KV token budget.

The page size cannot simply drop to 1: attention/state kernels require a kernel-friendly granularity. 128 is such a granularity, and halving the sidecar page (256 → 128) removes the rounding waste while staying kernel-compatible.

#### Proposal

Introduce a distinct `swa_page_size` for the sidecar, independent of the full pool `page_size`. Default: `swa_page_size == page_size` (no behavior change). A server flag opts a hybrid model into a finer sidecar (e.g. 128 against a 256 full page — a fixed 1:2 ratio).

#### Design

**Allocator (`SWATokenToKVPoolAllocator`).** Size the SWA sub-allocator and all SWA page accounting on `swa_page_size` instead of `page_size`:

- `new_pages_available` measures SWA headroom in `swa_page_size` units.
- `alloc_extend` / `alloc_decode` compute SWA new-page counts with `swa_page_size`, and pre-check both pools before allocating either, so a partial success never strands pages.
- Freeing generalizes to closed-form page arithmetic (`free_swa_pages`) keyed by `swa_page_size`. When the sidecar is *finer* than the full page, one full page spans several SWA pages; a `> 0` mapping mask dedups between the full-floored insert trim and the SWA-floored release frontier.

**Pool sizing.** Per-page state pools (sized as `swa_tokens / page * ring_size`) switch to `swa_page_size`, which is where the ~2x saving lands. Require `swa_tokens % swa_page_size == 0` so tail-slack accounting stays exact.

**Mapping.** The full→SWA index mapping preserves a token's in-page offset (both pools advance on the same `seq_lens`), so one full token every `swa_page_size` positions names exactly one distinct SWA page — the property the positional, sync-free frees rely on.

**Transfer & offload.** The same page granularity carries through the data paths, so the SWA side shrinks there too, not just in the pools:

- **PD disaggregation.** Both the prefill (sender) and decode (receiver) sides page the SWA window kv indices by `swa_page_size` (128), so the SWA KV moved over the wire is paged at the window granularity — no coarse-page over-transfer; the transmitted SWA volume roughly halves.
- **L3 offload.** When SWA KV is offloaded to the L3 tier it is written at `swa_page_size`, and the boundary full page's SWA sub-pages past the committed tail are freed by alignment rather than shipped, so the SWA footprint landing in L3 halves as well.
- **HiCache multi-tier transfer.** SWA pages move between the HiCache tiers at `swa_page_size` too, so every hop (GPU ↔ host ↔ remote/disk) carries half the SWA bytes.

#### Impact

- Frees SWA-side KV memory (~2x less over-allocation at the window boundary), raising effective token capacity for hybrid SWA models.
- No change when `swa_page_size == page_size` (the default).

### Related resources

_No response_

title: [tracking] thinking models + stop_sequences: five related defects — content loss, misreported stop_reason, enable_thinking ignored (PRs #33151–#33155)
body:
## Summary

When a thinking/reasoning model is used together with user stop sequences, five related defects
surface. Four are directly reproducible on the latest release; the fifth is masked by the first
one and only appears once it is fixed. Fixes are ready in five small, independently reviewable PRs:

| # | Defect | Symptom | PR |
|---|--------|---------|----|
| 1 | user stop checks are not skipped during the reasoning phase | a stop string mentioned *inside the thinking section* terminates generation; the final answer is never produced | #33152 |
| 2 | Anthropic adapter flattens user-stop and EOS into the same finish reason | `stop_reason` reports `end_turn` instead of `stop_sequence` (field missing) even though the user's stop sequence clearly matched | #33153 |
| 3 | reasoning parser classifies everything as reasoning when the think-end marker is missing | `content` is empty / no text block is emitted; all text lands in reasoning | #33154 |
| 4 | top-level `enable_thinking: false` is silently dropped (OpenAI route) | thinking cannot be disabled via the documented knob; the Anthropic route errors out instead — inconsistent behavior between routes | #33155 |
| 5 | stop-string trimming anchors on the first occurrence instead of the last | when the stop string also appears inside the thinking section, the answer is trimmed away entirely and only the first half of the thinking is returned | #33151 |

## Reliable reproducer

A system prompt asks the model to insert a fixed phrase at the end of the answer, and the tail of
that phrase is used as the stop sequence:

```json
{
  "max_tokens": 2000,
  "thinking": {"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": 1024},
  "stop_sequences": ["jingcai"],
  "messages": [
    {"role": "system", "content": "You MUST end your reply with the phrase 'fei chang jingcai!'"},
    {"role": "user", "content": "Hello, what model are you and what can you do?"}
  ]
}
```

(Original test used Chinese: system asks to insert `非常精彩！` at the end, stop sequence `精彩`,
model Qwen3-14B.)

Because the model inevitably quotes the phrase while planning its answer, the stop string appears
in **both** the thinking section and the final answer — exercising both hit paths deterministically.
Measured hit rate in our runs: 4 out of 5 requests triggered the stop, 2 in the thinking phase
(exposing defects 1/3) and 2 in the answer phase (exposing defect 2).

## Before / after (defect 1 + 3, Anthropic route)

Before:

```json
{ "content": [
    { "type": "thinking",
      "thinking": "...finally, remember to append the closing phrase \"fei chang " }
  ],
  "stop_reason": "end_turn" }
```

The thinking is cut mid-quote (the stop string matched inside it), and there is no text block at all.

After (#33152 + #33154): full thinking block + text block ending right before the stop string, and
`stop_reason: "stop_sequence"`.

## Before / after (defect 2, Anthropic route)

Before: the answer ends exactly at `...fei chang` (proof the stop sequence matched and was trimmed),
yet the response reports `"stop_reason": "end_turn"` and no `stop_sequence` field. Downstream
orchestration cannot distinguish "user-requested stop" from "model finished naturally".

After (#33153): `"stop_reason": "stop_sequence"`, `"stop_sequence": "<matched string>"`.

## Notes

- Defect 1 is a deliberate semantic choice (user stops delimit the final answer, not the thinking
  content); system EOS / think-end detection still runs during reasoning. Happy to discuss the
  intended behavior here.
- Defect 5 is masked by defect 1 on stock builds: once the stop string appears in the thinking
  section, defect 1 kills generation before trimming ever runs. It becomes observable only after
  #33152, verified on a patched deployment (Qwen3-14B).
- Related: #24839 (EOS inside thinking block) — same family, token-based path; closed without a
  real fix, covered by #33152.

## PRs

- #33151 — fix(detokenizer): use rfind to trim stop string at the actual hit point
- #33152 — fix(scheduler): skip user stop checks during the reasoning phase
- #33153 — fix(anthropic): report stop_sequence when user stop sequences match
- #33154 — fix(reasoning): avoid empty content when reasoning is truncated by a stop
- #33155 — fix(protocol): honor top-level enable_thinking field

All five are small and touch independent areas (scheduler / detokenizer / anthropic adapter /
reasoning parser / openai protocol). They were submitted on Aug 1 and have not received any review
yet — would a maintainer mind taking a look? Happy to rebase, split differently, or add tests as
needed.

title: [Roadmap] SGLang Prefill-Only 2026 CY26H1 and CY26H2 Design Proposal & Roadmap
body:
# Context
In the previous milestone ([#5973](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/5973), [#6460](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/6460)), Our community introduced the Scoring API into SGLang with several key implementation and optimization PRs:
1. [Tokenizer] Batch Tokenization —[ #5141](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/5141)
2. [Tokenizer] Dynamic Batch Tokenizer —[ #9382](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/9382)
3. [ZMQ] Batch Send from Tokenizer Manager —[ #9436](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/9436)
4. [Generative Score API] Remove Decode path —[ #8840](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/8840)
5. [Generative Score API] Prefill-only optimizations —[ #9748](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/9748)
6. [Benchmark] Prefill-only benchmarking scripts —[ #10240](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/10240)
7. [Garbage Collection] Memory optimization —[ #9241](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/9241)
8. [Generative Score API] Multi-item scoring with custom attention mask —[ #10979](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/10979)

# Goal
Our goal is to make Prefill-only inference in SGLang a first-class, production-ready execution path for scoring and other non-generative workloads.
1. Usability – Offer a simple, consistent Scoring API across model types (e.g., CausalLM, SequenceClassification, Bert based).
2. Performance – Deliver predictable, high-throughput, low-latency Prefill-only execution via efficient batching, KV reuse, and cache-aware optimizations, while matching HuggingFace reference correctness.

### Legend
  - [SignedUp] – Actively planned and driven by the SGLang Prefill-only contributor teams (LinkedIn and TikTok)
  - [Open for Contribution] – Community contributions welcome

# Call for Contributions
## Functionality
- [x]  [SignedUp] Overlap scheduling for non-generation paths (Embeddings and Sequence Classification)  —  #14032 @satyamk7054 
- [x] [SignedUp] Add support to enable lora with embedding models  —  #17780 @vedantjh2 
- [ ] [SignedUp] Support additional pooling types (e.g., MEAN pooling) for embedding models @satyamk7054 
- [ ] [SignedUp] Support additional encoding and response formats (e.g., base64, bytes, torch.Tensor) for non-generation models @satyamk7054 
- [x] [SignedUp] Add Scoring API support for SequenceClassification models (e.g., Qwen3ForSequenceClassification) @sundar24295s  - #22118 
- [x] [SignedUp] Support hybrid input formats, including mixed tokens + embeddings for both queries and items @fortunecookiee - #20960
- [x] [SignedUp] [Score API] Add return_pooled_hidden_states to Scoring API for SequenceClassification / RewardModel #22427
- [ ] [SignedUp] Enable Radix Cache and Hi-Cache for multi-item scoring scenarios @bluecoffee8 
- [x ] Return token usage from /v1/score API [Feature Request](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/18132)
- [ ] [SignedUp] [Feature] Setwise scoring for a single set @sundar24295s
