title: [Feature] deepseek_v2.py Refactor
body:
## Motivation
After months of development, the file `deepseek_v2.py` has grown to more than 4k lines of codes. As the key part for a series of popular MoE models (DeepSeek V3/V3.1/V3.2 family, Kimi-K2 family, Mistral-Large-3 family), this file deserves careful cleaning and refactoring to ensure its maintainability and extensibility.

## Current Structure of `deepseek_v2.py`

- Importing packages and device flag setting (~150 lines)  
- Definition of different attention forwarding methods (MHA, MLA, Chunked MHA etc...), and how each attention backend gets routed to these forward methods (~200 lines)
- MLP/MoE layer implementation (~800 lines)
- MLA layer implementation (~1500 lines)
    - About 900 lines are implementation of different attention forward methods
- Weight loading logics (~600 lines)
- Decoder Layer/whole model level implementation  (~500 lines)
- Other small functions (~300 lines)

## Parts for Improvement
- Many standalone modules can be extracted from modeling logic, and deserves a single file. Including:
    - Definition/Implementation of different attention methods
    - Routing strategy of different attention backends
    - NSA(V3.2) specific logics
    - Weight loading logics
    - Util functions
- There are too many if-else branches from different hardware platforms (AMD/NPU/CPU)

## Folder structure after Refactoring


```
├── deepseek_common
│   ├── attention_backend_handler.py
│   ├── attention_forward_methods
|   |   ├── forward_methods.py
│   │   ├── forward_mha.py
│   │   ├── forward_mla_cpu.py
│   │   ├── forward_mla.py
│   │   └── forward_mla_rocm.py
│   ├── hardware_backend
│   │   ├── deepseek_v2_amd_mixin.py
│   │   ├── deepseek_v2_cpu_mixin.py
│   │   └── deepseek_v2_npu_mixin.py
│   ├── utils.py
│   ├── v32_mixin.py
│   └── weight_loader_mixin.py
├── deepseek_v2.py
├── deepseek.py
...
```

For refactoring, we need to split the original `deepseek_v2.py` into these files or subfolders for mixin Classes:
-  `attention_backend_handler.py`: MLA routing logic on different attention backends
-  `attention_methods`: implementation of different attention forward methods. Including MHA (forward_normal), MLA (forward_absorb) and variants on other hardware platforms.
-  `hardware_backend`: mixin classes for different hardware platforms (AMD/NPU/CPU)
-  `utils.py`: util functions
-  `weight_loader.py`: weight loading logics
-  `v32_mixin.py`:  V3.2 related logics

In the original `deepseek_v2.py`, we keep the definition of basic blocks, like `DeepseekV2AttentionMLA` or `DeepseekV2MoE`, so the places importing these classes will not be broken.

For refactor of multiple hardware backends, `MultiPlatformOp` might be another way to simplify the codes. We should choose the one working better.


## Further Refactor

After the file has been split and stabilized. We can try to optimize the structure with some carefully designed abstractions. 

For example, we can create a class for attention_forward_method. It might include methods for different hardware, such as `forward_prepare_cuda`, `forward_core_cuda`, `forward_prepare_npu`, etc... So most of the if-else structures inside the forward logics can be replaced.



## Refactor Checklist
- [x]  Migrate MHA attention method #16817
- [x]  Migrate MLA attention method #19122
- [x] Attention backend handler #16306
- [x] Hardware backend  Rocm: #31531
- [ ] V32 Logics #16815
- [x] Weight Loader #16291
- [x] Util functions #16701

title: [RFC] Add CI Infrastructure for the SGLang MLU Backend
body: ## 1. Motivation The SGLang MLU backend needs a CI mechanism to keep its functionality continuously usable. Changes to MLU-specific code, as well as changes to shared SGLang components used by the MLU backend, can introduce regressions. Relevant pull requests therefore need to trigger MLU tests so that functional correctness is validated before the changes are merged. The MLU hardware and its supporting execution environment are accessible only from Cambricon's internal network and cannot be attached directly to GitHub-hosted runners. This RFC proposes a CI architecture that connects the public SGLang GitHub workflows to the internal Jenkins and MLU cluster while preserving the internal network boundary. The resulting CI lane makes MLU validation visible to the SGLang community and helps maintain the backend's functional availability as the project evolves. ## 2. Summary This RFC proposes community-visible PR and Nightly CI infrastructure for the Cambricon MLU backend in SGLang. The integration connects GitHub Actions to an internally operated Jenkins and MLU cluster without exposing Jenkins or internal infrastructure to the public Internet. The corresponding implementation is tracked in [sgl-project/sglang#26898](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/26898). The proposed CI infrastructure has these properties: - Pull requests run only after the existing `run-ci` gate and the `run-ci-mlu` opt-in label pass. - During the initial observation period, the PR lane is a non-required check and does not block pull requests from being merged. - Test failures fail the GitHub job and remain visible as code-related failures. - Infrastructure failures and MLU resource queue timeouts are reported with a warning annotation, while the GitHub job concludes successfully because contributors cannot repair the private CI infrastructure. - Nightly and trusted manual/default-branch runs remain strict. - Results distinguish test failures, infrastructure failures, and timeouts. - Jenkins logs and structured result metadata are uploaded as GitHub artifacts when the GitHub job has started and reaches the upload step. - PR and Nightly jobs use separate labels in a dedicated runner group and run on one-job ephemeral self-hosted GitHub Actions runners on the VPS. - The PR workflow runs with `pull_request_target`, so its YAML and reusable gate come from the reviewed base branch. - The self-hosted runner never checks out or executes client code from the pull request. The proposal is intended to begin with an observation period. It does not ask SGLang maintainers to make the MLU lane required at initial rollout. ## 3. Proposed Architecture The architecture consists of four modules across three trust zones: public GitHub, the VPS, and the trusted internal network containing the controller, Jenkins, and MLU resources. ### 3.1 GitHub Community The SGLang-side integration includes PR and Nightly workflows, the existing `run-ci` gate and the `run-ci-mlu` opt-in label, and a reliability reporting workflow. GitHub Actions dispatches eligible MLU CI jobs and displays their status, annotations, logs, and artifacts to contributors. ### 3.2 VPS The VPS hosts: - a GitHub Actions runner provisioner; - one PR runner slot and one Nightly runner slot; - a task submission bridge and task/status store; - a trusted, preinstalled `sglang-mlu-ci` client. `sglang-mlu-ci` is an operator-installed command-line client invoked by the GitHub workflow. It submits validated task metadata, polls for progress, and publishes the final result without fetching or executing pull request code. ### 3.3 Internal Controller The internal controller retrieves pending tasks from the VPS, coordinates their execution in Jenkins, and returns status and logs. It also provides a runner broker that issues restricted JIT configurations for ephemeral runners. GitHub Actions has no direct access to Jenkins or MLU resources, and communication with internal services is initiated from within Cambricon's network. ### 3.4 Jenkins / MLU Cluster Jenkins receives the repository URL, immutable commit SHA, task ID, and trigger type. It checks out the exact SHA in an isolated MLU pod, prepares the MLU backend dependencies, and runs the registered PR or Nightly test suites. Execution status and logs are returned through the internal controller. ## 4. GitHub Workflow Policy ### 4.1 Trigger Policy The workflow uses `pull_request_target` so the workflow definition and reusable gate are loaded from the reviewed base branch. It never checks out the pull request or executes repository code on the self-hosted runner. The untrusted repository URL and immutable head SHA are passed only as data to the trusted client, and PR code is executed later in the isolated Jenkins MLU pod. The MLU PR job is entered only when: 1. the PR targets `main`; 2. the PR has the `run-ci-mlu` label, an explicit opt-in for the MLU lane; 3. the PR is not a draft; 4. the PR has the `run-ci` label; 5. the existing PR gate and rate-limit policy pass. The label check runs at gate time with a live fetch of the pull request's current labels, so a rerun after adding `run-ci-mlu` picks up the new label set; the workflow also re-fires when `run-ci` or `run-ci-mlu` is added. > [!IMPORTANT] > SGLang maintainers must review and merge the MLU workflow files into the default branch before the PR and Nightly lanes can run. GitHub loads `pull_request_target`, `schedule`, and `workflow_dispatch` definitions from the default branch. This bootstrap also prevents a pull request from replacing the commands executed on the self-hosted runner. ### 4.2 Lane Isolation The Organization runner group is named `mlu-ci` and is restricted to the SGLang repository. The jobs select it as follows: ```yaml # Pull requests runs-on: group: mlu-ci labels: mlu-pr # Nightly runs-on: group: mlu-ci labels: mlu-nightly ``` Separate labels prevent a long Nightly GitHub job from occupying the PR runner slot. Each lane has one provisioner in the initial deployment, so the maximum GitHub-side concurrency is one PR job and one Nightly job. ### 4.3 Initial Observe-Only PR Policy During the initial observation period, the MLU PR lane is a non-required check. Its result policy is: | Result | GitHub annotation | PR job conclusion | Reason | | ---------------------------------- | ----------------- | ----------------- | ------ | | Success | none | success | MLU validation completed successfully. | | `test/pytest` | error | failure | A test executed and failed, indicating a possible code regression. | | Invalid request or source metadata | error | failure | The requested source cannot be safely or correctly tested. | | `infrastructure/*` | warning | success | Private CI infrastructure is unavailable and cannot be repaired by the contributor. | | `timeout/mlu_resource_queue` | warning | success | No MLU resource became available within the queue time budget. | | `timeout/external_task` | warning | success | The VPS task did not reach a terminal state within its active-task time budget. | | `timeout/github_client` | warning | success | The GitHub-side client did not receive a terminal result within its time budget. | | `timeout/jenkins_task` | error | failure | An executing Jenkins task exceeded its time budget, which may indicate a hung or regressed test. | Test failures remain visible as failing checks, but they do not block merging while the lane is non-required. Infrastructure failures conclude successfully with a warning because contributors cannot repair the private CI infrastructure. `timeout/jenkins_task` remains a failure because it indicates that an executing test may have hung or regressed. MLU resource queue timeout is advisory because a contributor cannot make internal hardware available. No automatic retry is proposed during the initial observation period. Returning a warning avoids blocking the PR, while not retrying prevents duplicate Jenkins work and makes infrastructure reliability visible in the data. An automatic single retry can be considered after the observation period. Nightly, default-branch, and trusted manual runs use strict conclusions so infrastructure operators still receive a red signal when the lane is unhealthy. ## 5. Test Scope PR validation currently uses: - `pr-test-1-mlu`: tests requiring one MLU device; - `pr-test-2-mlu`: tests requiring two MLU devices. Additional test cases and suites can be added as MLU coverage requirements evolve. Nightly uses the independent `nightly-test-mlu` suite. ## 6. Failure Classification and Reporting The status is not limited to pass/fail. The task result carries: ```json { "status": "error", "failure_type": "timeout", "failure_stage": "mlu_resource_queue", "observe_only": true, "github_conclusion": "success", "task_id": "" } ``` The main classifications include: | Failure type | Example stages | Meaning | | --- | --- | --- | | `test` | `pytest` | A test executed and failed | | `infrastructure` | `jenkins_connect`, `internal_poller`, `runner_client`, `vps_bridge` | CI infrastructure could not execute or report the test normally | | `timeout` | `mlu_resource_queue`, `jenkins_task`, `external_task`, `github_client` | A named layer exceeded its time budget | | `request` | `task_submission` | The submitted repository/ref/SHA metadata was invalid | The classification is emitted in four places: 1. the live Actions console log; 2. a GitHub warning or error annotation; 3. the GitHub step summary; 4. `result-.json` in the uploaded artifact. An example line is: ```text MLU CI failure classification: type=timeout, stage=mlu_resource_queue ``` ## 7. Log Streaming, Artifact Upload, and Retention The internal master incrementally reads the Jenkins console log and sends log chunks to the VPS task store. The trusted client polls for new log bytes and prints them to the GitHub Actions console. At terminal status, it downloads the complete log and writes: ```text jenkins-.log result-.json ``` The workflow upload step uses `if: always()` and `actions/upload-artifact@v4`. Result metadata is also uploaded as a separate small `mlu-ci-result-pr--` artifact with 30-day retention, so the weekly reporter does not need to download the complete Jenkins log. Artifact upload is best-effort rather than unconditional. It works for normal success, test failure, classified infrastructure failure, and classified timeout after the GitHub job has started. It cannot run when: - no runner ever claims the GitHub job; - the runner host or runner process is terminated before the upload step; - GitHub's artifact service itself is unavailable. To provide a recovery window, failed tasks and their logs remain on the VPS for 72 hours by default. The duration is configurable by the operator. Successful tasks are removed after complete log download. A successful task with incomplete log download is also retained for the recovery window. GitHub artifact retention remains controlled by the SGLang repository's Actions retention setting. ## 8. Timeout Budget The PR timeout budget is intentionally ordered from the execution layer outward: | Layer | PR timeout | | --------------------------------------------- | ----------: | | Internal poller claim | 5 minutes | | Continuous Jenkins unavailability | 5 minutes | | Jenkins pipeline, including MLU resource wait | 100 minutes | | VPS active task | 105 minutes | | Trusted GitHub client | 110 minutes | | GitHub Actions job | 120 minutes | This leaves time for the inner layer to publish a classified terminal result and for outer layers to drain logs and upload artifacts. Nightly has an independent longer budget: | Layer | Nightly timeout | | --------------------- | --------------: | | Jenkins Nightly task | 420 minutes | | VPS active task | 435 minutes | | Trusted GitHub client | 450 minutes | | GitHub Actions job | 480 minutes | ## 9. Ephemeral Runner Provisioning Each ephemeral runner requires a fresh GitHub JIT configuration, and the GitHub API that issues this configuration requires Organization-level self-hosted runner management permission. To keep this permission off the VPS, an internal broker uses a GitHub App with only: ```text Organization permission: Self-hosted runners, read and write Repository permissions: no additional permissions ``` The broker fixes the Organization, runner group, and allowed lane labels. The VPS can request only an `mlu-pr` or `mlu-nightly` JIT configuration and cannot use the broker to create runners with arbitrary access. The GitHub App credentials remain inside the internal network. Each runner is configured as ephemeral and processes at most one GitHub job. After it exits, the provisioner uses the broker to remove the old registration and obtain a JIT configuration for its replacement. Stale registrations are also removed without affecting runners outside the configured group and label boundary. The expected steady state is two registered runners: one PR runner and one Nightly runner. Runner IDs changing after jobs is expected; an ever-growing list of offline runners is not. > [!IMPORTANT] > Production rollout requires cooperation from `sgl-project` Organization administrators to authorize the restricted `mlu-ci` runner group and install the runner-provisioning GitHub App. SGLang repository maintainers must also keep the MLU PR check non-required during the initial observation period, as described in Section 4.3. ## 10. Security Model ### 10.1 GitHub Permissions and Credentials - The workflows declare explicit, minimal, read-only `GITHUB_TOKEN` permissions. - No repository write credential is installed on the self-hosted runner or passed to pull request code. - The runner-provisioning GitHub App has no repository permissions; it has only the Organization-level self-hosted runner permission required to manage ephemeral runners. - The VPS has no GitHub Organization credential and can request runners only for the predefined MLU runner group and lane labels through the broker. As a result, the MLU CI infrastructure cannot modify repository code, pull requests, or issues. An infrastructure outage can affect only the availability and reporting of the MLU lane. A compromise of the runner-provisioning GitHub App could affect Organization runner registrations, but it would not grant access to repository content or repository write operations. ### 10.2 Trusted Runner Code The self-hosted job does not run `actions/checkout` for the pull request. It invokes a preinstalled `sglang-mlu-ci` command deployed from a trusted infrastructure revision. The workflow passes only validated metadata: repository name, GitHub HTTPS clone URL, and full commit SHA. The `pull_request_target` workflow and its local reusable gate are loaded from the base branch. A pull request therefore cannot replace the `run:` block that invokes the trusted client. The workflow has explicit read-only permissions and does not expose repository or infrastructure secrets. The pull request code is fetched and executed only inside the isolated Jenkins MLU pod. Jenkins checks out the immutable SHA and verifies that `HEAD` matches it. ### 10.3 Remaining Trust Assumptions - The VPS, internal controller, Jenkins, and MLU pod isolation are managed by the Cambricon MLU CI maintainers and are treated as trusted infrastructure in this proposal. - The MLU workflow on the default branch has passed normal SGLang review. - The dedicated runner group remains restricted to the intended repository/workflow. ## 11. Operations and Response SLA The proposed primary community contact is `@chenxb002`. The response target applies to infrastructure-classified failures, repeated MLU resource queue timeouts, and runner unavailability. It does not apply to test failures caused by the code under test. During the observe-only period, the Cambricon MLU CI maintainers will: - acknowledge a reported or monitored infrastructure incident within one business day; - restore the affected lane, temporarily disable it, or publish a status update within two business days (worst case); - publish a follow-up when service is restored. While an infrastructure incident remains unresolved, the PR lane remains non-required and infrastructure-classified results do not block pull requests. These are proposed response targets rather than an uptime guarantee and should be confirmed by the named contact and SGLang maintainers during RFC review. ## 12. Reliability Visibility Infrastructure failures remain visible even when the PR conclusion is successful. A scheduled workflow aggregates only PR-lane runs and appends a reliability report to the public RFC issue. The report is published weekly while the lane remains observe-only. The report includes: - total triggered, started, completed, cancelled, and unclaimed jobs; - success and test-failure counts; - counts grouped by `failure_type` and `failure_stage`; - MLU queue timeout count; - median and p95 queue/completion time where available; - artifact and structured metadata coverage among jobs that started. Failure classifications come from the structured result artifact and are combined with GitHub run and job metadata. Jobs that never receive a runner or never upload result metadata are reported separately rather than silently excluded, allowing the community to distinguish runner assignment, reporting coverage, and classified CI reliability. The reporter runs only on GitHub-hosted runners. Report collection is read-only, while a separate publishing job receives `issues: write` only to append the report comment; the MLU PR workflow remains read-only. Every report is also available in the step summary and as Markdown/JSON artifacts. Each run creates a new issue comment so the community can compare historical snapshots. ## 13. Demonstrated Behavior > [!NOTE] > The following evidence was collected in the public [`sglang-mlu/sglang`](https://github.com/sglang-mlu/sglang) fork, which deploys the trusted-workflow, observe-only policy, and ephemeral-runner architecture proposed in this RFC. All demo pull requests, workflow runs, jobs, annotations, and artifacts linked in this section come from that fork. ### 13.1 Successful PR Run The final trusted-workflow and ephemeral-runner architecture successfully validated pull request [#5](https://github.com/sglang-mlu/sglang/pull/5): - [workflow run](https://github.com/sglang-mlu/sglang/actions/runs/30064140061), triggered by `pull_request_target` for commit `58bef9b52280d8637867bdb7e64608c35d8e2f4d`; - [`pr-test-mlu` job](https://github.com/sglang-mlu/sglang/actions/runs/30064140061/job/89391687467), completed successfully on an ephemeral runner with label `mlu-pr` in the dedicated `mlu-ci` runner group; - the MLU task, result metadata upload, and Jenkins log upload steps all completed successfully; - both `mlu-ci-result-pr-30064140061-1` and `mlu-jenkins-log-pr-30064140061-1` artifacts were created. ### 13.2 Successful Nightly Run The strict Nightly lane successfully validated the same commit: - [workflow run](https://github.com/sglang-mlu/sglang/actions/runs/30064649714), manually triggered for commit `58bef9b52280d8637867bdb7e64608c35d8e2f4d`; - [`nightly-test-mlu` job](https://github.com/sglang-mlu/sglang/actions/runs/30064649714/job/89393132734), completed successfully on an ephemeral runner with label `mlu-nightly` in the dedicated `mlu-ci` runner group; - the Nightly MLU task and Jenkins log upload steps both completed successfully; - the `mlu-jenkins-log-nightly-30064649714-1` artifact was created. ### 13.3 Intentional Test Failure Pull request [#6](https://github.com/sglang-mlu/sglang/pull/6) added a deterministic failing test to verify that a pytest failure remains red and is propagated through Jenkins: - [workflow run](https://github.com/sglang-mlu/sglang/actions/runs/30065563358), triggered by `pull_request_target` for commit `2400a0a9cd73c11540923a765787f4ce53fc2c2b`; - [`pr-test-mlu` job](https://github.com/sglang-mlu/sglang/actions/runs/30065563358/job/89395751493), failed as expected while both artifact upload steps completed successfully; - the Actions log identified `TestMLUCIFailureDemo::test_intentional_failure_reaches_github_actions` and showed the intentional `AssertionError`; - the failure annotation reported `MLU CI failure classification: type=test, stage=pytest`; - both `mlu-ci-result-pr-30065563358-1` and `mlu-jenkins-log-pr-30065563358-1` artifacts were created. This confirms that observe-only handling does not mask test failures: a code-related test failure still produces a failing GitHub conclusion. ### 13.4 Jenkins Unavailable Pull request [#7](https://github.com/sglang-mlu/sglang/pull/7) validated the observe-only behavior when the internal controller could not connect to Jenkins. For this experiment, the controller was temporarily pointed at an unreachable local endpoint; the Jenkins service itself was not stopped: - [workflow run](https://github.com/sglang-mlu/sglang/actions/runs/30068996587), triggered by `pull_request_target` for commit `42bfa1145c3a6a770a923844ccb954fb754dc1a3`; - [`pr-test-mlu` job](https://github.com/sglang-mlu/sglang/actions/runs/30068996587/job/89405643748), completed successfully after the five-minute Jenkins availability deadline; - the warning annotation reported `MLU CI failure classification: type=infrastructure, stage=jenkins_connect`; - the MLU task step and both artifact upload steps completed successfully under the observe-only policy; - both `mlu-ci-result-pr-30068996587-1` and `mlu-jenkins-log-pr-30068996587-1` artifacts were created. This confirms that an internal Jenkins outage remains visible as a warning and structured infrastructure result without making the contributor's PR job fail. ### 13.5 MLU Resource Queue Timeout Pull request [#8](https://github.com/sglang-mlu/sglang/pull/8) validated the observe-only behavior when Jenkins accepted the build but could not schedule an MLU worker. For this experiment, the pipeline temporarily used an unavailable MLU label and a five-minute outer timeout: - [workflow run](https://github.com/sglang-mlu/sglang/actions/runs/30069671544), triggered by `pull_request_target` for commit `a01f381b84b04c5e28197e2f88669c0f3515f240`; - [`pr-test-mlu` job](https://github.com/sglang-mlu/sglang/actions/runs/30069671544/job/89407780967), completed successfully after the Jenkins resource queue timeout; - the warning annotation reported `MLU CI failure classification: type=timeout, stage=mlu_resource_queue`; - the MLU task step and both artifact upload steps completed successfully under the observe-only policy; - both `mlu-ci-result-pr-30069671544-1` and `mlu-jenkins-log-pr-30069671544-1` artifacts were created. This confirms that unavailable internal MLU capacity remains visible as a classified timeout without blocking the contributor's PR. ### 13.6 Internal Poller Unavailable Pull request [#9](https://github.com/sglang-mlu/sglang/pull/9) validated the observe-only behavior when the VPS accepted a task but the internal controller was unavailable to claim it. For this experiment, only the internal task poller was stopped; the GitHub runner, VPS services, runner broker, and Jenkins remained available: - [workflow run](https://github.com/sglang-mlu/sglang/actions/runs/30070992748), triggered by `pull_request_target` for commit `1ff76ae934036c7aed99d497b35c60b327d824b1`; - [`pr-test-mlu` job](https://github.com/sglang-mlu/sglang/actions/runs/30070992748/job/89411696723), completed successfully after the five-minute task claim deadline; - the warning annotation reported `MLU CI failure classification: type=infrastructure, stage=internal_poller`; - no Jenkins build was created because the task was never claimed by the internal controller; - both `mlu-ci-result-pr-30070992748-1` and `mlu-jenkins-log-pr-30070992748-1` artifacts were created. This confirms that an unavailable internal poller is reported as a visible infrastructure warning without blocking the contributor's PR or silently losing the task. ## 14. Feedback Requested Feedback and suggestions are welcome. This proposal will be revised based on community discussion and the refreshed demonstration results.

title: [Feature] Native SM120 (Blackwell) support for flash_mla_sparse_fwd (DeepSeek-V4 sparse-attention prefill)
body:
### Describe the feature / gap

`DeepseekV4AttnBackend._forward_prefill_sparse()` (`sglang/srt/layers/attention/deepseek_v4_backend.py`) routes DeepSeek-V4 sparse-attention prefill through `flash_mla_sparse_fwd` (from `sgl_kernel.flash_mla`). This kernel unconditionally raises:

```
RuntimeError: Sparse Attention Forward Kernel is only supported on SM90a and SM100f architectures.
```

on any other compute capability, including **SM120 (Blackwell, e.g. RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q)**. Since PR #29775 ("[DeepSeek V4] Enable FlashMLA sparse prefill by default", merged into `lmsysorg/sglang:latest` as of v0.5.15.post1) flipped `SGLANG_OPT_FLASHMLA_SPARSE_PREFILL`'s default from `False` to `True`, this now fires unconditionally for DeepSeek-V4 on SM120 hardware — the model cannot serve any request through the default `dsv4` attention backend without the workaround below.

This is a **feature request for native SM120 support**, not a duplicate of #29900. #29900 documents the identical error text but strictly as a *test-suite gating gap* (`test_flashmla.py` needs a compute-capability skip so the 20 already-expected-unsupported failures don't drown out real bugs) — it explicitly does not ask for SM120 support to be implemented, only for the test to skip cleanly. This issue asks for the underlying capability itself.

### Environment

- GPU: 2x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q (SM120), 97,887 MiB each
- Image: `lmsysorg/sglang:latest` resolving to sglang v0.5.15.post1
- Model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash, `--attention-backend dsv4`, `--tp-size 2`

### Evidence an SM120-compatible code path is already partially plausible

The **decode-path** kernel (`flash_mla_with_kvcache`) already has an SM120 branch (`flash_mla_with_kvcache_sm120`, added in sglang v0.5.13 via PR #24692), reachable via `SGLANG_SM120_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=triton`. Setting `SGLANG_OPT_FLASHMLA_SPARSE_PREFILL=0` (to opt back out of the sparse-prefill default) together with `SGLANG_SM120_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=triton` avoids the unsupported sparse-prefill kernel entirely and routes decode through the existing Triton SM120 fallback — this combination, plus `--mem-fraction-static` tuned to ~0.98 (headroom for the Triton autotune scratch buffer) and `--disable-cuda-graph`/`--skip-server-warmup`, lets DeepSeek-V4-Flash serve real inference requests end-to-end on SM120 today. We verified this empirically with two successful `POST /v1/chat/completions` requests returning valid completions end-to-end.

This confirms an SM120-compatible execution path already exists for the decode side of FlashMLA — it seems plausible the same Triton (or an equivalent) approach could be extended/hardened to cover the sparse-*prefill* kernel (`flash_mla_sparse_fwd`) as well, rather than requiring every SM120 user to discover and apply this env-var combination themselves.

Precedent that SM120-dispatch PRs are accepted for adjacent kernels: PR #28125 ("feat(moe): add SM120/SM121 dispatch for fp8_blockwise_scaled_grouped_mm"), referenced from #29900's `test_fp8_blockwise_moe.py` findings.

### Request

Either:
1. Add native SM120 support to `flash_mla_sparse_fwd` (mirroring the existing `flash_mla_with_kvcache_sm120` decode-path support), or
2. If native support isn't planned near-term, document `SGLANG_OPT_FLASHMLA_SPARSE_PREFILL=0` + `SGLANG_SM120_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=triton` as an official, supported fallback for SM120 users running DeepSeek-V4 so it isn't discovered ad hoc.

Related: #29900 (test-gate gap for the same error, not a fix request), #29897, PR #28125 (SM120 dispatch precedent for a different kernel).

title: [Bug] --enable-expert-distribution-metrics + EAGLE speculative-num-steps >= 2 crash-loops at startup: recorder pass boundary runs inside draft CUDA-graph capture
body:
### Checklist

- [x] 1. I have searched related issues but cannot get the expected help.
- [x] 2. The bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] 3. Please note that if the bug-related issue you submitted lacks corresponding environment info and a minimal reproducible demo, it will be challenging for us to reproduce and address it, reducing the likelihood of receiving feedback.
- [x] 4. If the issue you raised is not a bug but a question, please raise a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions/new/choose Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] 5. Please use English, otherwise it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

Enabling `--enable-expert-distribution-metrics` on a MoE model served with EAGLE/MTP speculative decoding and `--speculative-num-steps >= 2` crash-loops the server during startup CUDA-graph capture:

```
torch.AcceleratorError: CUDA error: operation not permitted when stream is capturing   (cudaErrorStreamCaptureUnsupported)
→ CUDA error: operation failed due to a previous error during capture                  (cudaErrorStreamCaptureInvalidated)
→ Exception: Capture cuda graph failed
```

The identical configuration with `--speculative-num-steps 1` starts and serves fine (explanation below). Observed in production on v0.5.15.post1 (GLM-5.2 NVFP4 quant, 8×B200, TP8, EAGLE steps=3 / topk=1 / draft-tokens=4, using GLM's built-in MTP layer as the draft). The involved code is unchanged on `main` @ `108a183f6b` — all permalinks below point there.

#### Root cause

1. `--enable-expert-distribution-metrics` auto-starts recording at recorder construction ([expert_distribution.py#L161-L165](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/108a183f6bdd2035e649f6812c17ddb3193ebd65/python/sglang/srt/eplb/expert_distribution.py#L161-L165); the flag alone auto-sets `expert_distribution_recorder_mode="stat"`, [server_args.py#L5454-L5458](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/108a183f6bdd2035e649f6812c17ddb3193ebd65/python/sglang/srt/server_args.py#L5454-L5458)). The recorder is created by the target `ModelRunner.initialize()` ([model_runner.py#L677-L683](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/108a183f6bdd2035e649f6812c17ddb3193ebd65/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py#L677-L683)) and shared process-globally, so it is already recording when the scheduler later captures the spec-decode graphs (`init_tp_model_worker` → `maybe_init_draft_worker` → `init_all_cuda_graphs`, [scheduler.py#L850-L857](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/108a183f6bdd2035e649f6812c17ddb3193ebd65/python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py#L850-L857)).
2. EAGLE draft graph capture drives the **full `ModelRunner.forward`** inside the capture: `EagleDraftCudaGraphRunner.capture_one_shape` → `run_once()` → `eagle_worker.draft_forward` ([eagle_draft_cuda_graph_runner.py#L430-L450](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/108a183f6bdd2035e649f6812c17ddb3193ebd65/python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_draft_cuda_graph_runner.py#L430-L450)), and `draft_forward` calls `self.draft_runner.forward(forward_batch)` once per draft step, breaking before the forward on the last step ([eagle_worker_v2.py#L654-L694](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/108a183f6bdd2035e649f6812c17ddb3193ebd65/python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py#L654-L694)). So `speculative_num_steps >= 2` ⇒ at least one full `ModelRunner.forward` inside the capture (`torch.cuda.graph` context in [full_cuda_graph_backend.py#L89-L114](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/108a183f6bdd2035e649f6812c17ddb3193ebd65/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner_backend/full_cuda_graph_backend.py#L89-L114)).
3. `ModelRunner.forward` wraps every forward in `with_forward_pass(...)` — its only call site, not gated on `is_draft_worker` ([model_runner.py#L3002-L3024](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/108a183f6bdd2035e649f6812c17ddb3193ebd65/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py#L3002-L3024)) — which runs `_on_forward_pass_start` / `_on_forward_pass_end` ([expert_distribution.py#L193-L207](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/108a183f6bdd2035e649f6812c17ddb3193ebd65/python/sglang/srt/eplb/expert_distribution.py#L193-L207)).
4. The pass-end bookkeeping is not capture-safe. With metrics enabled, `_UtilizationRateAccumulatorMixin._append_utilization_rate` performs a rank-0 GPU→CPU sync — `utilization_rate_gpu.item()` ([expert_distribution.py#L746](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/108a183f6bdd2035e649f6812c17ddb3193ebd65/python/sglang/srt/eplb/expert_distribution.py#L746)) — which raises `cudaErrorStreamCaptureUnsupported` and invalidates the capture. The production traceback below shows this frame exactly. (The `torch.distributed.reduce` at [#L729](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/108a183f6bdd2035e649f6812c17ddb3193ebd65/python/sglang/srt/eplb/expert_distribution.py#L729) executed without raising first — but a default-PG collective plus the accumulator buffer writes at the pass boundary would in any case be baked into the draft graph and replayed on every draft step, which is not intended either.)

#### Why `--speculative-num-steps 1` is unaffected

`draft_forward` breaks before the forward on the last step ⇒ zero in-capture `ModelRunner.forward` calls. The draft-extend capture invokes the bare `model.forward` ([eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py#L422](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/108a183f6bdd2035e649f6812c17ddb3193ebd65/python/sglang/srt/speculative/eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py#L422)), as do the decode and prefill graph runners — so the recorder pass boundary never runs inside those captures. We ran a steps=1 fleet with metrics enabled for days without issue while the steps=3 fleet crash-looped on every start.

```
Exception: Capture cuda graph failed: CUDA error: operation failed due to a previous error during capture
```

</details>

#### Workarounds

- Drop `--enable-expert-distribution-metrics` (the mitigation we run in production), or
- `--speculative-num-steps 1`.

#### Proposed fix

Skip the forward-pass boundary while a stream capture is active, mirroring `_on_hook`, which is already capture-aware by design ([expert_distribution.py#L235-L247](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/108a183f6bdd2035e649f6812c17ddb3193ebd65/python/sglang/srt/eplb/expert_distribution.py#L235-L247)): per-layer hooks intentionally stay active during capture so the captured graphs keep accumulating into the gatherer buffers at replay — only the pass-boundary bookkeeping (reset / collect / accumulator append with its collective + host sync) must be skipped. There is same-file precedent for keeping recorder bookkeeping out of draft capture: `disable_routed_experts_capture_for_draft` ([model_runner.py#L707-L710](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/108a183f6bdd2035e649f6812c17ddb3193ebd65/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py#L707-L710)). PR incoming.

Alternatives considered: deferring the auto `start_record()` until after startup capture fixes only this instance (any future in-capture `ModelRunner.forward` would regress) and changes when recording starts; wrapping `draft_forward` in `disable_this_region()` would also silence per-layer hooks for EAGLE3 MoE draft models, changing recorded data.

#### Side notes (kept out of the fix PR to stay minimal)

- `_append_utilization_rate` has a stray debug `print(f"hi {self._rank=} {utilization_rate_gpu=}")` on the `SGLANG_ENABLE_EPLB_BALANCEDNESS_METRIC` path ([expert_distribution.py#L740](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/108a183f6bdd2035e649f6812c17ddb3193ebd65/python/sglang/srt/eplb/expert_distribution.py#L740)); formatting the device tensor syncs too, so that branch would invalidate the capture the same way.
- Eager (non-captured) draft forwards also run the pass boundary, and for NextN/MTP drafts the per-layer hooks are suppressed via `disable_this_region()` ([glm4_moe_nextn.py#L105](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/108a183f6bdd2035e649f6812c17ddb3193ebd65/python/sglang/srt/models/glm4_moe_nextn.py#L105), [deepseek_nextn.py#L232](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/108a183f6bdd2035e649f6812c17ddb3193ebd65/python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_nextn.py#L232)) — so those passes record all-zero data into the balancedness history/windows. Pre-existing data-quality quirk; possibly worth gating `with_forward_pass` on `is_draft_worker` as a follow-up.

### Reproduction

Any MoE model with an MTP/EAGLE draft should reproduce. Observed with GLM-5.2 (NVFP4) on 8×B200:

```
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model <GLM-5.2 NVFP4 checkpoint> --tp 8 \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
  --enable-expert-distribution-metrics --expert-distribution-recorder-mode stat
```

Crash-loops in "Capturing batches (...)" during startup. Dropping `--enable-expert-distribution-metrics` or setting `--speculative-num-steps 1` avoids it.

### Environment

sglang v0.5.15.post1 (cu130 build; code path identical on `main` @ `108a183f6b` by inspection), Python 3.12, 8×NVIDIA B200 (TP8), GLM-5.2 NVFP4 with the built-in MTP layer as EAGLE draft, EAGLE worker v2.

title: [RFC] Explicit, budgeted tail-replay for Mamba/GDN state in UnifiedRadixCache
body:
**Area**: `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/` (UnifiedRadixCache, MambaComponent, schedule_batch)
**Related**: HiCache buffer-mode (#37424), eviction-policy parameterization (#37795), external linker series (#37091–#37914), HiMambaRadixTree removal (#33468), Mamba checkpoint depth fix for off-page prefixes (#39115), ReplaySSM decode/spec-verify state reconstruction (#28511)

## Summary

Hybrid models (FULL + SWA + MAMBA/GDN components) reuse a prefix only up to the latest reusable Mamba state checkpoint. When that checkpoint is missing, evicted, or simply far behind the full-KV hit, the engine retreats the *entire* hit to the checkpoint boundary and re-prefills everything after it — even though only the GDN recurrent state needs rebuilding, and the full-attention KV for the gap is already cached.

We propose making the existing *implicit* tail recompute an **explicit, budgeted "tail-replay" path**: accept the full-KV hit up to `H`, seed the GDN state from the checkpoint at `C`, and replay only `(H - C)` tokens through the GDN layers, gated by a configurable budget and admission-time cost accounting.

## Motivation

1. **Checkpoint density vs. hit rate.** Mamba state is leaf-only checkpoint data (node split clears the parent's state). Checkpoints are sparse relative to full-KV pages, so on hybrid models the reusable prefix is effectively quantized to checkpoint positions. Short prompts and agentic workloads (many shared prefixes appended in small turns) are hit hardest: the nearest checkpoint often sits one full grid behind, and the hit collapses. The checkpoint-depth semantics here are live upstream surface — see #39115 (merged 2026-09-17), which fixed exactly the depth computation for prefixes ending off the radix page; our proposal composes with that fix and extends it from "place the checkpoint right" to "tolerate the checkpoint being behind".
2. **Eviction can strand the state.** Incremental persistence of a branching state is currently write-through only; write-back eviction may discard device-only state (comment in `MambaComponent.finalize_match_result_in_tree_core`). The next match then retreats to a much older checkpoint — or the root — with no policy deciding between "replay a longish tail" and "give up the hit".
3. **Two hard fences are landing soon.** `init_hicache` raises for Mamba components under `hicache-host-memory-mode=buffer_only` (TODO(Jialin) referencing #34798/#35769), and `MambaComponent.build_external_linker_transfer` asserts "will support soon". Both follow-ups will need a replay/charge semantics for the gap between a restored KV prefix and a missing state. Defining that semantics now lets the linker work build on it instead of inventing its own. (The linker-mode interface is being negotiated right now in #38652; a POC pair — #40759 and LMCache/LMCache#5304 — was posted and withdrawn by the author on 2026-09-22, so the interface is not yet locked. This RFC is timed to feed that discussion.)

## Current state (verified on main @ 224a247d5b, 2026-09-23)

- `MambaComponent.create_match_validator` (`mem_cache/unified_cache/components/mamba.py:143`; note the 10/N refactor renamed `mamba_component.py` → `mamba.py`, symbols unchanged): a node is a valid match boundary if it has a device mamba value (device-only mode) or any value (HiCache mode). Missing checkpoint ⇒ walk up to nearest checkpointed ancestor. No error path — silent retreat.
- `MambaComponent.finalize_match_result_in_tree_core` (`mamba.py:156`): computes `mamba_branching_seqlen = align_down(full_kv_hit_length, mamba_checkpoint_grid)` when the full hit extends past the mamba boundary; the retreated tail is then re-prefilled through **all** layers by the extend pass (gap KV recomputed, deduplicated at insert), and a new branching checkpoint is physically captured via `_force_track_h` (`managers/schedule_batch.py:2986`; `mamba_branching_seqlen` field at :1161).
- SWA precedent for an explicit short-tail re-prefill: `UnifiedRadixCache.swa_reprefill_tail_tokens` (`unified_radix_cache.py:3506`) caps the match by one sliding window when the SWA ring is not content-stable, with scheduler-side cap call sites at `schedule_batch.py:1595` and `:1613`. This is the pipeline we intend to mirror for Mamba.
- `init_hicache` at `unified_radix_cache.py:410`; the buffer_only Mamba fence and TODO(Jialin) at :414.
- No metrics expose how much recompute the mamba boundary retreat causes.

### Relation to ReplaySSM (#28511)

Not to be confused: ReplaySSM (`--enable-linear-replayssm` / `--enable-linear-replayssm-spec`; #28511, parts #28451/#28695) already reconstructs GDN/KDA recurrent state on the *decode* and *spec-verify* paths — from a frozen checkpoint plus a ring of recent `(d, k, g)` records, output-only, with pointer rollback for rejected drafts. It optimizes decode state-traffic bandwidth and never touches the match/finalize/admission path: a prefix-cache hit still retreats to the checkpoint. (The radix *track* does consume ReplaySSM force-flushes to materialize checkpoints — #35544 — but that is the write side.) The two share the algebraic primitive — a linear recurrence's state is reconstructable from a checkpoint plus suffix records — and compose; they do not overlap.

## Proposal

1. **`mamba_replay_tail_tokens()` on `UnifiedRadixCache`** (sibling of `swa_reprefill_tail_tokens`): returns the tail length the scheduler should treat as "hit for FULL, replay for GDN" for the current match, instead of collapsing the whole hit to the checkpoint boundary.
2. **Budget policy**: accept the extended hit iff `(H - C) <= mamba_replay_budget`, where the budget is `max(min_tail, replay_ratio * prefix_len)`; defaults chosen so current behavior is unchanged unless the policy is enabled (`SGLANG_MAMBA_REPLAY_TAIL_RATIO`, default off or a conservative value — open to maintainer preference).
3. **Admission-time charge**: the replayed tail consumes prefill compute; charge it against `req.mamba_host_hit_length`-style accounting so the scheduler's token budget reflects the real cost (this is also the hook the buffer_only and linker follow-ups will need).
4. **Metrics**: `mamba_replay_tokens_total`, histogram of `(H - C)` at admission, and a counter of "hit collapsed to checkpoint" events so operators can tune the budget.
5. **Out of scope** (coordination, not overlap): buffer_only state handoff and external-linker transfer for Mamba — owned by the TODO(Jialin) follow-up and the linker series (#37914+, and the #38652 LMCache discussion). This RFC only defines the replay/charge semantics they should consume.
6. **Execution-path note (the real engineering delta)**: today the extend pass re-prefills the retreated tail through *all* layers (gap KV recomputed, deduplicated at insert). The proposed win therefore needs a split-prefix extend — full-attention layers start at `H` (their KV is already cached) while the GDN layers consume `[C, seq_end)` seeded from the checkpoint at `C`. The forward path currently carries a single `extend_prefix_len` per request (`hybrid_linear_attn_backend` consumes `extend_prefix_lens` uniformly), so this needs forward-batch/backend plumbing on top of the cache-layer hooks above; no new kernels are required (the existing FLA chunked prefill runs the replay tokens), but the metadata layer must represent both prefix lengths. Once a ReplaySSM ring covers the gap, its reconstruction primitive (#28511) is a candidate accelerator for the replay segment; we scope plain chunked prefill as the baseline. Happy to split the execution path into a follow-up PR if maintainers prefer to land the policy/charge/metrics layer first.

## Cost-model evidence (offline measurements, our Draft-OPD/Tail-Replay setup)

On Qwen3-class GDN hybrids, replaying the trailing 5–10% of a prefix reconstructs the GDN recurrent state with 93–99.9% fidelity (measured against full prefill states), while a full re-prefill of the gap costs the entire gap's attention compute. The replay path turns "checkpoint miss ⇒ full gap re-prefill" into "checkpoint miss ⇒ GDN-only tail replay", which is strictly cheaper whenever the full KV is cached. We will publish the measurement harness and curves in the RFC thread.

## Testing plan

- Unit: synthetic unified trees with FULL+MAMBA components; assert match/finalize behavior for (a) checkpoint present, (b) checkpoint missing within budget, (c) missing beyond budget (hit collapses), (d) budget=0 ⇒ byte-identical to current behavior.
- Integration: HiCache L2 offload on a Qwen3-Next-class hybrid; measure hit-rate recovery on an agentic multi-turn trace.
- Regression: existing `test/` unified-cache and hicache suites must pass with the policy disabled (default).

## Asks

1. Budget-policy shape: env var vs. server arg vs. per-model default in the pool configurator?
2. Should the replay charge live in the admission path (`init_next_round_input`) or in the retract/eviction accounting?
3. Any objection to landing this ahead of the Mamba linker support, given (5) explicitly defers the handoff/transfer semantics to that work — and would the #38652 linker-mode participants rather consume this as an interface input now?

title: [Bug] GLM-5.3-Flash cannot use FP8 KV cache: `index_kpool > 1` excludes `flashmla_kv`, and no CUDA DSA backend supports bf16-query x fp8-KV
body:
## Summary

On 8xH20 (SM90), `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` cannot be used with **GLM-5.3-Flash**, while it works fine
with **GLM-5.2** on the *same hardware, same cluster, same image* (in production for months).

The difference is one model-config field: **GLM-5.3-Flash sets `index_kpool: 4`; GLM-5.2 does not set it
(defaults to 1)**. That single value excludes `flashmla_kv` — the backend GLM-5.2 uses for FP8 KV — and the
three replacement backends (`fa3` / `tilelang` / `trtllm`) have no bf16-query x fp8-KV path on CUDA.

Net effect: GLM-5.3-Flash is forced onto bf16 KV and loses **~1.75x-2.0x** of KV cache capacity.

## Positive control: GLM-5.2 with FP8 KV works on the same hardware

Production node, running continuously for months:

```
--model-path <path>/GLM-5.2-W4AFP8
--quantization w4afp8
--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3
```
Engine-resolved:
```
kv_cache_dtype='fp8_e4m3'
dsa_prefill_backend='flashmla_kv'
dsa_decode_backend='flashmla_kv'
```
```
KV Cache is allocated. dtype: torch.float8_e4m3fn, #tokens: 958208
```

So FP8 KV itself is healthy on SM90. The problem is specific to GLM-5.3-Flash.

## Root cause chain

**1. The only relevant config difference**

```
GLM-5.3-Flash : "index_kpool": 4   "index_topk": 2048  "index_n_heads": 32  "index_head_dim": 128
GLM-5.2       : (absent)           "index_topk": 2048  "index_n_heads": 32  "index_head_dim": 128
```
```python
# srt/configs/model_config.py:280
def get_dsa_index_kpool(config) -> int:
    return getattr(config, "index_kpool", 1)
```

**2. The guard excludes `flashmla_kv`**

```python
# srt/layers/attention/dsa_backend.py  _check_kpool_tail_backend
if (topk_indices is None
    or self.dsa_index_kpool <= 1                      # GLM-5.2 exits here
    or dsa_impl in ("fa3", "tilelang", "trtllm")):    # GLM-5.3 is limited to these
    return
raise NotImplementedError(
    "index_kpool > 1 appends tail tokens to topk_indices and is "
    "currently only supported by the FA3/TileLang/TRTLLM DSA {phase} backend.")
```

**3. The existing escape hatch only covers the bf16 path**

```python
# _resolve_kpool_tail_backend
if (topk_indices is None or self.dsa_index_kpool <= 1
    or dsa_impl != "flashmla_sparse"):     # does not cover flashmla_kv
    return dsa_impl
if self.device_sm_major == 9: return "fa3"
```

This is why the **bf16** configuration works: the engine auto-selects `flashmla_sparse` + `fa3`, and the
resolver hands the KPool tail to `fa3`. FP8 requires `flashmla_kv`, which this branch does not handle.

**4. None of the three allowed backends can consume FP8 KV on CUDA**

```python
# dsa_backend.py:594-601 - the only mixed q/kv dtype path
if (self.dsa_prefill_impl == "aiter" or self.dsa_decode_impl == "aiter") \
   and model_runner.kv_cache_dtype == fp8_dtype:
        self._ensure_aiter_dsa_decode_metadata_buffer(
            q_dtype=torch.bfloat16, kv_dtype=fp8_dtype)
```

It exists only for `aiter` (ROCm). `flashmla_sparse_q8` is native FP8 but **prefill-only** (its own error
message: *"flashmla_sparse_q8 is a prefill-only backend. For FP8, use --dsa-prefill-backend
flashmla_sparse_q8 together with --dsa-decode-backend flashmla_kv"*) - and `flashmla_kv` is exactly what
the KPool guard rejects.

## Reproduction

8xH20, image `lmsysorg/sglang:glm-5.3-flash`, two instances of `--tp-size 4 --expert-parallel-size 4`
(GPU 0-3 and 4-7), `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, `--context-length 200000`:

| # | prefill / decode backend | MTP | Failure |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `flashmla_sparse_q8` / `flashmla_kv` | on | `NotImplementedError: index_kpool > 1 ...` (decode cuda-graph capture) |
| 2 | `flashmla_sparse_q8` / `fa3` | on | `RuntimeError: query and key must have the same dtype` (target-verify graph) |
| 3 | as #2 + `--speculative-attention-mode decode` | on | same dtype error |
| 4 | `flashmla_sparse_q8` / `fa3` | **off** | **same dtype error** |

Case #4 matters: **the failure is not specific to speculative decoding.**

The KV pool itself allocates fine - the blocker is on the consumer side:

| config | KV tokens / instance |
|---|---|
| bf16 + MTP (the only working one) | 2,280,000 |
| fp8_e4m3 + MTP | 3,993,472 (1.75x) |
| fp8_e4m3, no MTP | 4,610,560 (2.02x) |

Launch command for case #2:
```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path <path>/GLM-5.3-Flash --trust-remote-code \
  --tp-size 4 --expert-parallel-size 4 \
  --quantization fp8 --disable-shared-experts-fusion \
  --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --dsa-prefill-backend flashmla_sparse_q8 --dsa-decode-backend fa3 \
  --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
  --context-length 200000 --mem-fraction-static 0.85
```

## A config-level workaround does not exist

`--json-model-override-args '{"index_kpool":1}'` is accepted, but leaves the engine in an inconsistent
half-KPool state:

| attempt | assertion |
|---|---|
| kpool=1 + `flashmla_kv` + MTP | `AssertionError: DSA kpool target_verify requires kpool_write_plan` |
| kpool=1 + `flashmla_kv`, no MTP | `AssertionError: kpool_decode_update_index_cache called when kpool compress is disabled` |

KPool has a dedicated indexer (`srt/layers/attention/dsa/dsa_indexer_kpool.py`) reading three fields
(`index_kpool`, `index_kpool_always_select_tail`, `index_kpool_compress`); overriding one is not enough.
We deliberately did **not** override the rest: KPool changes which tokens sparse attention selects, and the
indexer weights were exported for `kpool=4`, so such a run would silently produce degraded output.

**Consequently we could not verify whether KPool is the *only* blocker for FP8 KV on this model** - that
needs a code change, not a config.

## Suggested fixes (independent)

1. **Teach `flashmla_kv` to handle the KPool tail.** GLM-5.2 already proves `flashmla_kv` + FP8 KV is sound;
   only the tail handling is missing. This looks like the smaller change.
2. **Give the fa3 DSA path a bf16-query x fp8-KV mode**, mirroring what `aiter` already does.

(Extending `_resolve_kpool_tail_backend` to also cover `flashmla_kv` is *not* a third option on its own -
the tail would land on `fa3`, which still faces fp8 KV and hits the same dtype error. It depends on #2.)

## Environment

- 8x NVIDIA H20 (SM90), CUDA, driver/runtime per `lmsysorg/sglang:glm-5.3-flash`
- sglang `0.0.0.dev1+g033446bb05` (image `lmsysorg/sglang:glm-5.3-flash`)
- Models: `ZhipuAI/GLM-5.3-Flash` (native FP8, e4m3) and GLM-5.2-W4AFP8
- Related: #36802 (same model, `--enable-dp-attention` incompatibility)
